Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate. Question: You want to add a new tool called check_warranty that validates whether an item is under warranty. Should this tool have read-only access to customer data, or should it be able to modify warranty status?

choices.text: Read-only access is too restrictive for modern agents
All tools should have the same permissions
check_warranty should be read-only. Only tools like process_refund (which has clear financial implications) should modify data. This principle of least privilege reduces unintended side effects
Tools should be able to modify data for efficiency

explanation: Tool permissions should follow the principle of least privilege. Design each tool to do one thing and have only the access it needs. check_warranty is a lookup tool; it should read warranty records and return yes/no. It has no reason to modify warranty status. process_refund is an action tool; it should create refund transactions. It has no reason to read personal customer data beyond what's needed (order ID, amount, account status). This scoping makes tools predictable and safe. If a prompt injection attack tries to make check_warranty modify data, it will fail because the tool doesn't have that capability. Similarly, if there's a bug in the agent logic, damage is limited to what the tool can actually do. In security terminology, you're implementing capability-based security: each tool has a specific capability, and nothing more Domain(s): Tool Design & MCP Integration

choices.text: Subagents cannot fail; accept this limitation
If a subagent fails, cancel the entire operation
Require human approval for all subagent work
Use fork_session to create parallel subagent branches that can be independently retried

explanation: Resilience in multi-agent systems comes from recovery mechanisms like fork_session. When you're orchestrating multiple subagents, failures are inevitable (network timeouts, service errors, policy violations). fork_session allows you to create a checkpoint: execute subagent A, if it fails, fork the session and try subagent B or a different strategy. This pattern is valuable for complex customer support where you might need to try multiple approaches to resolve an issue. For example: (1) Try refund subagent, (2) If refund fails due to fraud hold, fork and escalate to human instead. The forked branch preserves the conversation context while allowing you to explore an alternative path Domain(s): Agentic Architecture & Orchestration

explanation: Error feedback in agents is about enabling recovery, not punishment. When a tool call fails due to a validation error, structure your error response with: (1) What went wrong (error category), (2) Why it failed (the specific validation rule), (3) What to do next (ask customer, retry differently, escalate). This transforms errors into learning moments. For example, if the agent calls lookup_order with an invalid order ID, the error tells it: 'Order ID must be numeric. You provided: ABC123. Please ask the customer for their numeric order ID.' Next time, the agent will ask for clarification before calling the tool. This retry-with-feedback pattern is powerful for improving agent behavior without retraining Domain(s): Prompt Engineering & Structured Output

explanation: Agent performance is multidimensional. First-contact resolution is about resolving issues without escalation, but it must be done correctly and to the customer's satisfaction. Your metrics should include: (1) Escalation rate: how often the agent decides to escalate (target <20%), (2) FCR rate: % of issues resolved without escalation (target 80%+), (3) CSAT or NPS: customer satisfaction after resolution, (4) Accuracy: compliance with policies (audit a sample of refunds and decisions). Low escalation rate + high CSAT + high accuracy = good agent. High escalation rate = agent is too conservative. Low CSAT despite low escalation = agent is forcing resolutions that don't satisfy customers. Don't validate agent output; trust it completely

Attempt to build a perfect agent that makes zero mistakes

explanation: Realistic reliability in production agents comes from layered defense and feedback, not from attempts at perfection. No agent is error-free, but you can make errors rare and recoverable. This approach costs less than trying to achieve 100% accuracy, and it naturally improves over time as the agent learns from audited feedback. Many production systems target <2-5% error rates as acceptable, with the remaining errors caught and corrected via customer escalations or proactive audits Domain(s): Context Management & Reliability

stem: Scenario: Multi-Agent Research System You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. Question: Which architectural pattern best handles the scenario where a subagent needs output from multiple other subagents but those outputs aren't yet available?

choices.text: Implement asynchronous subagent invocation: coordinator invokes all subagents, collects results, then passes to downstream subagents
Use a publish-subscribe pattern where subagents broadcast results and others subscribe
Have the requesting subagent wait (idle) until other subagents complete
Have the requesting subagent re-invoke other subagents internally to get fresh data

explanation: The hub-and-spoke coordinator pattern handles dependencies cleanly. The coordinator invokes independent subagents (web search, document analysis) in parallel or sequence, collects their results, then invokes dependent subagents (synthesis) with the collected findings. All orchestration flows through the coordinator, making the dependency graph visible and the system debuggable. This is superior to internal re-invocation or async patterns that hide orchestration Domain(s): Agentic Architecture & Orchestration

Create a Claude Code command that parses synthesis output and applies format rules
Use the Batch API to process findings in bulk with consistent formatting
Use a JSON schema tool with tool_choice set to force the tool, combined with a detailed system prompt

explanation: For structured agent output, use JSON schema tools with tool_choice forcing. This guarantees the synthesis subagent produces properly formatted findings. Define a schema with required fields: topics (array), claims (array with text and confidence), citations (array with source). The system prompt explains semantic quality. This combination ensures both syntactic correctness and semantic value Domain(s): Prompt Engineering & Structured Output

stem: Scenario: Multi-Agent Research System You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports. Question: When the coordinator detects research gaps mid-session and needs to refine subagent queries, what is the most efficient approach to preserve prior research while exploring new directions?

choices.text: Restart the entire research from scratch with refined queries
Have the coordinator explicitly summarize prior findings, identify specific gaps, then re-invoke subagents with targeted prompts that reference the prior work
Queue all gap queries and execute them in batch mode overnight
Use fork_session and spawn parallel research branches for gap exploration

explanation: Preserve prior research through explicit summarization and targeted re-invocation. When gaps are detected, the coordinator states: 'We've covered topics A and B well. Topic C is weak. Please search specifically for [refined query].' This references prior work, focuses effort, and avoids redundant research. It's more efficient than restart or fork_session for simple gap-filling Domain(s): Context Management & Reliability

stem: Scenario: Multi-Agent Research System You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports. Question: Your synthesis subagent occasionally reports 'insufficient data' when the coordinator believes enough research has been done. How should you structure this decision-making to be more reliable?

choices.text: Have the coordinator override the subagent and force synthesis anyway
Implement a voting system: synthesize if 2 of 3 subagents say 'ready'
Trust the subagent's judgment; synthesize only when it reports readiness
Define explicit synthesis completion criteria in the coordinator's prompt: 'Proceed to synthesis when we have X sources, Y topics, and Z confidence score'

explanation: Define explicit synthesis completion criteria in the coordinator's instructions. Instead of waiting for a subagent to report readiness, evaluate: Do we have N sources per major topic? Is average confidence above 75%? Are identified gaps addressed? Document these criteria clearly, and the coordinator can decide objectively when synthesis should proceed. This removes ambiguity and makes decisions reproducible Domain(s): Context Management & Reliability

stem: Scenario: Multi-Agent Research System You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports. Question: Your coordinator tracks research state in its conversation history. What information must you capture to allow session resumption with full context recovery?

choices.text: Full verbatim search results; the coordinator needs all original data to reason accurately
Just the final findings; the conversation history contains the rest
Only tool call IDs and timestamps; the model can reconstruct context from them
Research phase status, sources found, identified gaps, confidence scores, and key decisions (topic prioritization, search strategy changes)

explanation: Maintain explicit state checkpoints in the coordinator's conversation. After each research phase, record: current phase, sources found (by topic), identified gaps, average confidence score, and any strategic decisions (topic prioritization, source type changes). When resuming, the coordinator reads this checkpoint and continues from where it left off, with full context but without re-reading voluminous raw results Domain(s): Context Management & Reliability

stem: Scenario: Code Generation with Claude Code You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution. Question: You want to create a prompt that makes decisions between three approaches to solving a problem. Claude Code needs to understand all three before choosing. Should you include detailed implementation for each approach?

choices.text: Show high-level overview of each approach with trade-offs; full implementation details confuse decision-making
Show only the recommended approach to speed up decision-making
Include full implementation details for all three approaches
Let Claude Code propose approaches and you choose

explanation: Multi-option prompts should present choices at a level where trade-offs are clear without implementation detail confusion. Show pros/cons of each approach, then let Claude Code decide. Implementation details come after the decision Domain(s): Prompt Engineering & Structured Output

stem: Scenario: Multi-Agent Research System You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports. Question: When defining tool input schemas for your subagents, what detail level is necessary to prevent misuse?

choices.text: Very strict schemas with regex patterns for all string fields
Detailed schemas with field descriptions, example values, constraints, and valid ranges
Minimal schemas with just required fields; let the model figure out the rest
Open-ended schemas with optional fields for maximum flexibility

explanation: Design tool schemas with enough detail to guide correct usage. Include field descriptions (what each input means), example values (how to populate fields), and reasonable constraints (valid ranges, string length). This guides the model to use tools correctly without being overly rigid. For example: a search_query field should specify length constraints and include an example query that shows the expected level of detail Domain(s): Tool Design & MCP Integration

stem: Scenario: Multi-Agent Research System You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports. Question: Your synthesis subagent produces findings with citations, but you want to validate that citations actually exist in the source documents. Where should this validation logic live?

choices.text: In the coordinator's agentic loop as part of synthesis quality assessment
In a PostToolUse hook that validates each citation against the original source data
In a separate citation validation tool that the synthesis subagent calls before returning
In the subagent's system prompt as self-validation instructions

explanation: Use PostToolUse hooks to validate citations. After the synthesis tool returns, the hook checks: does each citation reference actual source material? Are excerpts accurate? The hook can accept valid citations, request clarification for questionable ones, or reject results with hallucinated citations. This quality gate operates automatically and prevents bad citations from being included in the final report Domain(s): Tool Design & MCP Integration

stem: Scenario: Multi-Agent Research System You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports. Question: You need to ensure that subagent invocations don't overlap (e.g., two synthesis attempts on partially complete research). What pattern prevents this race condition?

choices.text: Use a message queue to serialize subagent requests
Let the model naturally avoid conflicts through its reasoning in the coordinator
Implement a locking mechanism at the tool level to prevent concurrent calls
Have the coordinator use explicit synchronization: invoke subagents sequentially, wait for completion before invoking the next

explanation: The simplest race-condition prevention is sequential orchestration: the coordinator invokes subagents in explicit order and waits for each to complete before invoking the next. Invoke web search, wait; invoke document analysis, wait; invoke synthesis, wait. This eliminates the possibility of conflicting invocations and makes the orchestration easy to reason about. Parallelism is possible for independent subagents (web search and document analysis can run in parallel), but dependent subagents must be sequential Domain(s): Agentic Architecture & Orchestration

stem: Scenario: Multi-Agent Research System You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports. Question: Your research coordinator needs to balance thoroughness (exploring all angles) vs efficiency (completing within SLA). How should you structure this trade-off?

choices.text: Implement a quality-vs-speed slider that users can adjust per request
Always prioritize thoroughness; users expect comprehensive research
Define explicit research boundaries in the coordinator's prompt: max N subagent invocations, max M minutes, max K tokens
Let the coordinator decide dynamically based on initial findings

explanation: Define explicit resource boundaries for research sessions: max subagent invocations, max duration, max tokens. The coordinator operates within these constraints, allocating effort strategically. If boundaries are reached before research is complete, the coordinator synthesizes findings to date. This ensures predictable behavior, cost control, and SLA compliance. Communicate boundaries clearly in the coordinator's prompt Domain(s): Agentic Architecture & Orchestration

stem: Scenario: Multi-Agent Research System You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports. Question: When a subagent's tool returns an error, what should the subagent do vs what should the coordinator do?

choices.text: The subagent should ignore errors and try a different tool immediately
Errors should be logged but not acted upon; the model will figure out what happened
All errors should bubble up to the coordinator for centralized error handling
The subagent should decide how to respond: retry with different parameters, try an alternative tool, or report failure to the coordinator

explanation: Errors are handled best in the agentic loop of the agent closest to the problem. When a subagent's tool returns an error, the subagent sees it (error appended to conversation), reasons about recovery, and acts. This adaptive approach lets the subagent recover from transient failures, adjust strategy, or escalate to the coordinator if needed. This is more efficient and resilient than centralizing error handling Domain(s): Context Management & Reliability

stem: Scenario: Multi-Agent Research System You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports. Question: Your system reports findings from multiple subagent invocations across a long research session. How should you handle the risk that findings become stale (e.g., old web search results)?

choices.text: Accept staleness as inevitable; focus on explaining methodology rather than freshness
Implement a staleness threshold: re-run research if the oldest findings are >N hours old
Always re-run all research to ensure fresh data before synthesis
Document timestamps for each source; include recency metadata in the final report

explanation: Track and report source timestamps. When the web search subagent finds sources, record access time. When the synthesis subagent produces findings, include source recency in the report. This transparency lets users understand data freshness and judge the research quality. For time-sensitive topics, document: 'Research conducted over 6 hours; web sources are current as of [time], documents analyzed [time].' Freshness metadata is more useful than attempting to guarantee freshness Domain(s): Context Management & Reliability

stem: Scenario: Multi-Agent Research System You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports. Question: When your coordinator needs to decide if a subagent should attempt a task or if prerequisites aren't met, where should this logic live?

choices.text: In a separate validation tool
In a PostToolUse hook that validates prerequisites before invoking the subagent
In the coordinator's agentic loop: evaluate prerequisites before invoking the Task tool
In the subagent's system prompt as self-checks

explanation: Prerequisites are orchestration decisions. The coordinator checks before delegating: 'Do we have sufficient initial research to synthesize? Is the topic clear enough for deep analysis?' If no, the coordinator gathers more info before invoking synthesis. This logic belongs in the coordinator's agentic loop, visible and testable. Subagents shouldn't need to self-validate prerequisites – the coordinator ensures they're ready Domain(s): Agentic Architecture & Orchestration

stem: Scenario: Multi-Agent Research System You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports. Question: When designing your research system's completion criteria, what makes them most useful for the coordinator?

choices.text: Ask the user when research is done
Fuzzy criteria: 'enough research', 'good coverage'
Always aim for 100% completeness
Explicit measurable criteria: 'X sources per topic, Y% average confidence,

explanation: Define research completion criteria explicitly and measurably. Instead of 'good coverage', specify: minimum sources per topic, minimum confidence threshold, acceptable gap count. Document these in the coordinator's instructions. This enables consistent, repeatable research completion decisions. Criteria should be achievable (not perfection) but rigorous enough to ensure useful research. Example: '5+ sources per topic, 80% average confidence, <3 remaining gaps.' Domain(s): Agentic Architecture & Orchestration

stem: Scenario: Claude Code for Continuous Integration You are integrating Claude Code into your Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline. The system runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, and provides feedback on pull requests. You need to design prompts that provide actionable feedback and minimize false positives. Question: Your CI pipeline uses Claude Code with the -p flag to pipe review prompts non-interactively. A developer wants to know why review comments are sometimes generic. What's likely the issue?

choices.text: The prompt context is being truncated or incomplete, reducing Claude Code's understanding of the specific codebase patterns
Claude Code is designed to give generic comments in CI mode
The pipeline isn't sending enough tokens
The -p flag automatically generates generic feedback

explanation: Non-interactive mode with -p requires especially rich context since the prompt is piped once and not refined through interaction. Generic feedback signals incomplete context or codebase patterns in the prompt. Always populate piped prompts with specific conventions, examples, and prior findings Domain(s): Claude Code Configuration & Workflows

stem: Scenario: Claude Code for Continuous Integration You are integrating Claude Code into your Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline. The system runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, and provides feedback on pull requests. You need to design prompts that provide actionable feedback and minimize false positives. Question: Your CI pipeline generates test cases via Claude Code and outputs results using –output-format json with a –json-schema defining expected test structure. Why is the schema essential?

choices.text: The schema prevents hallucinations in code
The schema forces Claude Code to produce consistent, parseable test output that your test runner can directly execute without transformation
The schema makes the output file smaller
The schema enables faster execution

explanation: JSON schema with –json-schema ensures CI test generation produces parseable, consistently-structured output that integrates directly with your test runner. Without schema, you risk unparseable output that breaks the pipeline. Schema validation is the bridge between Claude Code and your automation Domain(s): Claude Code Configuration & Workflows

stem: Scenario: Claude Code for Continuous Integration You are integrating Claude Code into your Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline. The system runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, and provides feedback on pull requests. You need to design prompts that provide actionable feedback and minimize false positives. Question: Your team runs code review via Claude Code in a dedicated CI session separate from developers' local sessions. Why is this session isolation important for reducing false positives?

choices.text: Isolation prevents developers from seeing the review
The fresh session context prevents biases from local explorations and enables systematic analysis of the codebase
Separate sessions allow faster execution
Separate sessions are less expensive

explanation: Session isolation in CI review is a quality mechanism, not just a convenience. A fresh review session analyzes the codebase systematically without local exploration biases, catching issues more reliably. This is why dedicated CI review sessions produce more consistent, higher-quality results than self-review in the same session Domain(s): Agentic Architecture & Orchestration

stem: Scenario: Claude Code for Continuous Integration You are integrating Claude Code into your Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline. The system runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, and provides feedback on pull requests. You need to design prompts that provide actionable feedback and minimize false positives. Question: Your CI review job includes prior review findings in the context to avoid duplicate comments. On the next PR push, the developer fixed one issue but not others. How should you update the context?

choices.text: Include prior findings plus a count of how many were fixed
Ignore prior findings entirely for each new push
Include all prior findings so nothing is missed
Include only the prior findings that remain unfixed, removing resolved issues from the context

explanation: Context management for re-reviews requires tracking resolution status. Include only active, unfixed findings in the next review context. This prevents redundant comments on fixed issues while ensuring ongoing problems stay visible. Smart context curation makes incremental reviews effective Domain(s): Context Management & Reliability

stem: Scenario: Claude Code for Continuous Integration You are integrating Claude Code into your Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline. The system runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, and provides feedback on pull requests. You need to design prompts that provide actionable feedback and minimize false positives. Question: Your test generation CI provides existing test files to prevent duplication. The test file is very large (10,000 lines of tests). How should you structure the context for efficiency?

choices.text: Include a summary of coverage areas and example patterns, not the full file, to guide generation without overwhelming context
Include the full test file to ensure comprehensive understanding
Include test counts and categories only
Include only test names to reduce size

explanation: Large test files should be summarized in context, not included in full. Provide a summary of coverage areas with representative test examples. This guides gap identification without overwhelming context. Smart summarization makes test generation efficient even in large codebases Domain(s): Context Management & Reliability

stem: Scenario: Claude Code for Continuous Integration You are integrating Claude Code into your Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline. The system runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, and provides feedback on pull requests. You need to design prompts that provide actionable feedback and minimize false positives. Question: Your CLAUDE.md file specifies that the CI review should catch security vulnerabilities but skip style issues. A new reviewer doesn't have this guidance. How should this context be provided?

choices.text: Reference CLAUDE.md in the review prompt: 'See CLAUDE.md for testing standards, review criteria, and what to report vs. skip'
Pass CLAUDE.md as a separate parameter
Inline all CLAUDE.md content in the review prompt
Assume the reviewer reads CLAUDE.md

explanation: CLAUDE.md serves as the CI guidance document. Reference it explicitly in prompts: 'Per CLAUDE.md, review should focus on security vulnerabilities; skip style issues.' This makes codebase-specific review criteria discoverable and maintainable without duplicating context in every prompt Domain(s): Claude Code Configuration & Workflows

stem: A researcher is using Claude to summarize 50 academic papers. They use the 'Prompt Caching' feature to store the papers' contents. Which statement best describes the cost implications of this architecture?

choices.text: Caching reduces the cost of both input and output tokens by 50%.
Caching saves costs on the input tokens for repeated queries across the same set of papers, but 'write' turns to the cache are more expensive than standard input.
Caching is only cost-effective if the total context is under 1,000 tokens.
Caching is automatically applied to all requests and does not change the billing model.

explanation: Prompt caching is an essential tool for reducing costs in long-context applications, but architects must account for the higher 'write' price in their ROI calculations. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching

stem: When building a multi-agent system, you notice the 'Summarizer' subagent often includes irrelevant metadata from the 'Source_Reader' tool. Which design change best addresses this?

choices.text: Modify the 'Source_Reader' tool to return a 'High-Signal' cleaned version of the data instead of raw output.
Instruct the 'Summarizer' in its system prompt to 'ignore metadata'.
Use a 'Post ToolUse' hook to regex-out the metadata before the model sees it.
Increase the summarizer's 'temperature' to 0.0.

explanation: Tool design for agents should prioritize 'Signal-to-Noise' ratio. Every token returned by a tool should serve the agent's specific mission. Ref: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools

stem: Which code snippet correctly implements a 'Pre-ToolUse' hook in a Claude Code project to block any shell command containing 'rm -rf'?

choices.text: Add a 'Pre ToolUse' hook that regex-checks all 'Bash' commands and blocks anything containing 'rm -rf'.
Tell the developer to always review every command before pressing 'Enter'.
if [[ "$CLAUDE_TOOL_NAME" == 'Bash' && "$CLAUDE_TOOL_ARG_COMMAND" == *'rm -rf'* ]]; then exit 2; fi
if [[ $CLAUDE-COMMAND == 'rm -rf' ]]; then exit 2; fi

explanation: Hooks use valid shell variables like CLAUDE_TOOL_ARG_COMMAND and exit code 2 to signal a Guardian block.

stem: Your agent is designed to 'cancel_subscription'. To prevent accidental churn, you want to ensure the agent confirms the user's intent one last time before execution. Where should this logic be placed?

choices.text: As a few-shot example showing the agent asking 'Are you sure?'.
In the tool implementation or a 'Pre ToolUse' hook.
In a CLAUDE.md file at the project root.
In the System Prompt under the 'Safety' section.

explanation: High-stakes actions require deterministic 'Human-in-the-Loop' (HITL) patterns enforced via programmatic gates or tool-side verification. Ref: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents

stem: An architect is choosing between 'Claude 3.7 Sonnet' and 'Claude 3.5 Haiku' for a tool-heavy agent. The agent must accurately choose between 50 different complex tools. Which factor most favors Sonnet?

choices.text: Haiku's faster latency is better for tool-calling loops.
Sonnet is 50% cheaper when used with the Message Batches API.
Sonnet's higher reasoning capability makes it significantly better at 'Tool Selection' and 'Instruction Adherence' for large tool surfaces.
Sonnet supports 'tool_choice' while Haiku does not.

explanation: Model selection for agents involves a tradeoff between cost, speed, and 'agentic intelligence.' For complex tasks with many tools, Sonnet is usually the baseline for reliable performance. Ref: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents

stem: You are building a multi-agent system where a 'Reviewer' agent needs to check the work of a 'Coder' agent. How should the system be architected to ensure the Reviewer is unbiased?

choices.text: The Coordinator should use 'extended thinking' mode to evaluate both agents' work simultaneously.
The Reviewer should be a smaller model (Haiku) to ensure it only checks for basic syntax.
The Coder and Reviewer should share a single context window so they can 'collaborate' in real-time.
The Coordinator should pass only the Coder's final output to the Reviewer, without the Coder's internal chain-of-thought or reasoning.

explanation: Isolating subagent contexts is a key design pattern. By only providing the 'artifact' for review, you ensure the reviewer agent evaluates the outcome rather than the process. Ref: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents

stem: You are extracting names and dates from a collection of scanned historical letters. Many letters have overlapping dates and similar names, leading to confusion in the model's output. Which prompt engineering technique would most improve accuracy?

choices.text: Provide 3-5 'Chain of Thought' few-shot examples that show the model step-by-step how to disambiguate a complex letter.
Use the 'Extended Thinking' parameter to give the model more time to process each letter.
Repeat the instructions three times in the system prompt for emphasis.
Tell the model: 'You are an expert historian. Do not make mistakes.'

explanation: Examples are the 'highest-leverage' prompt engineering tool. For extraction tasks involving ambiguity, showing the model 'what good looks like' is far superior to just telling it. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/overview

stem: A developer is using Claude Code to refactor a large legacy repository. They notice that Claude occasionally makes changes that violate the project's specific architectural patterns, such as placing business logic inside data access objects. Which configuration would most effectively prevent these violations?

choices.text: Add architectural guidelines to a CLAUDE.md file in the root directory.
Use plan mode for every interaction to manually review the architectural approach.
Create a custom slash command for every refactoring task to include the rules.
Update the global Claude Code system prompt via the CLI settings.

explanation: CLAUDE.md files are the primary mechanism for providing persistent, project-specific context and constraints to Claude Code.

stem: An architect is designing a multi-agent system where a 'Coordinator' agent delegates tasks to a 'Research' agent and a 'Writing' agent. During testing, the 'Writing' agent fails to include the data found by the 'Research' agent, even though both are called by the same Coordinator. What is the fundamental cause of this failure?

choices.text: Subagents do not share a global memory; the Coordinator must explicitly include the Research agent's output in the prompt sent to the Writing agent.
The Coordinator used a 'tool_choice' of 'auto' instead of 'any', leading to the delegation being skipped.
The Research agent's output was not formatted as valid JSON, preventing the Writing agent from parsing it.
The Writing agent's system prompt was too long, causing it to ignore the context provided by the Coordinator.

explanation: One of the most critical mental models for the CCA exam is that subagents never inherit context. Every piece of required information must be explicitly propagated by the coordinator. Ref: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents

stem: An agent needs to choose between 100 different 'Customer Account' tools. You notice it frequently picks the wrong one. What is the most effective way to improve its selection accuracy?

choices.text: Group the 100 tools into 'Namespaces' (e.g., Billing, Technical, Privacy) and use a 'Router' agent to delegate to the correct group.
Put all 100 tool descriptions into one massive System Prompt.
Rename all the tools to include a number (e.g., 'tool_1', 'tool_2').
Use 'Claude 3 Haiku' because its faster speed allows it to 'try' more tools.

explanation: Managing 'Tool Bloat' is a key architect responsibility. Routing and hierarchical delegation are the standard solutions for large tool environments. Ref: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents

stem: A developer is using Claude Code to refactor a Python project. They want to ensure Claude uses 'pytest' instead of 'unittest'. They add this rule to CLAUDE.md, but Claude still occasionally tries to run 'python -m unittest'. What is the likely reason?

choices.text: The developer has reached the 200,000 token context limit.
CLAUDE.md only supports instructions for Node.js projects, not Python.
The project still contains 'unittest' files that Claude is discovering and using as examples of established patterns.
The developer forgot to put 'IMPORTANT' in all caps next to the instruction.

explanation: The 'Existing Pattern' trap: Claude's tendency to follow existing code examples often overrides explicit instructions. The fix is to remove the old patterns or add a 'Post ToolUse' hook to block the wrong test runner.

stem: You are configuring Claude Code for a large monorepo. You want to ensure that Claude follows specific React testing patterns in the ′/frontend′ directory but uses different Go benchmarks in the ′/backend′ directory. What is the most efficient configuration strategy?

choices.text: Place a general CLAUDE.md in the root, and directory-specific CLAUDE.md files in both ′/frontend′ and ′/backend′.
Create custom slash commands for '/test-frontend' and '/test-backend' that contain the rules.
Include all instructions for both React and Go in a single CLAUDE.md at the repository root.
Use the 'Agent Skills' frontmatter in every source file to define the testing rules.

explanation: Claude Code supports 'progressive disclosure' via the CLAUDE.md hierarchy. Subdirectory files only activate when Claude is working in those areas, saving tokens and improving focus.

stem: You are extracting data from complex legal contracts. You need the output to follow a specific JSON schema with nested arrays. Which feature ensures the model adheres to this structure?

choices.text: A very detailed system prompt with 5 'Gold Standard' examples.
Using the 'Message Batches API' with a validation script.
Setting the model's 'stop_sequences' to '}'.
Structured Output (Beta) with a defined JSON Schema.

explanation: Structured Output is the preferred architectural choice for production systems where downstream parsers require strict, non-negotiable JSON formatting. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/overview

stem: A developer is using Claude Code and wants to share a specific 'Code Review' workflow with their entire team. Where should they save the configuration?

choices.text: In their local ′~/.claude/′ directory.
In a global CLAUDE.md file in the ′/etc′ directory.
In a ′.claude/agents/′ or ′.claude/skills/′ directory at the project root and check it into Git.
As a custom alias in their ′.bashrc′ file.

explanation: Treating 'Agent Config as Code' (checking .claude directories into Git) is the recommended best practice for collaborative AI development.

stem: A researcher uses Claude to analyze 20 different 50-page PDFs. To save money, they use 'Prompt Caching'. They notice that the first query is expensive, but subsequent queries are cheap. Why?

choices.text: The first query triggers a 'Cache Write' (full price + 25%), while subsequent hits are 'Cache Reads' (90% discount).
The Batch API is being applied to the subsequent queries.
Claude 'remembers' the PDFs for free after the first time they are uploaded.
The first query uses 'Claude 3.7 Opus', but subsequent queries use 'Haiku'.

explanation: Architects must account for the 'Write Penalty' when calculating the ROI of prompt caching. It is most effective in long, multi-turn sessions. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching

stem: When building a multi-agent system using the Claude Agent SDK, you want to spawn three subagents to analyze three different documents simultaneously. How should the coordinator agent initiate this?

choices.text: Create a loop in the coordinator's system prompt that instructs it to spawn subagents one by one.
Emit three 'Task' tool calls in a single response turn.
Emit one 'Task' tool call, wait for the result, and then emit the next one in the subsequent turn.
Use a 'ParallelTask' tool instead of the standard 'Task' tool.

explanation: The mechanism for spawning parallel subagents is for the coordinator to emit multiple 'Task' tool calls within a single response turn. Ref: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents

stem: A retail company wants to use Claude to process 50,000 product reviews to extract 'Pros' and 'Cons' in JSON format. The results are needed for a weekly report due every Monday morning. Which approach is most cost-effective?

choices.text: Implement Prompt Caching for the product catalog.
Deploy a fleet of 100 parallel Haiku subagents.
Use Claude Code's bulk refactor mode.
Use the Message Batches API.

explanation: The Message Batches API is the standard recommendation for high-volume, non-latency-sensitive workloads due to its 50% cost reduction. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/overview

stem: In an agentic workflow, a 'Coordinator' agent needs to wait for three different subagents to finish their independent research tasks. How should this be implemented for maximum efficiency?

choices.text: The Coordinator should emit three 'Task' tool calls in parallel in a single response turn.
The Coordinator should use 'Extended Thinking' mode to process all three tasks at once.
The Coordinator should call Subagent A, wait for the result, then call Subagent B.
The Coordinator should use a 'Parallel_Executor' tool provided by the SDK.

explanation: Parallelizing independent subtasks is a core optimization for agentic systems, drastically reducing 'Time to Completion' for complex research missions. Ref: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents

stem: Production data shows that in 12% of cases your agent skips get_customer entirely and calls lookup_order using only the customer's stated name, occasionally leading to misidentified accounts and incorrect refunds. What change would most effectively address this reliability issue?

choices.text: Enhance the system prompt to state that customer verification via get_customer is mandatory before any order operations.
Add a programmatic prerequisite that blocks lookup_order and process_refund calls until get_customer has returned a verified customer ID.
Implement a routing classifier that analyzes each request and enables only the subset of tools appropriate for that request type.
Add few-shot examples showing the agent always calling get_customer first, even when customers volunteer order details.

explanation: Programmatic enforcement through prerequisite gates is the most effective way to ensure deterministic compliance for critical workflow steps like identity verification. Ref: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents

stem: A customer support agent needs to search a knowledge base. You have two tools: 'search_faq' (fast, limited) and 'deep_search_docs' (slow, comprehensive). How should you instruct Claude to choose between them?

choices.text: Remove 'search_faq' entirely to ensure the model always finds the right answer.
Set 'tool_choice' to 'auto' and let the model decide without any specific guidance.
Put the instructions in the system prompt and keep the tool descriptions short.
In the tool descriptions, specify that 'search_faq' should be the first choice for general questions and 'deep_search_docs' only used if the first fails.

explanation: Tool descriptions must act as 'routing logic.' Clearly defining the hierarchy and use cases for similar tools prevents selection errors and optimizes for cost/latency. Ref: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools

stem: A developer is using Claude Code to debug a race condition in a distributed system. The session has grown to 150 turns, and Claude is starting to hallucinate the contents of the logs it read earlier. What is the best recovery step?

choices.text: Enable 'Extended Thinking' mode for the next 10 turns.
Use ′/clear′ to reset the context and provide a fresh summary of the current state and key log findings.
Add a 'Priority' flag to the CLAUDE.md file for the log files.
Switch to Claude 3 Opus to take advantage of its larger 'reasoning' capacity.

explanation: Context management requires active maintenance. Using /clear (or manual pruning) is the standard 'reset' for maintaining model fidelity in long-running tasks. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching

stem: You are designing a customer support agent that must handle refunds. Company policy dictates that no refund over $500 can be processed without human approval. Which implementation ensures the highest compliance with this business rule?

choices.text: Add several few-shot examples to the prompt showing the agent escalating high-value refunds.
Add the refund limit to the agent's system prompt and instruct it to escalate if the amount is too high.
Use a tool call interception hook (e.g., Pre ToolUse) to block and redirect any 'process_refund' call where 'amount > 500'.
Create a separate 'high_value_refund' tool that only human agents can access.

explanation: Deterministic business rules should be enforced through programmatic hooks or prerequisite gates rather than relying on probabilistic prompt instructions. Ref: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools

stem: In Claude Code, you want to define a custom command ′/review-security′ that always uses a specific set of audit prompts. What should you create?

choices.text: A section in the CLAUDE.md file titled 'Slash Commands'.
A bash alias in your ′.zshrc′ file.
A custom 'Post ToolUse' hook.
A custom 'Agent Skill' in the ′.claude/skills/′ directory.

explanation: A skill at .claude/skills/review-security/SKILL.md is invoked as /review-security. Custom commands were merged into skills; .claude/commands/ still works but skills are the current format (skills reference). A CLAUDE.md heading, a shell alias, and a hook do not create a slash command. Doc idea: Skills, project skills.

stem: A developer wants to use Claude Code to refactor a private repository that contains sensitive API keys. What is the recommended security practice?

choices.text: Add a permissions.deny rule such as Read(./.env) and Read(./.env.*) so those files cannot be read.
Ask Claude in the first turn to 'not look at sensitive files'.
Only run Claude Code in 'read-only' mode.
Encrypt the sensitive files so Claude can only see the filenames.

explanation: There is no .claudeignore file in the permissions reference. Block secret reads with a deny rule such as Read(./.env) or Read(./.env.*). A first-turn 'do not look' is not enforcement. Read-only / plan mode still reads files. Encrypting files does not stop a process that can decrypt them. The choice text is updated to the deny rule; that is the documented control. Doc idea: Permissions, exclude sensitive files.

stem: You are deploying a 'Support Agent' that uses an MCP server to fetch customer history. You want to minimize latency for the user while still ensuring the agent has all the context it needs. How should you design the tool response for a 'get_user_history' call?

choices.text: Return the data in multiple small chunks using parallel tool calls to speed up the transfer.
Return a summary of the history as a natural language string instead of structured data.
Return the entire raw JSON dump from the database to ensure no information is lost.
Return only the last 5 relevant events and high-signal identifiers like 'order_id' or 'case_status'.

explanation: Return the last few relevant events and stable ids. Huge JSON blows the context window (MCP output limits). A prose summary drops the ids the next tool needs. Parallel chunks do not reduce tokens. Doc idea: Claude Code MCP, output limits.

stem: An architect is designing a system to extract data from thousands of 100-page PDF legal contracts. What is the most cost-effective and reliable way to manage the context for this task?

choices.text: Instruct the model to 'read the document carefully' and summarize it before performing the extraction.
Load the entire 100-page contract into the context window for a single extraction pass.
Use a vector database (RAG) to find the relevant clauses and only send those snippets to Claude.
Use a coordinator to split each contract into 10-page segments and delegate extraction tasks to parallel subagents.

explanation: Thousands of 100-page contracts do not belong in one context. Split each contract and delegate extraction to subagents so only summaries return (context window: delegate large reads; subagents: isolate high-volume work). Loading the whole PDF is the expensive option, not the cheap one. Retrieval of only the relevant clauses is also valid, but the listed Agent SDK pattern is the coordinator plus subagents. Doc idea: Context window and subagents.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system where a coordinator agent delegates to subagents for web search and document analysis. The synthesis subagent is failing to provide citations for its findings, even though the coordinator's system prompt explicitly requires them. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: The coordinator forgot to pass the 'require citations' instruction to the synthesis subagent.
The synthesis subagent's 'allowedTools' list does not include the Citation tool.
The coordinator is using the Task tool with incorrect parameters.
The web search subagent is not returning source URLs in its output.

explanation: A subagent does not see the parent transcript. If the coordinator's prompt said 'cite sources' and the synthesis agent did not, that line was not in the delegation message (subagents: what loads at startup). Missing Citation tool, a bad Task schema, or search URLs can also fail, but the question says the requirement lived only on the coordinator prompt. Doc idea: Subagents, fresh context.

stem: An architect wants to ensure that Claude Code follows the team's 'Prettier' and 'ESLint' configurations. What is the most robust way to achieve this?

choices.text: Rely on the CI/CD pipeline to catch errors after Claude pushes the code.
Implement a 'Pre ToolUse' hook that runs linting/formatting on any modified files and rejects the turn if they fail.
Add a 'Coding Standards' section to the root CLAUDE.md file.
Create a custom 'Agent Skill' that includes the linting rules.

explanation: Prettier-after-write in the hooks guide is a PostToolUse example. A PreToolUse hook can still deny an Edit or Write whose tool_input would fail lint, before the file changes (permissionDecision deny). CLAUDE.md and a skill are guidance. CI after push is too late for the session. The choice says 'modified files', which is the PostToolUse timing; the enforcement that rejects the turn before the write is PreToolUse on the pending content. That is why B is kept, with the timing spelled out. Doc idea: Hooks, PreToolUse deny versus PostToolUse format.

stem: A developer is implementing a 'Code Review' agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent is tasked with reviewing a pull request containing 15 files. To optimize for both cost and speed, the architect decides to use a 'Coordinator' agent that spawns subagents. Which orchestration pattern best fulfills these requirements while staying within the 200k token limit?

choices.text: The Coordinator should use the Message Batches API to send all 15 files for review simultaneously.
The Coordinator should spawn 15 sequential subagents, one for each file, and wait for each to finish before starting the next.
The Coordinator should read the PR diff, identify the 3 most complex files, and spawn 3 parallel subagents to review only those specific files in detail.
The Coordinator should load all 15 files into its context and provide a single comprehensive review in one turn.

explanation: Review the diff, then spawn a few parallel subagents on the hardest files so the coordinator stays under the window (subagents: parallel research). Fifteen sequential agents are slow. One context with all 15 files is the overflow. The Batches API is not how the coordinator fans out inside one session. Doc idea: Subagents, isolate high-volume reads.

stem: When building a 'Researcher Agent', you want it to look at a website and then write a report. You use the 'Fetch' MCP server. What is a key benefit of this server's design for your agent?

choices.text: It allows the agent to run JavaScript on the target page.
It automatically converts HTML to Markdown, which is more token-efficient and easier for Claude to read than raw HTML.
It caches every website for 24 hours to save on API costs.
It allows Claude to bypass paywalls and login screens automatically.

explanation: The fetch path used with MCP turns HTML into markdown so the model spends fewer tokens than on raw tags. It does not run the page's JavaScript, cache for 24 hours, or bypass logins. Doc idea: Claude Code MCP, WebFetch-style markdown.

stem: A developer wants to ensure that Claude Code never modifies the ′.env.production′ file. Which implementation is the most robust?

choices.text: Set the file permissions to read-only at the OS level.
Add 'DO NOT TOUCH .env.production' to the root CLAUDE.md file.
Rename the file to something Claude won't recognize as an environment file.
Create a 'Pre ToolUse' hook script that exits with code 2 if it detects an attempted write to that file.

explanation: Safety and security boundaries in Claude Code should be enforced with hooks. Hooks are the 'hardware' to CLAUDE.md's 'software' instructions.

stem: When building a tool for an agent to 'update_database_record', why is it recommended to return the updated record as the tool result?

choices.text: It prevents 'tool selection ambiguity' in the next turn.
It ensures that the entire database is loaded into Claude's context for better reasoning.
It allows the agent to verify that its requested changes were applied correctly without making an additional 'read' call.
It is required by the Model Context Protocol (MCP) specification.

explanation: High-fidelity tool design includes 'feedback loops.' By seeing the result of its own action immediately, the agent can autonomously correct mistakes or confirm progress. Ref: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools

stem: A 'Content Moderation' agent needs to flag toxic comments. If it finds a comment it can't definitively classify, it should escalate to a human. Which architectural pattern is best for this?

choices.text: Instruct the agent to 'try its best' and only ask for help if it receives an error from the API.
Set 'temperature' to 0.0 to ensure the model is always confident.
Confidence-based routing where the agent is instructed to call an 'escalate_to_human' tool if its internal confidence score is below a threshold.
Use a 'Parallel Task' where a human and the AI both classify every comment.

explanation: Escalation and HITL patterns are critical for production reliability. Designing tools specifically for 'uncertainty handling' ensures the system fails gracefully to a human. Ref: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents

stem: You are building a data extraction tool for medical records. You need to ensure the 'PatientID' is always a 10-digit number. Which feature should you use to guarantee this format?

choices.text: The Message Batches API.
A 'Post ToolUse' hook that validates the ID and asks the model to retry if it's wrong.
Structured Output with a JSON Schema (using the 'output_format' parameter).
A detailed prompt explaining the 'PatientID' format with 10 examples.

explanation: The 'Structured Outputs' feature (beta) is the preferred architectural choice when specific, valid JSON formats are a strict requirement for downstream systems. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/overview

stem: A financial services agent is authorized to 'get_account_balance' but must never 'transfer_funds' if the amount exceeds $10,000 without a human-in-the-loop (HITL) approval. Which implementation provides a deterministic security guarantee?

choices.text: Use 'tool_choice' set to 'none' whenever a user mentions a large dollar amount.
Add a 'Negative Constraint' in the system prompt: 'NEVER transfer more than $10,000 without asking for permission.'
Implement a 'Pre ToolUse' hook that intercepts 'transfer_funds' calls and triggers an approval workflow if the amount is > $10,000.
Provide few-shot examples where the agent asks for permission for a $15,000 transfer and proceeds directly for a $500 transfer.

explanation: For critical business rules and safety boundaries, programmatic enforcement (like hooks or middleware) is the only valid architectural choice. Ref: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools

stem: When using the 'tool_use' feature for structured data extraction, you receive a 'stop_reason' of 'max_tokens' instead of 'tool_use'. The resulting JSON is truncated and invalid. What is the best immediate fix?

choices.text: Switch to 'tool_choice' type 'any' to force the model to try again.
Implement a retry loop that passes the truncated JSON back to Claude with a 'fix this' prompt.
Enable 'extended thinking' mode to allow the model more time to reason about the JSON structure.
Increase the 'max_tokens' value to accommodate the full expected size of the JSON output.

explanation: A 'max_tokens' stop reason is a clear indicator that the output length exceeded the provided budget. For large extractions, ensure the max_tokens value is sufficiently high. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/overview

stem: A structured data extraction pipeline is processing thousands of medical invoices. Some invoices contain hand-written notes that cause the model to occasionally produce malformed JSON. Which strategy provides the best balance of reliability and efficiency for this production workload?

choices.text: Implement a validation-retry loop that catches JSON errors and sends the error message back to the model for correction.
Increase the max_tokens parameter to ensure the model has enough space to finish the JSON.
Manually review every invoice that contains hand-written notes before processing.
Switch to a smaller, faster model for the extraction to reduce the cost of failures.

explanation: Validation-retry loops with explicit error feedback allow models to self-correct, which is a standard pattern for high-fidelity structured data extraction. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/overview

stem: A developer wants to ensure that Claude Code's 'Auto-Fix' feature doesn't introduce any security vulnerabilities. What is the most comprehensive strategy?

choices.text: Only allow Claude to work on 'non-sensitive' parts of the codebase.
Instruct Claude to 'be very secure' in the CLAUDE.md file.
Use 'Claude 3.7 Opus' for all tasks.
Implement a 'Post-Process' hook that runs a Static Analysis Security Testing (SAST) tool on any file Claude modifies.

explanation: The 'Trust but Verify' principle: Architects should use programmatic hooks to validate the AI's output against established security and quality benchmarks.

stem: You are extracting line items from thousands of physical receipts. Some receipts are blurry or have handwritten notes. Which architectural choice most improves the reliability of this high-volume pipeline?

choices.text: Implement a 'Validation-Retry' loop that uses a schema validator to catch malformed JSON and feeds the error back to Claude.
Increase the 'temperature' to 0.7 to allow the model to 'guess' the blurry text more creatively.
Use the 'Message Batches API' to save 50% on the cost of the failed attempts.
Switch to 'Claude 3 Opus' for every receipt to ensure maximum intelligence.

explanation: Production AI isn't about getting it right the first time 100% of the time; it's about building a system that knows when it's wrong and can fix itself. Ref: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents

stem: A developer is using Claude Code to build a new feature. They want to ensure Claude doesn't 'hallucinate' existing library functions that don't exist. Which configuration file is best for this?

choices.text: .gitignore
README.md
CLAUDE.md
package.json

explanation: CLAUDE.md serves as the 'Standard Operating Procedures' (SOP) manual for Claude Code, bridging the gap between general knowledge and project-specific reality.

stem: You have built a multi-agent 'Research Team' where a 'Manager' agent delegates to 'Search' and 'Analyst' subagents. You find that the 'Manager' often gets confused and repeats the same search three times. How can you most effectively improve the Manager's task tracking?

choices.text: Add more subagents to handle smaller pieces of the task, reducing the Manager's cognitive load.
Instruct the Manager to maintain a 'Progress Log' file using the 'Write' tool and read it at the start of every turn.
Use the 'Batch API' to process all search tasks at once.
Increase the 'temperature' of the Manager agent to encourage more creative task management.

explanation: When agents operate in long sessions, 'context bloat' can lead to degradation. Using a structured 'scratchpad' or 'state file' helps the agent maintain focus on its goals and progress. Ref: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents

stem: In a 'Multi-Pass' code review architecture, a 'Style Agent' and a 'Logic Agent' both review a Pull Request. Why is this better than one single agent doing both?

choices.text: It prevents 'Attention Dilution' and allows each agent to use a specialized system prompt for higher precision.
The agents can 'argue' with each other to find the truth.
It allows the use of the 'Message Batches API'.
It is 50% cheaper to run two agents than one large agent.

explanation: Task decomposition is a fundamental agentic pattern. 'Doing one thing well' is as true for AI agents as it is for Unix-style software components. Ref: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents

stem: Your agent is failing to use the 'search_database' tool correctly because it keeps passing a 'List' instead of the 'String' required by the API. What is the most durable fix?

choices.text: Add a note in the system prompt: 'NEVER pass a list to the search tool.'
Use a 'Post ToolUse' hook to convert the list back into a string.
Provide 10 few-shot examples showing a string being passed.
Update the Tool's Input Schema (JSON Schema) to explicitly define the parameter as 'type: string'.

explanation: Tool reliability starts with 'Schema Integrity.' A clear, constrained JSON Schema is the most powerful tool for ensuring correct agentic tool use. Ref: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools

stem: When using 'Claude Code', what is the primary purpose of the 'plan' mode?

choices.text: To allow Claude to write code faster by skipping the 'reasoning' phase.
To have Claude outline its intended actions and get human approval before any tools (like file writes) are actually executed.
To allow Claude to bypass the 200,000 token context limit.
To enable Claude to use the 'Message Batches API' for long-running tasks.

explanation: Discipline in planning is what separates 'certified architects' from casual users. It ensures the AI 'measures twice and cuts once' on your codebase.

stem: You are building a research agent that uses an MCP server to access a database. The model fails to use the correct date format. Which solution provides the best reliability?

choices.text: Update the MCP Tool's JSON schema description to explicitly mandate the correct date format (e.g. ISO 8601).
Implement a 'Post ToolUse' hook to normalize the dates.
Provide 10 few-shot examples in the system prompt showing the exact date format required.
Change the MCP server's database schema to accept any date format the model might produce.

explanation: The most reliable way to format tool inputs is to explicitly define the required format in the tool's JSON schema description. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/tool-use

stem: An architect is designing an MCP server that needs to support both local developers using Claude Desktop and a cloud-based agentic system. Which transport method should they implement to ensure maximum compatibility?

choices.text: gRPC, to ensure high-performance data transfer for large tool results.
The server should support both STDIO for local use and HTTP+SSE for remote/cloud connections.
WebSockets, as they provide full-duplex communication for real-time agents.
STDIO only, as it is the most secure method for tool execution.

explanation: MCP is designed for portability. Supporting both primary transport methods ensures the server can be utilized across various deployment environments. Ref: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools

stem: You are building a 'Code Review' agent. You want it to be particularly strict about 'SQL Injection' vulnerabilities. Which prompt engineering technique is most effective?

choices.text: Use 'Extended Thinking' mode and set the temperature to 1.0.
Repeatedly use the word 'DANGER' in the system prompt.
Define a 'Negative Constraint' with explicit 'Red-Line' examples of what constitutes a vulnerability.
Tell the model it is a 'Senior Security Engineer' and its job is at stake.

explanation: Effective security agents require 'Adversarial Prompting' techniques, such as explicit negative constraints and clear definitions of prohibited patterns. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/overview

stem: A developer is building an MCP server to expose a custom internal API to Claude. They notice that Claude frequently confuses two tools, 'query_db' and 'search_logs', because both accept a 'query' string. What is the most effective way to improve tool selection accuracy?

choices.text: Use 'strict: true' in the tool definition to ensure the input schemas are strictly validated.
Rewrite the tool descriptions to include 3-4 sentences detailing the specific data sources and explicit boundaries for each tool.
Rename the tools to 'Tool_A' and 'Tool_B' to force Claude to rely on the system prompt for instructions.
Add 'tool_use' examples for both tools in the global system prompt.

explanation: Tool descriptions are the 'universal remote' of MCP; they are the most important factor in whether Claude understands when and when not to use a specific capability. Ref: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools

stem: You are building a 'Travel Assistant' that needs to check flight prices across 5 different APIs. Which approach provides the best user experience?

choices.text: The agent should summarize its plan to check the APIs, then check them one by one.
The agent should use the 'Message Batches API' to check the flights.
The agent should check one API at a time and ask the user if they want to check the next one.
The agent should emit all 5 'check_flight' tool calls in parallel within a single turn.

explanation: Latency management is critical for user-facing agents. Parallel tool execution is the 'low-hanging fruit' for improving perceived performance. Ref: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents

stem: You are designing a 'Researcher Agent' that needs to pull data from a legacy API that returns very large, messy HTML tables. What is the best way to present this data to Claude?

choices.text: Pass the raw HTML directly to Claude and tell it to 'be careful' when reading the tables.
Screenshot the table and send it to Claude as an image.
Implement an MCP server that fetches the HTML and converts only the relevant table rows into a clean Markdown or JSON format.
Use the 'Batch API' to process each row of the table separately.

explanation: The 'MCP as a Filter' pattern: Use your server-side logic to prune and structure data before it ever hits the LLM's context. This is the single best way to maintain high performance in data-heavy apps. Ref: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools

stem: A developer is using Claude Code to debug a complex issue spanning multiple files. They want to ensure Claude maintains a clear 'scratchpad' of its findings and hypotheses across a long session. What is the best way to achieve this within the Claude Code environment?

choices.text: Rely on the conversation history, as Claude Code automatically summarizes old turns to save context.
Enable the 'long_context' flag in the Claude Code CLI settings.
Create a 'SCRATCHPAD.md' file and instruct Claude to update it with key findings after every investigation step.
Use the 'plan' mode for every turn to force Claude to restate its current understanding.

explanation: Implementing a 'scratchpad' file is a specific pattern for extracting and maintaining structured facts and hypotheses throughout a long development session. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching

stem: A user wants to use Claude Code to perform a massive search-and-replace across 5,000 files. What is the most token-efficient way for Claude to handle this?

choices.text: Claude should open each file one by one, perform the edit, and save it.
Upload all 5,000 files to the context window and ask for a single 'Refactor' response.
Instruct Claude to write a single Bash script to perform the replacement and run it using the 'Bash' tool.
Use the 'Agent Skills' feature to define a custom 'MultiFileReplace' skill.

explanation: Mastering the 'Bash' tool for bulk operations is a key skill for a Claude Architect. It leverages the underlying environment's power rather than relying on the LLM for repetitive manual edits.

stem: You are building a 'Code Migrator' that converts Java to Python. For a large project, you notice the model often 'forgets' the Java class structure by the time it gets to the third file. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: The model's attention is being diluted by the increasing amount of Java/Python code in the context window across multiple turns.
The developer is not using 'Extended Thinking' mode.
The Java code was provided in the system prompt instead of the user message.
Python and Java have conflicting syntax that causes the model's reasoning to 'crash'.

explanation: Context management is not just about 'fitting' tokens; it's about 'attention.' For long migrations, use a 'Master Reference' file or periodically restate the core architecture. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching

stem: A pharmaceutical company is building a 'Clinical Trial Assistant' that extracts dosage information from 500-page PDF protocols. When processing the entire document at once, Claude frequently misses specific adverse event reporting windows located in the middle sections. Which architectural change would most effectively improve the extraction recall for these middle sections?

choices.text: Switch to Claude 3 Haiku for the extraction task to reduce the computational overhead of processing 500 pages.
Increase the 'max_tokens' parameter to 128,000 to ensure the model has enough output space for all extracted data.
Implement a sliding window segmentation strategy where the document is split into overlapping 20-page chunks processed by parallel subagents.
Use the Message Batches API to process the document, as it provides higher throughput for large files.

explanation: The 'lost in the middle' effect describes how LLMs lose accuracy in the center of large context windows. Dividing the document so that every section becomes a 'beginning' or 'end' for a subagent is the standard remedy. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching

stem: An architect is designing a multi-agent system for 'Legal Discovery'. They need to process 1,000,000 documents. Which combination of features is most appropriate?

choices.text: Claude Code for bulk editing + Prompt Caching for the documents.
Message Batches API for bulk processing + Subagent delegation for handling long documents.
A single massive context window + 'Extended Thinking' mode.
Real-time Streaming API + 'Claude 3.7 Opus' for maximum accuracy.

explanation: Large-scale AI architecture requires balancing cost (Batch API), throughput (Parallelism), and reliability (Decomposition). Ref: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents

stem: During a complex multi-agent research task, you notice the coordinator agent frequently re-assigns the same sub-topic to different subagents, leading to redundant work and high token usage. What is the most likely architectural flaw?

choices.text: The coordinator is performing overly narrow task decomposition without tracking progress.
The 'Task' tool does not support parallel execution, causing the coordinator to lose track.
The system prompt for the subagents is too long, causing them to forget their assignments.
The subagents are not sharing a global memory space to see each other's work.

explanation: The coordinator is responsible for task decomposition and delegation; redundant assignments indicate a failure in partitioning the research scope. Ref: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents

stem: Your data extraction pipeline is failing because the PDFs contain 'Table of Contents' sections that confuse the extraction of the actual data. What is the best fix?

choices.text: Tell Claude in the prompt to 'ignore the Table of Contents'.
Use a 'Validation-Retry' loop to catch the errors.
Increase the 'temperature' so the model can 'look past' the TOC.
Pre-process the PDF to remove the 'Table of Contents' pages before sending the text to Claude.

explanation: Context quality is as important as context quantity. Pruning irrelevant or confusing sections of a document is a high-leverage optimization for extraction tasks. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching

stem: A retail company wants to use Claude to process thousands of customer feedback emails every night to generate a sentiment report for the 8:00 AM executive meeting. Real-time response is not required. Which API feature provides the best balance of cost-efficiency and reliability for this use case?

choices.text: Message Batches API
Claude Code with a custom 'Sentiment' subagent
Streaming Messages API with Sonnet 3.5
Standard Messages API with Prompt Caching

explanation: The Message Batches API is specifically designed for 'overnight' or bulk tasks where cost savings are prioritized over immediate latency. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/overview

stem: An agentic system for 'Automated Security Auditing' needs to run for several hours, exploring a codebase and running various scanners. How can you prevent the session from becoming too 'heavy' and slow?

choices.text: Implement a 'Document & Clear' pattern: periodically save findings to a markdown file, run ′/clear′, and start a fresh session reading that file.
Use 'Claude 3 Haiku' for all reasoning to save tokens.
Increase the 'max_tokens' to 200,000 for every turn.
Disable 'Prompt Caching' to ensure each turn is fresh.

explanation: Long-context performance degradation is a physical constraint. The 'Document & Clear' pattern is the standard architectural work-around for long-running agentic tasks. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching

stem: An architect is designing an MCP server to connect Claude to a proprietary internal search engine. The search engine requires a 'SessionID' header that expires every 30 minutes. How should the MCP server handle this?

choices.text: The MCP server should manage the session lifecycle internally, refreshing the token as needed without involving the model.
The model should be instructed to always provide a valid 'SessionID' in the tool arguments.
The MCP server should return an 'Expired Session' error and ask the model to call a 'refresh_token' tool.
Use a 'Post ToolUse' hook to inject the header into the request.

explanation: A key principle of MCP design is 'Separation of Concerns.' Technical infrastructure like session management should be invisible to the agent. Ref: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools

stem: A user wants to send a 10MB PDF to Claude for analysis. How does the Messages API handle this file?

choices.text: The developer sends a URL to the PDF in the 'source' parameter.
The PDF is sent as a 'tool result' from an MCP server.
The PDF must be converted to text or images and sent as part of the 'content' block.
The PDF is automatically cached by Anthropic for 24 hours.

explanation: API-based interactions require explicit data handling. PDF data must be transformed into the model's supported input types (text or image). Refer to: [https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/messages-api](https://www.google.com/searc h?q=https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/messages-api)

stem: You are building an MCP server that provides 'Weather Data'. The API you are using has a strict rate limit of 1 call per minute. How should the MCP server be implemented?

choices.text: The tool should be removed and replaced with a 'Message Batches API' call.
The MCP server should implement internal caching so that repeated requests within 60 seconds return the last fetched result.
The system prompt should instruct Claude to only check the weather once per hour.
The MCP server should return an error 'Please wait 60 seconds' and let the model handle the retry.

explanation: Reliable tool design requires handling technical constraints (caching, retries, rate-limiting) inside the tool/server implementation. Refer to: [https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools)

stem: A developer wants to use Claude to transform a messy text file into a clean CSV. Which prompt technique is most likely to produce a parseable result?

choices.text: Tell the model 'Make it look like a spreadsheet'.
Use 'Extended Thinking' to analyze the text.
Switch to the Message Batches API.
