Provide a 'CSV Header' example and specify the delimiter (e.g., 'Use a comma-separated format').

explanation: Structured output requires 'Syntactic Constraints.' Providing headers and delimiters is a fundamental engineering task. Refer to: [https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/structured-outputs](https://www.google.co m/search?q=https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/structured-outputs)

stem: You want Claude Code to always run your test suite (′npm test′) before it suggests a git commit. Which configuration approach is most robust?

choices.text: Implement a 'Pre ToolUse' hook that intercepts 'git commit' and executes the test script first.
Add 'Always run npm test before committing' to the project's CLAUDE.md file.
Use 'Extended Thinking' mode to remind the model to test its code.
Create a bash alias for 'git commit' that includes 'npm test'.

explanation: Programmatic hooks in Claude Code serve as 'Local CI,' enforcing project standards before state-changing actions occur.

stem: In an agentic system, what is the primary risk of 'Sycophancy' during a multi-agent review process?

choices.text: The agents will enter an infinite loop of apologizing to each other.
The Reviewer agent may try to delete the Coder agent's files.
The Coordinator agent will spend too many tokens on the review.
The Reviewer agent may agree with the Coder agent's mistakes simply because the Coder's reasoning sounds confident.

explanation: To combat sycophancy, architects should isolate the Reviewer's context from the Coder's internal chain-of-thought. Refer to the research at: [https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents](https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents)

stem: An MCP server is returning a 50MB CSV file to Claude's context. Claude starts becoming unresponsive and making errors. What should the architect change?

choices.text: Enable 'Extended Thinking' to help the model process the large file.
The MCP server should implement a 'summarize data' tool or return only the first 100 rows with a 'search' function.
Switch to the 'Message Batches API' to process the 50MB file.
Increase the 'max tokens' parameter to 1,000,000.

explanation: Architects must manage the 'Information Density' of tool outputs. MCP servers should filter and prune data before sending it to the model. Refer to: [https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools)

stem: You are configuring a 'Pre ToolUse' hook in Claude Code to prevent the agent from deleting files. Which exit code should the hook script return to indicate a policy violation and block the action?

choices.text: Exit code 1
Exit code 127
Exit code 2
Exit code 0

explanation: Claude Code interprets specific exit codes from hook scripts. Code 2 is the reserved signal for a 'Guardian' policy block. This is a core security feature documented in the Claude Code Customization guide: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/claude-code/customization

stem: A developer needs to ensure that a tool call for 'process payment' never runs twice for the same transaction. How should this be handled?

choices.text: Use Prompt Caching to remember the first call.
Tell Claude 'Do not call this tool twice' in the system prompt.
The tool implementation should require an 'idempotency key' and verify it on the backend.
Set the model's temperature to 0.0.

explanation: Building 'Resilient Tools' requires defensive programming on the server side. Never rely solely on the model for state integrity. Refer to: [https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools)

stem: An agentic workflow needs to process 5,000 customer feedback forms overnight for a report due the next morning. What is the most cost-efficient way to implement this?

choices.text: Use Claude 3.7 Haiku with parallel tool calls.
Use the Message Batches API.
Implement Prompt Caching for the feedback forms.
Deploy 100 parallel subagents using the Claude Agent SDK.

explanation: The Message Batches API is designed specifically for high-volume, non-latency-sensitive workloads. Refer to: [https ://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/batch-processing](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/batch-pro cessing)

stem: A lead engineer wants to enforce a rule that Claude Code can never 'git push' to the 'main' branch. How can this be achieved?

choices.text: Use a '.claudeignore' file to hide the '.git' directory.
Add 'DO NOT PUSH TO MAIN' in large letters in the CLAUDE.md file.
Delete the 'git' tool from the Claude Code binary.
Create a 'Pre ToolUse' hook that regex-checks the command for 'git push' and the 'main' branch, then exits with code 2 if found.

explanation: Hard security constraints in Claude Code are best implemented through hooks that return exit code 2.

stem: A legal research agent is failing to find specific clauses in 200-page contracts using standard RAG. What is the most reliable architectural improvement?

choices.text: Switch to an 'Opus-only' architecture for the embedding model.
Increase the 'top k' parameter to 100 to retrieve more snippets.
Use the Message Batches API to index the documents.
Contextual Retrieval: Use a subagent to prepend every 1000-token chunk with a brief context-setting summary before indexing.

explanation: Contextual Retrieval is a signature Anthropic pattern that addresses the limitations of standard RAG in long documents by providing context to individual chunks. Details can be found at: https://www.anthropic.com/news/contextual-retrieval

stem: You are building a tool that requires complex, multi-step reasoning before outputting a final JSON result. Which parameter should you enable to improve accuracy?

choices.text: reasoning mode': 'ultra'
max tokens': 200000
temperature': 0.0
thinking': { 'type': 'enabled', 'budget tokens': 2000 }

explanation: Extended Thinking is a specific feature of Claude 3.7 Sonnet that allows for internal chain-of-thought to improve logic performance. Refer to the Extended Thinking guide: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/extended-thinking

stem: Which 'tool choice' should a Coordinator use for a 'Reviewer' agent to ensure a structured report is always generated?

choices.text: { 'type': 'none' }
{ 'type': 'any' }
{ 'type': 'auto' }
{ 'type': 'tool', 'name': 'submit review' }

explanation: Forcing a specific tool via 'tool choice' is a powerful pattern for ensuring that an agent always outputs a deterministic artifact. See the Tool Use guide: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/tool-use#forcing-tool-use

stem: An MCP server is being designed to allow Claude to interact with a secure Financial API. How should the 'read account balance' tool handle authentication?

choices.text: The model should be prompted to ask the user for their API key and pass it as a tool argument.
The 'read account balance' tool should be defined in the system prompt rather than the MCP server.
The MCP server should use environment variables to manage API keys and handle the auth handshake internally.
The tool should return an 'Unauthorized' string and a URL for the model to click.

explanation: A key design principle of MCP is 'Separation of Concerns.' Technical details like authentication belong in the server layer. Refer to: [https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools)

stem: Which 'stop reason' indicates that the model has successfully completed its task and has nothing more to say?

choices.text: max tokens
stop sequence
tool use
end turn

explanation: Correctly identifying why a model stopped is essential for orchestrating the next turn in an agentic loop. Refer to: [htt ps://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/messages-api](https://www.google.com/search?q=https://docs.anthropic.com/e n/docs/build-with-claude/messages-api)

stem: An MCP server is designed to fetch 'Latest News'. It returns 20 full-length articles in every tool result. The agent is becoming slow and inaccurate. What should be done?

choices.text: Use Prompt Caching for the news articles.
Switch to 'Claude 3.7 Opus' to handle the extra context.
Increase the 'Extended Thinking' budget.
The MCP server should return only the Headlines and Summaries, with a separate tool to 'Read Full Article' by ID.

explanation: Information Density is key to agent performance. Multi-step 'Discovery-then-Retrieval' patterns are a standard architect choice. Refer to: [https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools)

stem: Which MCP concept allows Claude to 'view' a dynamic data source that changes over time, such as a live server log?

choices.text: Hooks
Prompts
Tools
Resources

explanation: Correct Option (D. Resources)This is correct because in the Model Context Protocol (MCP), Resources are the primitive designed to expose data and content from applications to the model. Resources can represent dynamic data sources that change over time, such as live server logs, current metrics, or real-time system states. MCP Resources support URI-based identification and can provide updated content when the underlying data changes.

stem: Your agentic research system is running too slow. The 'Analyzer' agent waits for the 'Downloader' agent to finish 10 separate files one by one. How should you optimize?

choices.text: Use Prompt Caching for the Downloader agent's system prompt.
Increase the 'Extended Thinking' budget for the Downloader agent.
Switch the Downloader agent to 'Claude 3.7 Haiku' to speed up the individual calls.
The Downloader agent should emit all 10 'download file' tool calls in parallel in a single turn.

explanation: Optimizing agentic latency requires moving from sequential to parallel orchestration where tasks are independent. Refer to: [https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents](https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents)

stem: A developer is extracting names from a text. The model keeps returning 'Name: John Doe' instead of just 'John Doe'. Which prompt engineering fix is best?

choices.text: Tell the model its output will be used in a Python script.
Use 'Extended Thinking' mode.
Specify 'Return ONLY the raw string, no labels or conversational filler' and use a few-shot example.
Set the temperature to 0.0.

explanation: Controlling the 'Post-Processing' burden is a key skill. Precision prompts and examples reduce the need for cleaning data. Refer to: [https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/structured-outputs](https://www.google.c om/search?q=https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/structured-outputs)

stem: A developer is implementing an MCP server in TypeScript to handle local file operations. Which code snippet correctly defines the 'list files' tool using the MCP SDK?

choices.text: server.createTool('list files').onCall(({ path }) => fs.list(path));
server.addTool({ name: 'list files', handler: (args) => { return fs.readdirSync(args.path); } });
server.tool('list files', { path: z.string() }, async ({ path }) => ({ content: [{ type: 'text', text: fs.readdirSync(path).join(' ') }] }));
mcp.register({ command: 'ls', schema: { path: 'string' }, callback: (path) => ls(path) });

explanation: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) requires tools to return a specific 'content' array containing objects with 'type' and 'text' fields to ensure interoperability. Refer to the official MCP documentation on 'Implementing a Server' at https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools

stem: An architect is designing a RAG system for a 100,000-page knowledge base. What is the most reliable way to handle the 'Lost in the Middle' problem in Claude?

choices.text: Use Prompt Caching for the entire 100,000-page dataset.
Contextual Retrieval: Prepend chunks with context and use a 'Reranker' to select the top 5 most relevant snippets.
Simply pass the top 100 chunks into the 200k context window.
Switch the embedding model to Claude 3.7 Sonnet.

explanation: Context Management is about 'Quality over Quantity.' Using Rerankers and Contextual Retrieval are the gold standards for reliability. Refer to: [https://www.anthropic.com/news/contextual-retrieval](https://www.anthropic.com/news/contextual-retrieval)

stem: Your agentic system needs to extract data from a document. You notice the model often gets the 'Date' format wrong (e.g., DD/MM vs MM/DD). What is the best fix?

choices.text: Update the JSON Schema in the 'tool definition' to include an 'example' or 'description' specifying the format.
Increase the 'temperature' to 1.0.
Use 'Extended Thinking' mode for every extraction.
Tell the model to 'be careful with dates' in the user prompt.

explanation: Structured output reliability is a function of 'Schema Clarity.' Always provide format hints within the schema properties. Refer to: [https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/tool-use\#best-practices](https://www.google.com/searc h?q=https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/tool-use%23best-practices)

stem: In an agentic system, the 'Coordinator' is failing to properly summarize the results from three subagents. What is the best reliability fix?

choices.text: Switch all agents to 'Claude 3.7 Haiku' to reduce 'reasoning noise'.
Implement a 'Verification' turn where a separate agent checks the Coordinator's summary against the subagents' raw outputs.
Increase the 'temperature' of the Coordinator to 0.7.
Put all three subagent results into the Coordinator's 'System Prompt'.

explanation: Reliability in agents is built through 'Check-and-Balance' architectures. Refer to: [https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents](https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents)

stem: In an agentic workflow, a 'Validator' agent marks a 'Coder' agent's work as 'Failed'. What should the Coordinator do to ensure progress?

choices.text: Assume the Validator is wrong and accept the Coder's original work.
Human-in-the-loop: Immediately stop and wait for a human to fix the code.
Restart the entire process from scratch with a higher temperature.
Pass the specific error message from the Validator back to the Coder for a second attempt (Self-Correction).

explanation: The 'Review-Correction' loop is a fundamental pattern for building high-reliability agentic systems. Refer to: [https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents](https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents)

stem: An architect is designing a 'Multi-Agent Coding Assistant'. Which role is responsible for ensuring the final code is merged without conflicts?

choices.text: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) server
The Coordinator Agent
The Prompt Caching layer
The Subagent (Coder)

explanation: Agentic orchestration requires a 'Central Authority' to manage state and resolve conflicts between parallel tasks. Refer to: [https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents](https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents)

stem: You are building a 'Code Migration' agent to move code from Python 2 to Python 3. Which agentic pattern is most appropriate for a 1,000-file repository?

choices.text: Parallel Subagent Delegation: A Coordinator triages files and assigns chunks to 10 parallel subagents for refactoring.
Sequential Loop: A single agent processes one file at a time until all 1,000 are complete.
Message Batches API: Send all 1,000 files in one batch for 'Zero-Shot' refactoring.
Extended Thinking: Use a single model with a massive thinking budget to refactor the entire repo in one turn.

explanation: Scaling agentic workflows requires 'Divide and Conquer' architectures. Parallel subagents provide both speed and fresh context for each file. Refer to: [https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents](https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents)

stem: When using the Messages API, which 'role' is required for the message containing the results of a tool execution?

choices.text: user
tool
system
assistant

explanation: A tool_result block is sent in a user-role message, tied to the tool_use id (Messages API). There is no tool role. system is the top-level system parameter. assistant is the model's own tool_use. Doc idea: Messages API, tool results.

stem: A developer needs Claude to extract 'Total Amount' and 'Currency' from receipts. The output must be consumed by a legacy system that only accepts XML. How should the architect proceed?

choices.text: Use the 'Structured Output' (JSON) feature and then write a Python script to convert it to XML.
Force 'tool choice' to a JSON schema, as Claude cannot generate XML natively.
Enable 'Extended Thinking' to help the model understand the XML tag structure.
Use the Messages API with a system prompt specifying the exact XML schema and few-shot examples.

explanation: If the consumer requires XML, say so in the system prompt and show a few examples. Structured outputs are JSON. tool_choice does not emit XML. Extended thinking does not change the schema. Doc idea: Prompt engineering, specify the format with examples.

stem: A developer wants to ensure that Claude Code never modifies any files in the 'archive/' folder. What is the correct way to enforce this?

choices.text: Tell Claude 'Don't touch the archive folder' in the first turn.
Make the 'archive/' folder 'read-only' at the OS level.
Use a 'Post ToolUse' hook to undo any changes to the folder.
Add an Edit deny such as Edit(archive/**). A Read deny on that path also blocks Edit and Write there.

explanation: Stop writes under archive/ with an Edit deny such as Edit(archive/**). A Read deny also blocks Edit and Write on that path (permissions: Read and Edit). .claudeignore is not a documented file. A PostToolUse undo runs after the write. OS read-only also works and is what B says; the permissions page is the Claude Code control, so the repaired choice D states the deny rule. A prompt in the first turn is not enforcement. Doc idea: Permissions, deny rules.

stem: In Claude Code, you want to see all available tools and their current configuration. Which command do you use?

choices.text: claude status
/mcp lists connected MCP tools. Built-in tools are in the tools reference. /config opens settings. There is no claude config tool inventory.
claude list-tools
claude help

explanation: There is no `claude config` inventory of every tool. /config opens settings. /mcp lists connected servers and tool counts (commands reference). Built-in tools are listed in the tools reference. `claude status`, `claude list-tools`, and `claude help` are not those commands. The choice text is corrected to the commands that exist. Doc idea: Commands, /mcp and /config.

stem: An agent is stuck in a loop calling the same 'search' tool with the same query 5 times. What is the likely cause?

choices.text: The tool result returned a vague error message that didn't help the agent realize it needed to pivot its strategy.
The agent is using the 'Message Batches API'.
The temperature is set to 0.0.
The model's 'max tokens' were set too low.

explanation: Debugging agent loops requires looking at the 'Feedback Loop.' Better error messages in tool results are the primary fix. Refer to: [https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents](https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents)

stem: Which MCP transport should be used for a web-based client that needs to connect to a remote MCP server?

choices.text: MQTT
GraphQL
Stdio
SSE (Server-Sent Events)

explanation: MCP is designed to be transport-agnostic, but SSE and Stdio are the two primary officially supported implementations. Refer to: [https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/transports](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/transports)

stem: An agentic system is tasked with 'Finding Security Vulnerabilities' in a codebase. Which architectural pattern improves reliability and reduces false positives?

choices.text: Few-Shot Prompting: Give the model 10 examples of vulnerabilities.
Multi-Agent Consensus: Use three independent agents to scan the code and only report vulnerabilities found by at least two.
Sequential Chain: Agent A finds bugs, Agent B finds bugs, and Agent C finds bugs in a single long thread.
Chain of Thought: Ask one agent to 'think step-by-step' about the vulnerabilities.

explanation: Building 'High-Fidelity' agents requires multi-agent verification strategies. Refer to: [https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents](https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents)

stem: In Claude Code, you notice that the agent is struggling to understand your project's custom folder structure. Which file should you update to fix this?

choices.text: CLAUDE.md at the root of the project.
The .gitignore file.
The project's README.md.
The package.json or requirements.txt file.

explanation: CLAUDE.md is the 'source of truth' for project-specific developer experience (DX) in Claude Code.

stem: You are using Claude Code and want to prevent it from ever reading your '.env' files. What is the most reliable method?

choices.text: Set the .env file to be 'Hidden' in the OS.
Rely on the fact that Claude Code is programmed by Anthropic to be safe.
Instruct Claude 'Do not read .env files' in the CLAUDE.md file.
Add a permissions.deny rule such as Read(./.env) and Read(**/.env).

explanation: There is no .claudeignore file. The permissions reference blocks reads with a deny rule such as Read(./.env) or Read(**/.env). A hidden OS flag and a CLAUDE.md sentence do not stop Read. 'It is safe because Anthropic built it' is not a control. Doc idea: Permissions, exclude sensitive files.

stem: In the Claude Agent SDK, a 'Coordinator' agent manages three subagents. When a subagent finishes its task, how is the state normally passed back to the Coordinator?

choices.text: The subagent directly modifies the Coordinator's system prompt.
The Coordinator receives a tool result containing the subagent's output string or structured data.
The Coordinator and subagents share a single synchronized memory object.
The subagent sends a Webhook directly to the client UI.

explanation: The Claude Agent SDK uses a hierarchical tool-calling pattern. Subagents are effectively 'tools' that return information to the parent. Refer to: [https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python)

stem: An agent is processing a long conversation (180k tokens). You notice it has started to forget the user's name provided in the first turn. What is the most cost-effective fix?

choices.text: Switch to Claude 3.7 Opus to take advantage of its better long-context recall.
Restart the session every 10 turns and manually re-paste the user's name.
Use Prompt Caching to pin the first turn (system prompt and initial user data) so it remains high-signal throughout the session.
Enable 'Extended Thinking' and increase the budget to 5000 tokens.

explanation: Context Management requires 'anchoring' critical information. Caching the start of a session is a primary technique for maintaining fidelity. Refer to: [https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching](https://docs.anthropic.com/ en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching)

stem: A developer wants to use an MCP server to connect Claude to a local SQLite database. Which transport protocol does the MCP SDK use by default for local communication?

choices.text: gRPC
WebSockets
HTTP/REST
Stdio (Standard Input/Output)

explanation: MCP transport layers are designed for simplicity. Stdio is the most common choice for local tool integration. Refer to: [https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/transports](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/transports)

stem: In the Claude Agent SDK, a subagent fails with an unhandled exception. How does the Coordinator agent perceive this event?

choices.text: The Coordinator is automatically 'rolled back' to the previous turn.
The 'Task' tool returns an error message as the tool result, allowing the Coordinator to attempt a recovery.
The entire Coordinator process crashes immediately.
The Coordinator receives a blank response turn.

explanation: Robust agentic systems treat subagent failures as data, allowing for autonomous recovery. Refer to the Claude Agent SDK documentation on GitHub for architecture patterns: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python

stem: A team wants to ensure that Claude Code follows a specific naming convention for all new documentation files. Where is the most effective place to define this?

choices.text: The project's CLAUDE.md file.
The project's README.md file.
The global \~/.claude config file.
A .claudeignore file.

explanation: CLAUDE.md acts as the persistent 'local memory' for Claude Code, ensuring it adheres to a project's unique Developer Experience (DX) rules.

stem: An MCP server provides a tool to 'Search Jira'. The tool takes a 'query' string. How should the server handle a case where the Jira API returns a 401 Unauthorized error?

choices.text: Crash the MCP server to signal a hard failure to the client.
Return an empty list of results [].
Retry the request 100 times in a loop.
Return a tool result string explaining that the API key is invalid or expired.

explanation: MCP servers must provide semantic feedback for errors. This allows the Claude agent to provide helpful troubleshooting advice. Refer to: [https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools)

stem: You are using 'tool choice' to force an agent to use a 'database query' tool. The agent's response turn only includes the tool call and no conversational text. Why?

choices.text: The agent is using the 'Message Batches API'.
The model's 'temperature' is set to 0.0.
This is the expected behavior of 'forced tool use'; the model bypasses natural language to fulfill the constraint.
The 'thinking' budget was set to 0.

explanation: Architects use forced tool calls to create 'Headless' agents that generate structured data without conversational overhead. Refer to: [https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/tool-use\#forcing-tool-use](https://www.google.com/sear ch?q=https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/tool-use%23forcing-tool-use)

stem: Which of the following JSON fragments correctly implements 'Prompt Caching' for a large system prompt using the Messages API?

choices.text: content': 'You are an expert...', 'cache control': {'type': 'ephemeral'}
system': 'You are...', 'persistent': true
metadata': {'cache': 'true'}, 'content': 'You are...'
cache breakpoint': 0, 'content': 'You are...'

explanation: To enable caching, you must explicitly mark content blocks with the 'ephemeral' cache control type to signal the API to store that prefix. Refer to the Prompt Caching guide: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching

stem: A developer wants Claude Code to 'write a summary of the current git diff and save it to DIFF.md'. Which command is most efficient?

choices.text: claude write-file DIFF.md --content $(git diff)
claude --task summarize-diff
claude run git diff \> DIFF.md
claude 'summarize the git diff and save to DIFF.md'

explanation: Claude Code is 'Tool-Augmented.' It uses its understanding of the environment to choose the right sequence of actions.

stem: Your agentic workflow is hitting the '60 requests per minute' rate limit of the Anthropic API. What is the most effective architectural fix?

choices.text: Create 10 different API keys and rotate them.
Switch to the Message Batches API for all real-time tasks.
Increase the 'Prompt Caching' TTL.
Implement a 'Tool Output Aggregator' so the agent makes fewer, larger turns instead of many small ones.

explanation: Architecting for 'Throughput' involves optimizing the conversational loop. Fewer, higher-signal turns are better for scaling. Refer to: [https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/messages-api](https://www.google.com/search?q=https://d ocs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/messages-api)

stem: A researcher is using Claude to summarize a 500-page book. They plan to use Prompt Caching to save money. Where should the 'cache control' block be placed for maximum effect?

choices.text: In the 'metadata' field of the API request.
Immediately after the book's full text content in the user message.
In the tool definition for the 'summarizer' tool.

explanation: The Batch API provides independent processing of requests, ensuring that one malformed item doesn't invalidate the entire workload. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/batch-api#handling-errors

stem: A developer wants to use Claude to generate a complex Kubernetes manifest. The model keeps making small syntax errors. Which prompt engineering technique is most likely to resolve this?

choices.text: Increase the temperature to 0.7 to allow for more creative manifest designs.
Ask the model to 'Be a Kubernetes Expert' and use 'Chain of Thought'.
Tell the model 'This is very important for my job'.
Provide 3-5 'few-shot' examples of valid Kubernetes manifests in the system prompt.

explanation: Few-shot prompting is the gold standard for improving performance on technical tasks with specific syntax requirements. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/few-shot-prompting

stem: A developer wants to implement a multi-agent system where a 'Planner' agent creates a JSON list of tasks for a 'Worker' agent. Which pattern is most effective for ensuring the Worker follows the JSON exactly?

choices.text: Use 'Extended Thinking' to help the Worker understand the JSON better.
Set temperature to 1.0 to ensure the Worker is flexible.
Tell the Worker 'You are a JSON parser' in the system prompt.
Enforce the JSON structure using 'tool_use' with a predefined JSON schema on the Worker agent.

explanation: JSON schemas and tool_use provide the strongest guarantees for structured data extraction and instruction following. Refer to: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/tool-use

stem: What is the role of the 'Server Discovery' phase in the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?

choices.text: It is a security handshake where the server validates the LLM's API key.
It is a broadcast signal that allows MCP servers to find any available LLM on the network.
It is a process where the LLM automatically scans the user's hard drive for .mcp files.
It is not a formal protocol phase; clients are manually configured with server connection details (like an executable path or SSE URL).

explanation: MCP servers are explicitly configured in the host client; there is no 'magic' discovery mechanism in the current protocol. Ref: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/architecture

stem: A developer wants Claude Code to deny reads of every file ending in .log and everything in build/. Which permissions.deny rules are correct?

choices.text: Read(**/*.log) and Read(build/**)
NO_READ: [.log, build/]
CLAUDE_EXCLUDE: build/, .log
ignore .log, build/

explanation: Deny rules take gitignore-style patterns inside the tool specifier, such as Read(**/*.log) and Read(build/**). A line that is only '.log build/' is not a settings entry. NO_READ and CLAUDE_EXCLUDE are not keys. Doc idea: Permissions, wildcard patterns.

stem: A structured data extraction pipeline is processing thousands of medical invoices. Some invoices contain hand-written notes that cause the model to occasionally produce malformed JSON. Which strategy provides the best balance of reliability and efficiency for this production workload?

choices.text: Implement a validation-retry loop that catches JSON errors and sends the error message back to the model for correction.
Switch to a smaller, faster model for the extraction to reduce the cost of failures.
Increase the max_tokens parameter to ensure the model has enough space to finish the JSON.
Manually review every invoice that contains hand-written notes before processing.

explanation: Validation-retry loops with explicit error feedback allow models to self-correct, which is a standard pattern for high-fidelity structured data extraction. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/retry-logic

stem: You are designing a coding agent that needs to work across a mono-repo with millions of lines of code. How should the agent find the relevant files to edit?

choices.text: Use the Batch API to index the repository every time the agent starts.
Implement a multi-step 'Explore-then-Act' loop where the agent first uses search tools (like grep or ripgrep) to identify relevant files.
Load the entire mono-repo file tree into the system prompt.
Ask the user to provide the exact file paths for every single turn.

explanation: Navigating large contexts requires tools for search and discovery, enabling an 'Explore-then-Act' workflow. Ref: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents

stem: When implementing an MCP server that manages a local file system, which security measure is MOST critical to prevent a 'Path Traversal' attack where an agent might access files outside the project directory?

choices.text: Sanitize all input paths by resolving them to their absolute path and checking if they start with the allowed root directory.
Use a .claudeignore file to list all folders on the machine.
Add 'Stay within the current directory' to the MCP tool description.
Configure the MCP transport to use 'stdio' instead of 'SSE'.

explanation: Server-side validation is required for security; agents should never be trusted to self-police their file access limits. Ref: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/security

stem: In an MCP server, what is the purpose of the 'resources' concept compared to 'tools'?

choices.text: Resources are used to manage API keys, while tools manage function calls.
Resources provide read-only data (like a documentation file or log), while tools are for taking actions (like writing a file).
Resources allow the LLM to call other LLMs, while tools are for local code execution.
Resources are only for image files, while tools are for text-based tasks.

explanation: Resources provide a standardized way to expose data to Claude, while tools expose capabilities. Ref: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/resources

stem: You are implementing Prompt Caching for a financial analysis tool that uses a massive 100k token quarterly report. The user often asks follow-up questions about specific tables. How should you structure the message to maximize cache hits?

choices.text: Send the report as a separate 'user' message with no caching, as 100k tokens is too large to cache.
Place the quarterly report at the beginning of the prompt and mark it with 'cache_control': {'type': 'ephemeral'}.
Use the Message Batches API for all queries related to the 100k report.
Place the user's latest question first, followed by the quarterly report.

explanation: Prompt caching is prefix-based; placing stable, large context blocks at the start of the message array is the recommended architecture. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching

stem: A coordinator agent is failing to correctly synthesize information from two subagents because the outputs from the subagents are too long, causing the coordinator to hit its context limit. What is the best fix?

choices.text: Switch the coordinator to a model with a smaller context window to force it to be faster.
Instruct the subagents to provide their findings in a structured, concise JSON format or bulleted summary.
Have the coordinator read the subagents' outputs from a shared text file instead of receiving them in the message history.
Tell the coordinator to ignore any output longer than 1000 tokens.

explanation: Context management in multi-agent systems requires designing subagents to be 'high-signal, low-noise' in their reports. Ref: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents

stem: A developer wants Claude Code to always run 'npm run lint' before every git commit it makes. Where should this instruction be placed for the most reliable enforcement?

choices.text: In a project-level 'pre-commit' git hook that the developer configures in the repository.
In the system prompt provided to Claude via the CLI.
In the user's ~/.bashrc file.
In the CLAUDE.md file as a 'Rule'.

explanation: Reliable automation should use standard software engineering practices like Git hooks to enforce quality standards.

stem: A multi-agent system uses a 'Refining' subagent to check the work of a 'Drafting' subagent. The Architect notices the 'Refining' agent is providing generic feedback like 'looks good' instead of detailed critiques. What is the most effective fix?

choices.text: Enable 'Extended Thinking' for the 'Drafting' agent only.
Increase the temperature of the 'Refining' agent to 1.0.
Use a larger model for the 'Drafting' agent and a smaller one for 'Refining'.
Provide the 'Refining' agent with a specific rubric or checklist to use for evaluation in its system prompt.

explanation: Multi-pass review architectures require explicit rubrics to guide the reviewing model's attention. Ref: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents

stem: When implementing an MCP server in Python, which library is typically used to handle the JSON-RPC communication and protocol state?

choices.text: The official 'mcp' Python SDK.
Pytest.
Flask or FastAPI.
Requests.

explanation: Using the official SDK ensures compliance with the Model Context Protocol specification. Refer to: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/tools/python

stem: An architect is designing an MCP server to provide real-time inventory data from a legacy SQL database. The LLM occasionally attempts to join too many tables, causing timeout errors. What is the most resilient tool design to prevent this?

choices.text: Enable Prompt Caching for the database schema to help the model reason better.
Add 'Do not perform complex joins' to the tool's description field.
Refactor the MCP tool to accept only a single 'Product_ID' and return pre-joined view data rather than allowing raw SQL generation.
Increase the timeout duration on the MCP server to 60 seconds.

explanation: Constraining tool inputs and returning structured views is a core principle of reliable tool design for agentic systems. Ref: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools

stem: A developer is using Claude Code to refactor a large legacy repository. They notice that Claude occasionally makes changes that violate the project's specific architectural patterns, such as placing business logic inside data access objects. Which configuration would most effectively prevent these violations?

choices.text: Update the global Claude Code system prompt via the CLI settings.
Use plan mode for every interaction to manually review the architectural approach.
Add architectural guidelines to a CLAUDE.md file in the root directory.
Create a custom slash command for every refactoring task to include the rules.

explanation: CLAUDE.md files are the primary mechanism for providing persistent, project-specific context and constraints to Claude Code.

stem: A financial analyst is using Claude to summarize a 200-page regulatory filing. The model's response is often cut off mid-sentence. Which API parameter adjustment is most likely to resolve this?

choices.text: Decrease 'temperature' to 0.0.
Add 'summarize the whole document' to the user prompt.
Enable 'Extended Thinking' with a 2000 token budget.
Increase 'max_tokens' to its maximum limit (e.g., 4096 or 8192).

explanation: Response truncation is almost always caused by the 'max_tokens' limit being reached. Refer to: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/messages-api

stem: A developer wants to use Claude 3.5 Sonnet to extract data from 5,000 scanned invoices. They have the images as JPEGs. What is the most cost-effective architecture?

choices.text: Use the Message Batches API to process all images in bulk, as it offers a 50% discount on token costs.
Use Prompt Caching for each image.
Process them sequentially using a single real-time API connection.
Convert the JPEGs to text using an OCR service first, then use Claude 3.5 Haiku.

explanation: For large-scale, non-interactive document processing, the Message Batches API is the standard recommendation. Refer to: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/batch-api

stem: You are extracting data from hundreds of resumes. Some resumes are in PDF format and others are images. How should you optimize your API usage to handle both formats efficiently while ensuring structured JSON output?

choices.text: Use the 'thinking' parameter to have Claude describe the resume first, then extract the data.
Pass the document content to Claude 3.5 Sonnet using the 'tool_use' parameter with a strictly defined JSON schema.
Convert all documents to raw text using OCR first, then send the text to Claude.
Use the Batch API with a simple text-based prompt asking for 'CSV format'.

explanation: JSON schema via tool_use is the most reliable way to perform structured data extraction in production. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/tool-use#json-schema

stem: A coordinator agent is managing 5 parallel subagents. One subagent returns a 'Tool Error' because an external API is down. What is the BEST orchestration strategy for the coordinator?

choices.text: The coordinator should retry the failed subagent 50 times in a loop.
The coordinator should ignore the error and 'hallucinate' a successful result for the failed subagent.
The coordinator should immediately terminate all other subagents to save tokens.
The coordinator should analyze the error, report it to the user, and proceed with the results from the other 4 subagents if possible.

explanation: Reliable agents must be designed to handle partial failures gracefully. Refer to: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents

stem: When using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) with 'stdio' transport, how does the client communicate with the server?

choices.text: The client sends HTTP POST requests to a local port (e.g., 8080).
The client writes a file to disk that the server polls every 5 seconds.
The client and server communicate via a shared SQLite database.
The client spawns the server as a child process and uses standard input/output streams for JSON-RPC messages.

explanation: Stdio transport is the foundation of local MCP integration, enabling low-latency communication between processes. Refer to: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/transports

stem: Production data shows that in 12% of cases your agent skips get_customer entirely and calls lookup_order using only the customer's stated name, occasionally leading to misidentified accounts and incorrect refunds. What change would most effectively address this reliability issue?

choices.text: Add a programmatic prerequisite that blocks lookup_order and process_refund calls until get_customer has returned a verified customer ID.
Implement a routing classifier that analyzes each request and enables only the subset of tools appropriate for that request type.
Add few-shot examples showing the agent always calling get_customer first, even when customers volunteer order details.
Enhance the system prompt to state that customer verification via get_customer is mandatory before any order operations.

explanation: Programmatic enforcement through prerequisite gates is the most effective way to ensure deterministic compliance for critical workflow steps like identity verification. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/tool-use

stem: When implementing a 'Human-in-the-Loop' (HITL) pattern for a high-value payment agent, at which point should the system escalate to a human?

choices.text: After every single tool call, to ensure 100% accuracy.
When the API returns a 500 error code.
When the model identifies a policy gap, or when the confidence score for a proposed action is below a certain threshold.
Only when the model explicitly says 'I need help'.

explanation: Effective HITL design uses confidence thresholds and policy-based triggers to balance autonomy and safety. Ref: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents

stem: You are building an MCP server that connects to a company's Jira instance. To ensure the LLM doesn't accidentally spam tickets, which tool design pattern is BEST?

choices.text: Implement a 'Human-in-the-Loop' confirmation step in the client application before the MCP tool call is executed.
Use a system prompt that says 'Never create more than one ticket per hour'.
Change the MCP transport from stdio to SSE.
Set 'max_tokens' to a low value for the 'create_ticket' tool.

explanation: Critical or destructive actions should always have a deterministic safety gate, usually involving human approval. Refer to: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools

stem: Which of these is NOT a valid field in an MCP 'Tool' definition?

choices.text: description'
input_schema'
max_tokens_per_call'
name'

explanation: MCP tool definitions focus on identity and interface; execution constraints are managed elsewhere. Refer to: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools

stem: A multi-agent research system uses a 'Manager' to coordinate 10 subagents. You notice the Manager frequently gets confused and re-assigns the same sub-task multiple times. Which architectural fix is most effective?

choices.text: Instruct the Manager to maintain a 'Task Board' file and read it at the start of every turn.
Increase the 'temperature' of the Manager.
Use 'Claude 3 Haiku' for the Manager to save on token costs.
Add more subagents to reduce the Manager's cognitive load.

explanation: Coordinating 10 parallel subagents is an 'Information-Dense' task that can quickly saturate an orchestrator's context window. To prevent 'Reasoning Drift' and redundant task assignments, the 'Manager' needs a 'Persistent Source of Truth.' The 'Task Board Pattern' involves giving the agent a tool to update a structured file (like TASKS.json) that tracks the status of every sub-mission. By reading this file at the start of every turn, the agent maintains a clear 'State Map,' ensuring it only assigns new work and avoids looping on completed items. This programmatic memory is essential for stable, long-running agentic missions. Ref: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents

stem: When extracting data from a multi-column table in a PDF, you receive a 'stop_reason' of 'max_tokens' and the JSON is cut off. What is the best immediate fix?

choices.text: Switch to 'tool_choice' type 'any'.
Increase the 'max_tokens' value in the API request to accommodate the full expected size of the JSON output.
Provide few-shot examples of smaller tables.
Enable 'Extended Thinking' mode.

explanation: A 'max_tokens' stop reason is a 'Physical Resource Boundary' signal. It indicates that the model's response reached the 'Output Token Budget' you set in the API request before it could finish generating the JSON structure. For structured extraction tasks, which often involve verbose JSON formatting, architects must ensure the 'max_tokens' parameter is set high enough to accommodate the worst-case output length. If the issue persists despite a high limit, the secondary architectural strategy is 'Task Decomposition' breaking the large table into smaller sub-sections (e.g., 5 rows at a time) to ensure each turn completes successfully. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/overview

stem: During a multi-agent research session, the 'Search' subagent fails because a target website's API is down. How should a robust 'Coordinator' agent handle this partial failure?

choices.text: Immediately terminate the entire session and return an error to the user.
Ask the user to fix the website's API before continuing.
Use its internal reasoning to 'hallucinate' plausible data to fill the gap.
Catch the error from the Search subagent and re-task it to use an alternative tool or data source.

explanation: Professional agent architecture requires 'Graceful Failure Recovery.' In a multi-agent system, the failure of a single subagent should not necessarily crash the entire mission. A robust 'Coordinator' agent should be prompted with 'Fallback Strategies.' If a primary tool call (like a specialized API search) returns an error, the Coordinator should detect this in the tool output and attempt to re-route the task. For example, it could re-task the subagent to use a general web search or a different database. This 'Self-Healing' behavior is what distinguishes a reliable agent from a simple automation script. Ref: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents

stem: When designing a JSON schema for 'Structured Output', you want to ensure the model extracts dates in the ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). What is the most effective way to enforce this?

choices.text: Use few-shot examples with different date formats.
Add 'Use ISO 8601' to the field's description in the JSON schema.
Implement a regex check in a 'Post ToolUse' hook.
Set the temperature to 1.0.

explanation: Structured output reliability starts with 'High-Fidelity Tool Schemas.' In the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the 'Description' field of a JSON parameter is more than just documentation it is a 'Direct Instruction' that the model attends to during the generation phase. By explicitly defining the required format (e.g., 'ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD)') within the schema itself, you provide the model with a 'Guardrail' that is present at the exact moment of decision-making. This structural grounding is significantly more effective than general system prompt instructions and ensures the output is machine-readable without needing extensive post-processing. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/tool-use

stem: In which scenario is 'plan' mode in Claude Code most beneficial for a developer?

choices.text: When performing a complex refactor that affects multiple modules and architectural layers.
When performing a simple one-line bug fix in a single file.
When searching the codebase for a specific string using 'grep'.
When running a single unit test using the 'bash' tool.

explanation: Plan mode is a critical 'Human-in-the-Loop' (HITL) safety feature designed for 'Destructive' or 'Wide-Ranging' operations. By forcing the AI to generate a step-by-step strategy *before* executing any file writes or tool calls, the developer has the opportunity to audit the reasoning and catch potential side effects. This 'Think-Before-Act' pattern is essential for complex architectural changes where an incorrect assumption by the AI could lead to extensive manual cleanup. Architects should advise using Plan mode for any task that involves more than 3 files or changes to core interfaces, as it ensures the AI 'measures twice and cuts once.'.

stem: An architect is designing a pipeline to extract data from 10,000 unstructured invoices. The extraction requires high precision but can be processed overnight. Which approach is most cost-effective?

choices.text: Message Batches API
Streaming Messages API.
Claude Code with a custom 'Extractor' skill.
Prompt Caching for each invoice.

explanation: The 'Economic Selection' for high-volume, offline workloads is the Message Batches API. In a large-scale invoice processing project, real-time response (latency) is less important than cost-per-unit. The Batch API provides a 50% discount on standard token pricing by allowing the infrastructure to process requests in bulk over a 24-hour window. This 50% cost saving can be the difference between a project being commercially viable or not. Architects should always identify 'Latency-Agnostic' workloads and route them through the Batch API to maximize ROI. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/overview

stem: A support agent is being used for 'Troubleshooting' complex hardware issues. The interaction often spans 30+ turns. After 20 turns, the agent starts repeating the same basic diagnostic steps. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: The temperature is set too high (1.0).
The model has run out of tokens in its context window.
The model's attention is being diluted by the growing conversation history, causing it to lose track of completed steps.
The user is providing inconsistent information.

explanation: Looping behavior and repetition are technical signals of 'Context Saturation.' As a conversation grows, the model's attention must be distributed over an increasing number of tokens, making it harder to distinguish between 'completed steps' and 'next steps.' To prevent this, architects should implement 'Context Maintenance' strategies. This includes using a 'State Tool' to track diagnostic progress in a dedicated file, or performing periodic 'Context Pruning' (e.g., using the /clear command in developer tools or programmatically truncating older turns). By keeping the context window focused on the current problem state rather than the entire raw history, you maintain the model's reasoning fidelity over long durations. Ref: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents

stem: You are building a 'Legal Discovery' system where an agent must find relevant clauses across 10,000 documents. To ensure high recall for information located in the middle of long documents, which strategy should you use?

choices.text: Use the 'Message Batches API' to process the full documents.
Implement a sliding window segmentation strategy where documents are split into overlapping 20-page chunks.
Load each full document into the context window for a single pass.
Instruct the model to 'be very careful with the middle pages'.

explanation: Long-context performance is not uniform. LLMs exhibit the 'Lost in the Middle' effect, where they are significantly better at attending to information at the very beginning or very end of their context window. For critical missions like legal discovery, relying on a single large-window pass is risky. The 'Segmentation Pattern' involves splitting large documents into smaller, overlapping chunks (e.g., 20 pages with a 5-page overlap). This ensures that every section of the text is processed as 'Primary Context' by an agent, maximizing recall and ensuring that no vital clauses are missed due to attention dilution in the center of a massive token stream. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching

stem: You are running Claude Code in a CI environment with strict time limits (10 minutes per job). How can you most effectively ensure the review completes within this window?

choices.text: Use the --max-turns flag to limit the total number of steps Claude can take during the automated session.
Disable all 'Bash' and 'Read' tools to speed up the turns.
Switch to 'Claude 3.7 Opus' to get the answer faster in fewer turns.
Instruct Claude to 'work as fast as possible' in the CLAUDE.md file.

explanation: Running agentic tools in ephemeral CI environments requires 'Deterministic Boundaries.' Unlike a local terminal where a human can wait, a CI job has a fixed cost and a hard timeout. The –max-turns flag is a vital architectural tool for 'Execution Control.' It limits the number of 'Reason-Act-Observe' loops the model can perform, preventing 'Agentic Loops' (where the AI gets stuck trying to fix a complex problem) from consuming the entire CI budget. As a best practice, architects should set a conservative –max-turns limit for automated reviews, ensuring that the tool provides a 'Best-Effort' analysis within the allotted time and budget.

stem: A developer wants to ensure that Claude Code's automated PR feedback is posted directly as comments on the GitHub Pull Request. What is the best architectural approach?

choices.text: Instruct Claude to 'log in to GitHub' and post the comment itself.
Claude Code natively supports posting to GitHub via the --github flag.
Use the '--output-format json' flag and a separate script that pipes the JSON results to the GitHub PR Comments API.
Give Claude Code the 'write' permission to the '.git' directory.

explanation: Professional CI/CD architectures follow the 'Decoupling Principle.' While it is tempting to want the AI tool to 'do everything,' a more robust and secure pattern is to have the AI perform the 'Reasoning' (analysis) and output the results in a 'Structured Format' (JSON). A separate, lightweight automation script (like a GitHub Action) then handles the 'Platform-Specific Integration' by posting those results to the API. This separation of concerns allows for easier testing, better security (you don't need to give the AI your GitHub credentials), and the ability to swap out the AI tool or the hosting platform without a total system redesign.

stem: A research agent needs to summarize 50 academic papers. You use 'Prompt Caching' to store the papers' contents. Which statement best describes the cost implications of this architecture?

choices.text: Caching is automatically applied and does not change the billing model.
Caching is only cost-effective for contexts under 5,000 tokens.
The first 'write' turn to the cache is more expensive than standard input, but subsequent 'hits' are 90% cheaper.
Caching reduces the cost of both input and output tokens by 50%.

explanation: Prompt Caching is an 'Economic Optimization' that requires careful architectural calculation. The pricing model involves a 'Write Penalty' (25% higher cost for the first turn) followed by a 'Read Discount' (up to 90% cheaper for subsequent hits). This means caching is only cost-effective for 'Heavy-Context' scenarios where the same baseline tokens (like 50 academic papers) are reused for at least 3-4 turns. If the mission is a single turn, caching will actually *increase* your costs. Architects should identify 'Persistent Context' layers and use caching breakpoints to optimize long-running research sessions. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching

stem: In a multi-agent research system, the 'Synthesis' agent is producing reports that lack the specific data found by the 'Search' agent. Investigation shows both agents are being called successfully. What is the most likely architectural flaw?

choices.text: The 'Synthesis' agent has a lower 'temperature' setting than the 'Search' agent.
The 'Search' agent's context is too large for the 'Synthesis' agent to read.
The Coordinator is not explicitly passing the 'Search' agent's results into the 'Synthesis' agent's prompt.
The 'Search' agent is using 'Prompt Caching' incorrectly.

explanation: The 'Data Propagation' pattern is the most critical mental model for multi-agent architects. Because subagents operate in 'Isolated Contexts,' they have no awareness of what other agents have discovered unless that information is explicitly 'Bridged' by the Coordinator. If a Synthesis agent fails to use data found by a Search agent, it is almost always because the Coordinator failed to summarize and inject those findings into the Synthesis agent's initialization prompt. Architects must ensure that the 'handoff' between agents includes all necessary facts, acting as the 'Context Router' for the entire system. Ref: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents

stem: You want to use the 'Glob' tool to find all JavaScript files in a repository, but only those within the 'src' directory. What is the most efficient pattern to use?

choices.text: src/*.js
src/**/*.js
ls -R | grep .js

explanation: Precision in tool calls is a hallmark of an expert agent. When navigating large repositories, using generic patterns (like **/*.js) can cause the tool to scan thousands of irrelevant files (like node_modules), consuming time and potentially hitting file limits. By 'Scoping the Search' (e.g., src/**/*.js), the developer (or the agent) provides a clear hint to the underlying system to ignore unrelated directories. This optimization reduces the 'Exploration Token Cost' and ensures the agent finds the relevant files faster, maintaining a cleaner and more efficient session context.

stem: A customer support agent is receiving a high volume of off-topic requests (e.g., asking for weather updates). Which architectural component most efficiently prevents the main support agent from wasting tokens on these requests?

choices.text: Set the temperature to 0.0 to ensure the agent stays focused.
Increase the 'max_tokens' to allow the agent to explain why it cannot help.
Add a 'No Off-Topic' section to the system prompt.
Implement a lightweight 'Routing Classifier' (using Haiku) to filter or redirect requests before they reach the main agent.

explanation: Token efficiency is a major architectural concern in production support systems. Processing every user message with a high-capability model like Sonnet or Opus is expensive, especially when many messages are trivial or irrelevant. A 'Tiered Triage' architecture uses a lightweight 'Routing Classifier' (typically powered by Haiku) to analyze the intent of the incoming message first. If the message is off-topic, the classifier can trigger a hard-coded rejection response or redirect the user, bypassing the expensive main agent entirely. This pattern drastically reduces operational costs, mitigates the risk of prompt injection, and ensures the main agent's context window is reserved for high-value support interactions. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/overview

stem: A developer is using productivity tools to navigate an unfamiliar 5,000-file codebase. They need to find all occurrences of a specific internal error code ('ERR_731') across the entire project. Which built-in tool is most efficient for this task?

choices.text: Glob
Read
Grep
Bash

explanation: Efficient codebase navigation requires using 'High-Throughput' search tools. In a large project, reading files individually is the most expensive and slowest way to find information. The built-in 'Grep' tool allows the agent to scan thousands of files in a single turn, returning only the relevant 'Signal' (matching lines and filenames). This drastically reduces the number of tokens the model has to consume to find its goal. As a best practice, architects should prompt agents to 'Search before Reading,' ensuring they use Grep or Glob to narrow down their search space before performing high-fidelity file reads.

stem: When building an MCP tool that returns 10MB of raw log data, how should you optimize the response for the agent?

choices.text: Implement server-side filtering to return only the 100 most relevant log lines or high-signal errors.
Compress the log data using GZIP before returning it.
Return the data in 100 separate 100KB chunks.
Return the full 10MB to ensure no information is lost.

explanation: Context Hygiene' is a primary architectural responsibility in agentic systems. Passing massive, unfiltered data structures into the model's context window leads to 'Attention Dilution' and significantly higher costs. Professional MCP tools should perform 'Edge Processing.' Instead of returning 10MB of raw logs, the tool should accept parameters for filtering (e.g., 'level=ERROR') and only return the high-signal data. If the model needs more detail, it can make a follow-up call. This 'Demand-Driven Detail' pattern ensures the context window remains small and focused on reasoning, while the 'grunt work' of filtering is handled by the cheaper, faster MCP server. Ref: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools

stem: In an automated CI/CD environment, you want to ensure that Claude Code's session is completely isolated from any previous runs. What is the most reliable way to achieve this?

choices.text: Use the /clear command at the start of every script.
Instruct Claude to 'start fresh' in the system prompt.
Use the --no-history flag.
Run Claude Code inside an ephemeral Docker container for each job.

explanation: Isolation is the cornerstone of secure and deterministic CI/CD pipelines. When using AI agents that have the power to write files and execute shell commands, 'Session Pollution' is a significant risk. If an agent modifies a file in one job and that modification persists to the next, it can lead to 'Invisible Dependencies' and hard-to-debug failures. The standard architectural solution is 'Environment Ephemerality' using a fresh Docker container for every CI job. This ensures that every run starts from a 'Known Good' state, with no residual history, file changes, or credentials from previous executions. This is a core requirement for 'Reproducible AI Quality Gates.'.

stem: You are building a pipeline to extract data from thousands of messy HTML pages. You find that the presence of 'Navigation Bars' and 'Footers' confuses the extraction of the main article. What is the best fix?

choices.text: Use 'Claude 3.5 Haiku' as it is faster at reading noise.
Increase the context window to allow for more noise.
Use a pre-processing script to strip non-essential HTML tags before sending the text to Claude.
Tell Claude to 'Ignore the navigation bar' in the system prompt.

explanation: The 'Signal-to-Noise Ratio' (SNR) is the primary driver of extraction accuracy. Raw web data is filled with 'Contextual Noise' (ads, nav bars, footers) that consume tokens and dilute the model's attention. An expert architect implements a 'Pre-Filtering' layer (using tools like BeautifulSoup or Readability.js) to strip out non-semantic content *before* it reaches the LLM. This optimization reduces token costs, decreases latency, and significantly improves the 'Reasoning Fidelity' of the model by ensuring that 100% of the input context is high-signal information relevant to the extraction task. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching

stem: When building a tool for an agent to 'update_database_record', why is it recommended to return the updated record as the tool result?

choices.text: It ensures that the entire database is loaded into Claude's context.
It prevents 'tool selection ambiguity' in the next turn.
It is required by the MCP specification.
It allows the agent to verify that its requested changes were applied correctly without making an additional 'read' call.

explanation: High-fidelity tool design includes 'Feedback Loops.' In agentic systems, every action should be 'Self-Verifying.' By returning the updated record (or a status summary) as the result of a 'Write' operation, you allow the agent to immediately confirm that its intent was translated into reality. Without this feedback, the agent must either 'Assume Success' (which is risky) or make a follow-up 'Read' call (which increases cost and latency). This 'Informative Return' pattern ensures the agent can autonomously detect and correct errors, such as database validation failures or partial updates, leading to a significantly more robust and reliable system. Ref: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools

stem: A team wants to use Claude Code in CI to automatically generate a 'Security Review' for every PR. They are worried about the high token cost of reading the entire codebase for every change. What is the best optimization?

choices.text: Switch to Claude 3 Haiku for the review task.
Disable Prompt Caching to save on the 'Cache Write' costs.
Use the Message Batches API for the security review.
Only send the 'git diff' of the PR to Claude Code instead of the full file contents.

explanation: Optimizing the 'Context-to-Insight' ratio is the primary way to manage AI costs in CI/CD. For a Pull Request, the most high-signal information is the 'Delta' what has changed since the last version. By architecting your pipeline to only pass the 'git diff' (and perhaps a few layers of surrounding context), you reduce the token input by orders of magnitude compared to reading the entire repository. This 'Differential Context' approach allows you to use more capable (and expensive) models like Sonnet for every PR without exploding your operational budget. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching

stem: A pharmaceutical company is extracting dosage information from 5,000 legacy PDF protocols. Some PDFs are low-quality scans. Which combination of features ensures the highest data quality?

choices.text: Claude 3.5 Sonnet + Vision + Validation-Retry Loop.
Message Batches API + Standard Messages API.
Claude 3 Opus + 100 few-shot examples.
Claude 3.5 Haiku + Prompt Caching.

explanation: High-stakes extraction from 'Dirty Data' (low-quality scans) requires a 'Multi-Modal Defensive' architecture. Relying solely on text (OCR) is insufficient because OCR errors will be propagated into the model's context. By using 'Claude Vision,' the model can 'see' the raw pixels of the document, resolving ambiguities that text-based OCR might miss. Combining this with a 'Validation-Retry Loop' (where an external script checks the output for common dosage errors and asks for a correction) provides the highest possible precision. This tiered strategy ensures that even in the presence of technical noise, the 'Final Extracted Fact' remains accurate. Ref: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents

stem: In a long Claude Code session involving 100+ files, you notice the tool is becoming slow and 'forgetful' of the initial project brief. What is the most token-efficient way to restore performance?

choices.text: Switch to Claude 3 Opus.
Use the /clear command and then provide a concise summary of the current state and goals.
Restart the terminal.
Increase the 'max_tokens' setting to 400,000.

explanation: Peak performance in agentic sessions requires active 'Context Pruning.' As the session length increases, the 'Context Window' becomes crowded with previous attempts, tool results, and conversational noise, leading to 'Attention Dilution.' The /clear command is the primary tool for 'Resetting the Reasoning Engine.' By clearing the history, you remove the noise while keeping the session active. Providing a concise 'State Summary' immediately after clearing ensures the model has the high-level context it needs to continue without re-reading the entire project. This practice is essential for maintaining accuracy and reducing token costs during deep-dive refactoring or debugging tasks. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching

stem: You are extracting structured information from messy, unstructured medical records. Some fields, like 'middle_name', are often missing. How should you design your JSON schema to prevent the model from hallucinating values for these fields?

choices.text: Set 'nullable: true' for optional fields and instruct the model to return 'null' for missing data.
Use 'Claude 3 Opus' to ensure the model is smart enough to know when a field is missing.
Implement a 'Validation-Retry' loop that fails if any field is empty.
Make every field 'required' and instruct the model to use 'N/A' if unknown.

explanation: High-fidelity data extraction requires 'Schema Integrity.' When a model is forced to fill a 'Required' field that doesn't exist in the source text, it often 'hallucinates' a plausible but incorrect value. This is a major risk in fields like healthcare or finance. The architectural fix is to use 'Explicit Nullability.' By setting 'nullable: true' in the JSON schema and providing a clear 'Out' (e.g., 'If the middle name is not explicitly mentioned, return null'), you provide a structural signal that 'None' is a valid and correct answer. This pattern drastically reduces hallucination rates and improves the overall trustworthiness of the extracted dataset. Ref: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/overview

stem: To achieve a target of 80% first-contact resolution, a support agent must manage complex, multi-turn interactions without losing track of the user's original issue. Which architectural pattern is most effective for maintaining focus in long sessions?

choices.text: Increase the context window to 200,000 tokens for every turn.
Instruct the agent to 'be brief and resolve the issue quickly' in the system prompt.
Use the 'Write' tool to maintain a 'CASE_SUMMARY.md' scratchpad file that is read at the start of every turn.
Switch to 'Claude 3.5 Haiku' to minimize the cost of long-running sessions.

explanation: Effective state management is critical for agents performing complex, multi-turn resolutions. While Claude has a massive context window, relying solely on 'History Memory' can lead to attention dilution as the session grows, causing the agent to forget early details or duplicate diagnostic steps. The 'Scratchpad Pattern' involves giving the agent a tool to write to a persistent state file (like CASE_SUMMARY.md) which acts as its 'Short-Term Working Memory.' By reading this file at the start of every turn, the agent maintains a high-fidelity summary of the goals, facts gathered, and steps remaining. This reduces the cognitive load on the model and ensures the resolution stays on track regardless of session length. Ref: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents

stem: You are building a multi agent system where a Coordinator agent delegates billing disputes to a specialized Billing subagent. During testing, the subagent fails to resolve a dispute because it cannot see the customer's VIP status, even though the Coordinator mentioned it in the initial turn. What is the fundamental cause?

choices.text: The subagent's 'allowedTools' list did not include the 'get_customer_status' tool.
Subagents operate with isolated context and do not inherit the history or system prompt of the Coordinator.
The Coordinator's system prompt was too long, causing it to 'forget' the VIP status.
The Coordinator used the wrong JSON schema for the subagent's tool call.

explanation: The billing subagent does not inherit the coordinator transcript (subagents: fresh context). VIP status mentioned only in the parent turn is invisible unless the delegation message includes it. allowedTools, prompt length, and schema are not why a fact in the parent history is missing. Doc idea: Subagents, what loads at startup.

stem: You are configuring Claude Code for a large monorepo. You want to prevent Claude from ever reading or indexing the '.env.production' file for security reasons. Which file should you use?

choices.text: permissions.deny with a Read rule such as Read(./.env.production)
CLAUDE.md
.gitignore
package.json

explanation: Deny Read(./.env.production) in permissions. That blocks Read and also Edit/Write on the same path. .claudeignore is not a documented file. CLAUDE.md does not enforce. .gitignore changes what Grep skips by default; it does not stop Read of a known path. package.json does not hide files. Doc idea: Permissions, exclude sensitive files.

stem: You are integrating Claude Code into a CI/CD pipeline to provide automated code reviews on every Pull Request. Which flag should you use to ensure the tool focuses only on the changes within the current project context?

choices.text: The --no-history flag
The -p / --print flag, which runs Claude Code non-interactively. It does not by itself limit the review to the git diff.
The --cloudeignore flag
The --output-format json flag

explanation: -p is --print, non-interactive mode for CI (CLI reference). It is not --project and it does not limit the review to the git diff. --output-format json shapes the result; it does not select the diff. The other flags are not real. To review a diff, tell the prompt to look at the diff, or use the /code-review skill in an interactive session. Doc idea: CLI reference, --print.

stem: An engineer is using the 'Bash' tool to debug a performance issue. They want to ensure Claude doesn't accidentally kill critical production processes while running 'top' or 'kill' commands. What is the best safety measure?

choices.text: Implement a 'Pre ToolUse' hook that regex-checks the 'kill' command for specific process IDs.
Run Claude in a 'sandbox' environment that has no access to the production network.
Add 'BE CAREFUL' to the system prompt.
Ask the developer to approve every single Bash command manually.

explanation: A PreToolUse hook can match Bash and deny a kill command (exit code 2 or permissionDecision deny) before it runs (hooks; permissions). A sandbox without a production network is stronger isolation, but the question is about blocking specific kill text while the session can still debug. A prompt does not block. Manual approval of every command is the default prompt, not a targeted check. Doc idea: Hooks, PreToolUse on Bash.

stem: Scenario: When using Claude Code for a large scale refactoring task, you notice that the model's suggestions are becoming less accurate after 50 turns. You want to reset the context while still preserving the changes already made to the codebase. Question: Which command should you use?

choices.text: /compact
/exit followed by a restart.
/reset
/clear

explanation: /clear starts an empty context and leaves files on disk (sessions; commands). /compact keeps a summary, so it does not reset. /exit ends the process. There is no /reset; /reset is an alias of /clear in the commands table, so the command that matches the stem is /clear. Doc idea: Commands, /clear.

stem: A developer wants to share a specific 'Code Review' workflow with their entire team using Claude Code. What is the recommended way to distribute this configuration?

choices.text: Use the 'global_config' flag in the Claude Code CLI.
Add the instructions to the company's internal Wiki.
Check the '.claude/skills/' directory into the project's Git repository.
Email the instructions to every developer.

explanation: Commit .claude/skills/ so the team gets the skill (skills: share skills, project location). A wiki or an email is not loaded. There is no global_config flag that distributes a workflow. Doc idea: Skills, project skills.

stem: A support agent for an airline must handle flight changes. If a user becomes frustrated or uses abusive language, the agent should immediately hand over to a human supervisor. How can this 'Sentimental Escalation' be implemented most reliably?

choices.text: Implement an MCP tool named 'escalate_to_human' and a 'Post ToolUse' hook that analyzes the agent's output sentiment.
Increase the model's temperature to 0.9 to make it more 'empathetic'.
Instruct the agent to 'be polite' in the system prompt.
Tell the user to 'calm down' if they get angry.

explanation: Reliable human handover (Escalation) is a key requirement for enterprise support agents. A 'Dual-Trigger' escalation strategy is most effective. First, the agent is given an 'escalate_to_human' tool and instructed to use it if they detect user frustration. Second, a 'Safety/Sentiment Hook' runs on the model's output to detect abusive language or extreme sentiment, automatically triggering the escalation even if the model fails to do so. This architectural pattern ensures that high-friction situations are always moved to a human expert, protecting the brand's reputation and ensuring the customer receives the appropriate level of care. Ref: https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents
