explanation: "In Claude Code, custom slash commands have been merged into skills, and for personal and project skills the command a user types is determined by the skill directory name, not by anything in the frontmatter. A skill at .claude/skills/generate-api-docs/SKILL.md creates /generate-api-docs; the frontmatter name field is only a display label at these scopes. The one place frontmatter name can shape the invocation is plugin skills, where commands are namespaced by plugin and name can set the final command segment. This path-based convention keeps invocation predictable: the thing you type maps directly to a folder you can find in the repository.

stem: SCENARIO: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.In this system, the document analysis subagent has two custom MCP tools: extract_document_text (description: "Extracts text from a document URL") and get_document_metadata (description: "Returns title, author, and publication date for a document URL"). Quality reviews of final reports reveal fabricated publication dates and author names in citations. Trace logs show the analysis subagent almost always calls only extract_document_text and then fills in citation fields itself, rarely invoking get_document_metadata. What is the most direct fix for the root cause?

choices.text: Rename extract_document_text to extract_body_text_only so the tool name itself signals that citation metadata is not included in its results.
Add few-shot examples to the analysis subagent's system prompt demonstrating the correct sequence of calling both tools before reporting findings.
Expand extract_document_text's description to state it returns body text only and that get_document_metadata must be called for citation fields.
Add a post-processing validation step that rejects the subagent's findings and forces a retry whenever citation fields appear to be missing.

explanation: "Anthropic documents tool descriptions as the single most important factor in tool performance. A complete description covers what the tool does, when to use it and when not to, what each parameter means, and, critically here, caveats and limitations such as information the tool does not return. The description 'Extracts text from a document URL' is silent on the fact that no bibliographic metadata comes back, so the agent has no signal that its citation fields are missing rather than embedded in the text it received. Faced with a report schema demanding authors and dates, the model fills the gap the only way it can: by inventing values.

stem: SCENARIO: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow using custom slash commands and CLAUDE.md configuration, and to know when to use plan mode rather than direct execution.Yesterday, one of your developers ran a long Claude Code session that analyzed the codebase and identified 12 modules requiring updates as part of a planned refactoring. Overnight, teammates merged changes that substantially modified 8 of those 12 modules. Today the developer wants to continue the refactoring work with Claude Code. Which approach best preserves the value of yesterday's analysis while ensuring the agent works from accurate information?

choices.text: Resume yesterday's session by its session ID so the full analysis context is restored, and let the agent continue from where it stopped.
Start a fresh session and inject a structured summary of yesterday's findings, flagging the 8 changed modules for re-examination.
Fork yesterday's session into a new branch so the original analysis stays intact while today's refactoring work proceeds in the copy.
Resume yesterday's session and immediately run /compact so the older context is condensed before continuing the refactoring.

explanation: "A Claude Code session is the accumulated conversation history: prompts, tool calls, tool results, and responses. Resuming or forking a session restores that history exactly as recorded; it does not re-read the filesystem or refresh tool results. This is why the key architectural question before resuming is always: is the prior context still valid? If files the agent previously read have changed, every one of those cached reads is now misinformation sitting in context, and the model has no reliable way to know which parts are outdated.

stem: SCENARIO: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is a first-contact resolution rate of 80% or higher, with reliable escalation to a human when a case falls outside what the agent should handle.To improve consistency in how the agent handles return requests, your team pasted three complete example conversations (customer message, agent reasoning, tool call sequence, final response) as plain text into the system prompt, interleaved directly with the behavioral instructions. Return handling became more consistent, but the agent now occasionally references order numbers and customer names from the examples when talking to real customers, and it once called lookup_order with an order ID taken from an example. Which change would most effectively fix this problem while preserving the consistency benefits?

choices.text: Replace concrete details in the examples with placeholder tokens such as [ORDER_ID] and [CUSTOMER_NAME] so no example data can leak into real conversations.
Wrap each demonstration in tags inside an enclosing block, structurally separated from the instructions and the live conversation.
Remove the example conversations and expand the prose instructions to describe the desired resolution flow in greater detail.
Increase from three to ten example conversations so the correct pattern is reinforced strongly enough to override the confusion.

explanation: "The symptom in this case, an agent quoting order numbers from its own prompt examples and even passing an example order ID to lookup_order, is a classic sign of missing delimitation. When demonstrations, behavioral instructions, and live conversation data all sit in the same undifferentiated block of text, the model has no reliable signal for which content is illustrative and which is actionable. Anthropic's guidance is to wrap each demonstration in tags and group them inside an block, and more generally to use XML tags such as and in complex prompts so different content types are much less likely to be misinterpreted.

stem: SCENARIO: You are building developer productivity tools using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent helps engineers explore unfamiliar codebases, understand legacy systems, generate boilerplate code, and automate repetitive tasks. It uses the built-in tools (Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob) and integrates with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.Your team runs a weekly job that generates boilerplate documentation for the legacy codebase by submitting roughly 40,000 Messages requests (one per module, each with a unique custom_id) in a single Message Batches API batch. This week the batch's processing_status reached ended, but when the pipeline downloaded the results JSONL, several hundred entries had result type expired instead of succeeded, leaving those modules without documentation. How should you redesign the pipeline to handle this situation?

choices.text: Parse the per-request result types in the results file and resubmit only the expired requests in a follow-up batch, merging results across batches by custom_id.
Move the weekly documentation job to synchronous Messages API calls so that individual requests are no longer subject to batch expiration.
Keep polling the results endpoint after the batch ends, since expired requests continue processing and their results will appear within the 29-day availability window.
Resubmit the entire 40,000-request batch whenever any request expires, because results returned from separate batches cannot be reliably merged.

explanation: "The Message Batches API separates the batch-level status from per-request outcomes. A batch's processing_status moves from in_progress to ended once every request has reached a terminal state, but ended does not mean every request succeeded. Each line in the results JSONL carries its own result type: succeeded, errored, canceled, or expired. A request is marked expired when the batch hits its 24-hour processing limit before that request completes, and no further processing happens afterward; the 29-day window only controls how long results remain downloadable after batch creation.

stem: SCENARIO: You are building developer productivity tools using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent helps engineers explore unfamiliar codebases, understand legacy systems, generate boilerplate code, and automate repetitive tasks. It uses the built-in tools (Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob) and integrates with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.Your team wants the agent to never execute Bash commands that pipe environment variables to external network endpoints. An engineer wrote a hook callback that scans the command text for these patterns and registered it under the PostToolUse event with a Bash matcher. Monitoring confirms the hook correctly identifies offending commands, yet the network requests still go out. What change will ensure these commands never execute?

choices.text: Add explicit instructions to the agent's system prompt stating that commands sending environment variables to external endpoints are forbidden.
Keep the PostToolUse hook but change its return value to a blocking decision so the flagged command is rejected.
Keep the PostToolUse hook and use updatedToolOutput to strip the sensitive content from the tool result before Claude sees it.
Register the check as a PreToolUse hook matched on Bash and return a deny permissionDecision in hookSpecificOutput when the pattern matches.

explanation: The core issue is choosing the correct interception point in the hook lifecycle. PreToolUse runs after Claude has generated the tool parameters but before the tool call is processed, which makes it the enforcement primitive: a hook that returns a permissionDecision of "deny" inside hookSpecificOutput stops the call outright, and the permissionDecisionReason is fed back to Claude so it can adjust its approach. PostToolUse, by contrast, fires only after a tool has run successfully; it exists for after-the-fact work such as feedback, auditing, or rewriting what Claude sees via updatedToolOutput, but it cannot prevent side effects that have already happened. A command that exfiltrates environment variables completes its network request before any PostToolUse hook executes.

stem: SCENARIO: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.During validation of the system's output, you find that final reports contain plausible-looking citation URLs that do not match the pages the web search subagent actually retrieved. Trace logs show that at each handoff, the coordinator passes the downstream subagent a prose summary of the upstream findings, and these summaries contain no source URLs or document identifiers. What change would most effectively ensure the final reports cite the actual sources?

choices.text: Grant the report-generation subagent access to a web search tool so it can look up and attach a matching source URL for each claim before finalizing the report.
Reconfigure the pipeline so the web search subagent hands its results directly to the report subagent instead of routing them through the coordinator.
Strengthen the report subagent's system prompt with an explicit instruction to cite only sources that were actually consulted during the research phase.
Have subagents return findings in a structured format pairing each claim with its source metadata, which the coordinator includes in each delegation prompt.

explanation: "The root cause here is a combination of context isolation and lossy handoffs. In the Claude Agent SDK, each subagent runs in its own fresh conversation: the only information it receives from the parent is the prompt string in the Agent tool call, and the only thing it returns is its final message. When the coordinator condenses upstream findings into prose summaries, the source URLs are silently dropped, and by the time the report generator is asked to produce citations, the real provenance no longer exists anywhere in its context. A language model asked to cite sources it never saw will produce plausible-looking but fabricated references.

stem: SCENARIO: You are building developer productivity tools using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent helps engineers explore unfamiliar codebases, understand legacy systems, generate boilerplate code, and automate repetitive tasks. It uses the built-in tools (Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob) and integrates with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.Engineers ask the agent to map how order processing works across an unfamiliar 200-module monolith before generating integration boilerplate. During the mapping phase, Grep calls return hundreds of matches and Read calls pull full source files directly into the main conversation. Midway through the task, the context window is nearly exhausted, even though the agent only needs high-level findings (which modules participate, their dependencies, and key interfaces) to complete the boilerplate phase. Which change would most effectively preserve the main agent's context for the remainder of the task?

choices.text: Start a fresh session for each module being investigated, discarding the prior exploration context once that module has been fully documented.
Increase the frequency of conversation summarization so accumulated tool results are compressed into shorter form after every investigation step.
Enable prompt caching on the static system prompt and tool definitions so the repeated prefix consumes fewer resources on each API request.
Delegate each investigation question to a subagent that performs searches and file reads in its own context and returns only summarized findings.

explanation: Agentic exploration of large codebases has an inherent context problem: discovery tools like Grep and Read produce output whose volume is disproportionate to its lasting relevance. A Grep call returning hundreds of matches is useful for a few seconds of reasoning, but every one of those tokens then sits in the conversation for the rest of the session, crowding out the durable findings the agent actually needs.

stem: SCENARIO: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.The document analysis subagent extracts findings as JSON using structured outputs, with a schema containing claim, quoted_excerpt, source_url, and publication_date fields. A validation-retry loop resends any schema violations back to the model, but logs show schema validation has passed on every run for weeks. However, editors reviewing the final reports find that roughly 8% of quoted excerpts do not actually appear anywhere in the cited source document. Which change to the extraction pipeline most effectively addresses this quality issue?

choices.text: Add a programmatic check that each quoted_excerpt appears in the retrieved source text, and feed mismatches back to the model for correction.
Increase the maximum number of retries in the schema validation loop from two to five to give the model more chances to produce accurate excerpts.
Convert the extraction to a tool definition with strict: true so the schema is enforced by the API rather than by post-hoc validation code.
Have the subagent output a self-reported confidence score for each finding and automatically discard findings that fall below a fixed threshold.

explanation: This scenario illustrates a fundamental boundary of structured outputs: they solve the syntactic problem, not the semantic one. Whether you use JSON outputs via output_config.format or strict tool use via strict: true, the guarantee is that the response conforms to your JSON Schema. Neither mechanism can verify that a quoted_excerpt value actually exists in the source document, that a date is accurate, or that a claim is supported by the citation. A finding with a fabricated quote is perfectly valid JSON.

stem: SCENARIO: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is a first-contact resolution rate of 80% or higher, with reliable escalation to a human when a case falls outside what the agent should handle.Load testing reveals that the backend order service intermittently returns 503 errors. The current lookup_order MCP tool implementation catches these exceptions and returns an empty order array as a normal successful result, so the agent tells customers with valid orders that no orders were found and denies legitimate refund requests. Which change to the tool's error handling best fixes this reliability issue?

choices.text: Return failures as structured tool error results flagged as errors, including the failure type and the attempted lookup parameters so the agent can retry, try an alternative, or escalate.
Have the tool wrapper block and repeatedly retry the backend call until it succeeds, so the agent never observes a failed lookup.
Keep returning an empty array on failure, but add a system prompt instruction telling the agent to treat empty order results as a possible backend outage and double-check before responding.
Catch the exception in the tool wrapper and immediately invoke escalate_to_human whenever lookup_order fails, ending the agent's attempt at resolution.

explanation: "The core principle here is that errors must propagate as errors, never as fabricated success. When a tool swallows a backend exception and returns an empty result, it destroys the one piece of information the agent needs to behave correctly: whether the data is genuinely absent or simply unavailable right now. From the model's perspective, an empty order array is a legitimate finding, so it confidently tells the customer no orders exist. No amount of prompting can recover a signal that was erased at the tool boundary.

stem: SCENARIO: You are building developer productivity tools using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent helps engineers explore unfamiliar codebases, understand legacy systems, generate boilerplate code, and automate repetitive tasks. It uses the built-in tools (Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob) and integrates with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.An engineer on this team is about to have Claude Code explore an unfamiliar legacy billing subsystem to understand its structure before any changes are made. The session is currently in accept edits mode, and permission bypass is not enabled. The engineer wants the permission system itself to prevent source file edits while Claude reads code and runs investigation commands, but plans to have Claude implement changes later in the same session. What is the most reliable approach?

choices.text: Switch the session into dontAsk mode so that tool calls that would otherwise require an approval prompt are automatically denied during the exploration.
Switch the session into plan mode with Shift+Tab for the exploration, then move to an execution mode once ready to implement.
Remain in accept edits mode and include a chat instruction telling Claude not to modify any files during the exploration.
Add a rule to the project CLAUDE.md stating that Claude must never edit files while exploring unfamiliar code.

explanation: Permission modes are how Claude Code decides what Claude may do without asking; they are changed through the UI, CLI flags, or settings, and can be switched mid-session, but not by merely asking Claude in chat. This is the critical mental model: a chat instruction or a CLAUDE.md rule shapes what Claude tends to do, while a permission mode determines what the tool layer allows it to do. When the requirement is enforcement ('no source files change during this phase'), the permission system is the right layer, keeping in mind that plan mode's blocks apply only when permission bypass is not enabled, as in this scenario.

stem: SCENARIO: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow using custom slash commands and CLAUDE.md configuration, and to know when to use plan mode rather than direct execution.A senior developer on the team just finished a lengthy Claude Code session that thoroughly explored a legacy billing module, mapping its dependencies and identifying constraints for an upcoming refactoring; the session ID was captured. The team now wants to prototype two competing refactoring strategies, each building on that same completed analysis and each implemented in its own separate git worktree, and compare the results side by side without either attempt's reasoning or conversation history influencing the other. Which session management approach best supports this comparison?

choices.text: Fork the completed analysis session twice, giving each refactoring strategy its own independent branch that starts from a copy of the shared exploration history.
Resume the original session for the first strategy, then use file checkpointing to restore the session transcript to the analysis baseline before attempting the second.
Start two completely fresh sessions and have each one re-explore the legacy module independently before implementing its assigned strategy.
Resume the original session by its session ID and evaluate both strategies sequentially, instructing Claude to disregard the first approach before starting the second.

explanation: "The Claude Agent SDK and Claude Code persist a session as the accumulated conversation history: the prompt, every tool call, every tool result, and every response. Because this transcript is written to disk automatically, a completed run becomes a reusable asset. Three distinct operations act on it: continue picks up the most recent session in the current directory, resume reopens a specific session by ID and keeps appending to it, and fork creates a brand-new session seeded with a copy of the original history while leaving the original untouched.

stem: SCENARIO: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow using custom slash commands and CLAUDE.md configuration, and to know when to use plan mode rather than direct execution.An engineer on this team starts a Claude Code session that opens in plan mode because the project's settings set "permissions": {"defaultMode": "plan"}. A failing unit test has already pinpointed the problem: a missing null check in one function of a single file, and the fix is obvious and well understood. The engineer wants to resolve this quickly while keeping sensible safeguards. What is the most appropriate workflow?

choices.text: Stay in plan mode, have Claude produce a written remediation plan for the null check, and approve the plan before any edit occurs.
Keep the current mode and tell Claude in the chat prompt to disregard plan mode restrictions and edit the file immediately.
Press Shift+Tab to switch to a direct execution mode such as acceptEdits, let Claude make the change, and review the diff afterward.
Switch the session to bypassPermissions so Claude can complete the fix without any permission checks slowing it down.

explanation: "Claude Code's plan mode is one of several permission modes, not a separate product feature: it lets Claude research, read files, and propose an approach while blocking source edits until you approve a plan. Its value is proportional to task uncertainty. When a change has architectural implications, competing valid approaches, or touches many files, the plan-review checkpoint catches bad directions before code hits disk. When the diagnosis is already complete and the fix is a well-scoped, single-file change, that checkpoint is pure overhead; the diff itself is the natural review artifact.

stem: SCENARIO: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow using custom slash commands and CLAUDE.md configuration, and to know when to use plan mode rather than direct execution.Your team's automated refactoring audit script calls the Messages API with JSON outputs (output_config.format) to classify each refactoring candidate. The schema includes a severity field constrained by a string enum: "Critical", "Warning", "Suggestion". A validation-retry loop resends the document with the validation error whenever the output fails schema checks. Reviewing the logs, you find that the large majority of retries are triggered because Claude returned "critical" or "warning" in lowercase, and retries frequently return the same lowercase value, causing repeated round trips and wasted tokens. What change most effectively improves this validation-retry loop?

choices.text: Replace JSON outputs with an assistant prefill that starts the response with an opening brace so the JSON output format is fully controlled.
Move the classification into a tool definition configured with strict: true so the enum values are guaranteed to match the schema's exact casing.
Compare enum values case-insensitively in validation code and normalize casing before downstream use, reserving retries for other schema violations.
Add few-shot examples demonstrating the exact enum capitalization and raise the retry limit so the loop eventually converges on correct casing.

explanation: "A well-designed validation-retry loop distinguishes failures the model can meaningfully fix from mismatches your code should absorb. Anthropic explicitly documents that structured outputs do not guarantee exact capitalization of string enum or const values, and recommends comparing enum values case-insensitively and avoiding enum values that differ only by capitalization. In other words, a lowercase 'critical' is not an extraction quality problem; it is expected variance that deterministic normalization handles instantly, without another model round trip.

stem: SCENARIO: You are building developer productivity tools using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent helps engineers explore unfamiliar codebases, understand legacy systems, generate boilerplate code, and automate repetitive tasks. It uses the built-in tools (Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob) and integrates with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.Your agent answers engineers' questions about a legacy payments service by combining Grep and Read results from the code with design documents retrieved through an internal wiki MCP server. An engineer recently discovered that the agent's answer about the service's retry policy described behavior from a wiki page written before a major refactor and contradicted the current code; the answer presented a single blended description with no indication of which statements came from the code and which came from the wiki. What change most effectively prevents this class of error?

choices.text: Instruct the agent to always defer to the wiki documentation when it conflicts with retrieved code, since the wiki captures the intended design of the system.
Have the agent append a self-reported confidence score to each answer so engineers know which responses need manual verification against the current codebase.
Add a second synthesis pass that rewrites the answer to smooth out inconsistencies between the code findings and the wiki content before presenting it to the engineer.
Require each claim to carry a source attribution (file path, or wiki page and last-updated date), and annotate points where code and wiki disagree instead of merging them.

explanation: When an agent synthesizes answers from multiple sources with different reliability and freshness (live code versus dated design documents), the essential safeguard is a claim-source mapping: a structured association between each claim and where it came from, preserved all the way through synthesis. Once findings are compressed into blended prose, attribution is gone and the reader has no way to distinguish a statement grounded in the current code from one lifted from a two-year-old wiki page. Attaching temporal metadata (a page's last-updated date) is equally important, because it prevents a stale-but-plausible description from being misread as current behavior; a discrepancy between an old document and new code is often not a contradiction to resolve but a signal that the documentation has drifted.

stem: SCENARIO: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is a first-contact resolution rate of 80% or higher, with reliable escalation to a human when a case falls outside what the agent should handle.The team is designing how the agent handles standard return-refund requests. Six months of transcripts show these requests follow an identical sequence every time: verify the customer, look up the order, check return eligibility against the published policy, then either process the refund or escalate. Each step depends on the output of the previous step. Which task decomposition strategy best fits this workflow?

choices.text: Spawn parallel subagents that run customer verification, order lookup, and eligibility checking simultaneously to minimize end-to-end latency.
Use dynamic adaptive decomposition so the agent generates its own subtasks at runtime based on what it discovers in each individual conversation.
Structure the workflow as a fixed sequential pipeline where each step consumes the previous step's output and follows the documented sequence.
Begin each request with an interview phase where the agent asks clarifying questions to determine which steps apply before proceeding.

explanation: "The core decision in task decomposition is whether the steps of a workflow are predetermined or must be discovered. When transcript analysis shows a request type follows an identical, well-understood sequence, a fixed sequential pipeline (prompt chaining) is the right structure: each step consumes the previous step's output, the flow is easy to audit, and failures can be localized to a specific stage. Dynamic adaptive decomposition, where the agent invents subtasks based on what it finds, earns its complexity only when the path genuinely cannot be known in advance, such as open-ended investigations; applying it to a routine refund flow trades away determinism for flexibility the task does not need.

stem: SCENARIO: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.The team maintains this research system's codebase with Claude Code and has built a project skill, /trace-run, that reads through a completed research run's agent transcripts and tool logs to diagnose why a report came out incomplete. The skill works, but each invocation dumps thousands of lines of transcript excerpts into the main conversation, and developers notice Claude's follow-up work in the same session degrades afterward. Which change best fixes this while keeping the skill's diagnostic capability?

choices.text: Move the diagnostic procedure out of the skill and into the project CLAUDE.md so it is available in every session without invocation overhead.
Add context: fork to the SKILL.md frontmatter so the skill executes in an isolated subagent and returns only its conclusions to the main session.
Add allowed-tools frontmatter to the skill so it can only use read-only tools while diagnosing runs.
Instruct developers to run /compact immediately after each /trace-run invocation to summarize the accumulated output.

explanation: "Skills in Claude Code load their full content only when invoked, but by default they execute inside the main conversation, so everything a skill reads and reasons over becomes part of the session's context. For workflows that are inherently verbose, such as combing through agent transcripts and tool logs, this fills the context window with exploratory material that degrades everything Claude does afterward. The context: fork frontmatter option changes the execution model: the skill runs in an isolated subagent with its own context, does its noisy work there, and hands back only its conclusions. The mental model is the same as delegating research to the Explore subagent: keep discovery-heavy work in a disposable context and preserve the main session for decisions.

stem: SCENARIO: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow using custom slash commands and CLAUDE.md configuration, and to know when to use plan mode rather than direct execution.During a codebase-wide refactor to standardize error handling, Claude Code encountered several legacy patterns that your CLAUDE.md conventions do not address. It silently picked a different approach in each case, and developers later discovered inconsistent patterns mixed throughout the changed files. You want Claude Code to reliably stop and ask the developer when it hits a situation the team's conventions do not cover, while still proceeding autonomously on cases the conventions clearly address. Which approach best achieves this?

choices.text: Add criteria to CLAUDE.md directing Claude to pause and ask whenever it hits a pattern the conventions do not cover, with examples of when to ask versus proceed.
Require plan mode for every Claude Code task so the developer approves a proposed plan before any change is executed, regardless of the task's scope or complexity.
Instruct Claude to output a self-assessed confidence score for each change and ask the developer only when its confidence falls below a defined threshold.
Let Claude apply its best judgment during the refactor and list any ambiguous decisions in a summary at the end for the developer to review afterward.

explanation: "The core design question here is ambiguity resolution: how does an agent know when to act autonomously versus when to pause for human input? The reliable answer is explicit escalation criteria with concrete examples, not indirect signals. A rule like 'if the team conventions do not cover the pattern you are looking at, stop and ask before changing it' gives the model a testable condition it can evaluate against CLAUDE.md, and two or three ask-versus-proceed examples anchor that rule far better than prose alone, because examples communicate the boundary unambiguously.

stem: SCENARIO: You are building developer productivity tools using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent helps engineers explore unfamiliar codebases, understand legacy systems, generate boilerplate code, and automate repetitive tasks. It uses the built-in tools (Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob) and integrates with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.Your team configures the agent to automate a repetitive task: regenerating API client boilerplate whenever backend contracts change. Team policy requires the project's test suite to pass before the agent finishes any code-modification task. Despite a system prompt instruction stating this requirement, session logs show that in about 10% of runs the agent edits files and then ends its turn without ever running the tests. Which change most reliably enforces the policy?

choices.text: Rewrite the system prompt with stronger mandatory language and few-shot examples showing the agent running tests before finishing.
Add a PreToolUse hook on the Edit and Write tools that denies file modifications until the test suite has passed.
Add a PostToolUse hook on the Edit and Write tools that runs the test suite after each modification and logs any failures.
Add a Stop hook that runs the test suite and blocks turn completion with feedback whenever tests have not passed.

explanation: "The core architectural distinction here is between probabilistic guidance (system prompts, few-shot examples) and deterministic enforcement (hooks). The failure already occurred with an instruction in place, so the fix must be a mechanism the agent cannot simply ignore. Hooks are code that runs at fixed points in the agent loop, and each hook event guards a different point: PreToolUse gates individual tool calls before they run, PostToolUse fires after a tool has already executed, and Stop fires when the agent wants to end its turn.

stem: SCENARIO: You are building developer productivity tools using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent helps engineers explore unfamiliar codebases, understand legacy systems, generate boilerplate code, and automate repetitive tasks. It uses the built-in tools (Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob) and integrates with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.Your agent inventories components in a large legacy monorepo by calling a catalog_component tool defined with strict tool use (top-level "strict": true), so tool inputs are constrained to conform to the schema. The tool's input_schema constrains the framework field with an enum limited to react, angular, vue, and svelte. When the agent runs against a newly acquired codebase, engineers notice that hundreds of components built with an in-house UI framework are being cataloged as react, silently corrupting the inventory that downstream tooling depends on. Which schema change best resolves this misclassification while keeping the catalog machine-readable?

choices.text: Replace the enum with a free-form string field so the model can write any framework name it observes.
Make the framework field optional so the model can omit it when a component does not match a listed framework.
Add few-shot examples to the prompt demonstrating correct classification of react, angular, vue, and svelte components.
Add an "other" value to the framework enum along with a detail string field where the model records the actual framework name.

explanation: "This failure is a predictable consequence of how schema-constrained output works. Because the tool is defined with strict tool use ('strict': true), sampling is constrained so the tool input conforms to the input_schema; when that schema uses an enum, the model must emit one of the listed values to produce a valid tool call, with no legal way to say 'none of these.' Faced with an in-house framework, the model does not refuse, it picks the closest plausible value, which is why the misclassification is silent. Schema enforcement guarantees structural validity, but it cannot make an incomplete category set complete; a syntactically perfect payload can still be semantically wrong.

stem: SCENARIO: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow using custom slash commands and CLAUDE.md configuration, and to know when to use plan mode rather than direct execution.This team installed the Claude GitHub App and added the anthropics/claude-code-action@v1 workflow with a pull_request trigger so Claude can review generated and refactored code. In practice, Claude only reviews a pull request after a teammate comments @claude on it; newly opened PRs get no review until someone remembers to mention Claude. The team wants Claude to run on every newly opened pull request with no comment required. What change should they make to the workflow?

choices.text: Grant pull-requests: write and issues: write permissions to the workflow so Claude can respond without being mentioned.
Add the pull request authors to allowed_non_write_users so their PRs trigger Claude automatically when opened.
Provide a prompt input to the claude-code-action step so it runs in automation mode as soon as the pull_request event fires.
Set the trigger_phrase input to an empty string so the action stops waiting for a mention before starting.

explanation: "The anthropics/claude-code-action@v1 integration has two documented run modes, and the switch between them is a single input. When no prompt is provided, the action runs in interactive mode: it starts on the configured events but then waits for the trigger phrase (@claude by default) in a comment or mention, and replies as an issue or PR comment. When a prompt input is provided, the action runs in automation mode: Claude executes immediately for the triggering workflow event (such as a pull request opening) and writes its results to the workflow run log rather than waiting for a human. The behavior this team observed, a workflow that fires on pull_request but does nothing until someone comments, is the signature of interactive mode with no prompt configured.

stem: SCENARIO: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow using custom slash commands and CLAUDE.md configuration, and to know when to use plan mode rather than direct execution.This team shares an internal code-search MCP server through a project-level .mcp.json checked into the repository. The team recently updated that entry to point at a new startup command that exposes additional tools. Every developer picked up the change after pulling, except one engineer who, months ago, had registered a server with the same name using claude mcp add with the default local scope, pointing at the old command. Their sessions still show only the old tools even after pulling the updated .mcp.json. What should this engineer do to get the updated server?

choices.text: Run claude mcp reset-project-choices so Claude Code re-prompts for approval of the project-scoped server.
Re-register the updated server with user scope so the new configuration applies across all of the engineer's projects.
Add the new startup command fields to the local entry's missing sections so Claude Code merges them with the project definition.
Remove the local-scoped server definition so the project-level entry in .mcp.json takes effect.

explanation: "Claude Code resolves MCP servers through a strict scope precedence order: local (the default for claude mcp add, private to the current project), then project (the shared .mcp.json checked into version control), then user (cross-project personal config), followed by plugin-provided servers and connectors. When two scopes define a server with the same name, Claude Code picks the single highest-precedence complete entry; it never merges fields between entries. This design keeps resolution deterministic: a developer's deliberate local override always wins over team config, which is useful when intentionally testing a modified server, but it becomes a silent trap when a forgotten local entry shadows an updated shared one.

stem: SCENARIO: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow using custom slash commands and CLAUDE.md configuration, and to know when to use plan mode rather than direct execution.This team is building an internal command-line automation that drives Claude Code's agentic loop to perform repetitive refactoring tasks across dozens of repositories. The automation must be written in Go to integrate with the team's existing internal libraries, and the team wants to reuse Claude Code's built-in tools, permission handling, and agent loop rather than rebuilding them. What is the most appropriate way to implement this?

choices.text: Rewrite the automation in TypeScript using the @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk package so it can invoke the query function directly.
Call the Messages API directly from Go and implement the tool-use loop yourself, re-creating the file and shell tools the automation needs.
Launch Claude Code in its interactive terminal interface from the Go tool and programmatically send keystrokes, parsing the rendered screen output for results.
Run the Claude Code CLI as a subprocess from the Go tool using the -p flag with --output-format json, and parse the structured result from stdout.

explanation: "The Claude Agent SDK is distributed as libraries for Python and TypeScript only. For any other language, Anthropic's documented pattern is to drive the same agent loop by running the Claude Code CLI as a subprocess: the -p flag (alias –print) runs Claude Code non-interactively, reading a prompt and writing the result to stdout so it composes like any other shell tool, and –output-format json makes that result machine-parseable, including the final text, session ID, and usage details. A Go program (or any language with subprocess support) gets the complete agentic loop, including the built-in Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob, and Bash tools and the permission system, without reimplementing anything.

stem: SCENARIO: You are building developer productivity tools using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent helps engineers explore unfamiliar codebases, understand legacy systems, generate boilerplate code, and automate repetitive tasks. It uses the built-in tools (Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob) and integrates with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.This team runs nightly automation jobs in their CI pipeline using claude -p to apply repetitive codebase updates without human supervision. Most runs finish within a handful of agentic turns, but occasionally Claude enters an extended exploration loop and the job consumes far more tokens and runtime than budgeted. The team wants runaway runs to fail deterministically once a bounded number of agentic iterations is exceeded, while leaving normal runs unaffected. What should they do?

choices.text: Configure a wall-clock timeout on the CI job so the runner terminates the Claude Code process after a fixed duration.
Have the pipeline prompt invoke /compact partway through the run to compress accumulated context so tasks complete in fewer turns.
Pass the --max-turns argument with an appropriate cap to the claude -p invocation so the run exits with an error when the limit is reached.
Add an instruction to the pipeline prompt directing Claude to complete the task within a fixed number of tool calls and stop if it exceeds that budget.

explanation: "Non-interactive pipeline runs use print mode (claude -p or –print): prompt in, result out, exit. Because nobody is watching these runs, any safety limit must be deterministic, enforced by the tooling rather than requested of the model. The –max-turns argument is that mechanism: it caps the number of agentic turns in print mode, has no default limit (so unattended jobs are unbounded unless you set it), and causes the run to exit with an error when the cap is hit. That error exit is exactly what a CI job needs to fail fast and alert the team, while runs that complete under the cap proceed normally.

stem: SCENARIO: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is a first-contact resolution rate of 80% or higher, with reliable escalation to a human when a case falls outside what the agent should handle.Production traces show that when the payment gateway behind process_refund returns a transient network error, the agent retries the identical process_refund call eight to ten times in a row, consuming tokens until the session's cost ceiling terminates it. The customer ends the conversation with neither a completed refund nor an escalation to a human. Which change most effectively improves the system's error handling and recovery?

choices.text: Catch gateway failures inside the tool and return a refund-initiated success status, queuing the failed transaction for a nightly retry job outside the agent's workflow.
Configure the application layer to end the agent session on the first process_refund error and transfer the conversation immediately to the general human support queue.
Return the gateway failure in the tool_result with is_error set to true and the failure type and retryability, enforcing a retry cap that routes to escalate_to_human.
Add a system prompt instruction that the agent must never repeat a failed process_refund call with identical parameters and should try a different approach instead.

explanation: "This failure is a classic stuck loop: the agent observes a failure but has no structured signal telling it whether retrying is worthwhile and no enforced boundary that stops repetition. Two mechanisms fix it together. First, the tool should surface the failure honestly in a tool_result with is_error: true, carrying structured context such as the failure type and retryability; this gives the model something to reason about rather than an opaque outcome it keeps re-attempting. Second, the application layer should enforce a retry cap, because loop termination with financial consequences is a deterministic requirement that should not depend on probabilistic model compliance. When the cap is reached, routing to escalate_to_human is the correct graceful degradation: the customer still gets resolution, just through a different channel.

stem: SCENARIO: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is a first-contact resolution rate of 80% or higher, with reliable escalation to a human when a case falls outside what the agent should handle.This team documented critical refund-handling policies (refunds over $500 must always route through escalate_to_human, and the agent must never auto-approve disputed charges) in a CLAUDE.md file located at src/tools/CLAUDE.md, next to the MCP tool wrapper code. Engineers launch Claude Code from the repository root, and inspecting loaded context with /context shows the policy file enters context only after Claude reads files under src/tools/. In sessions focused on prompt templates or escalation-flow design elsewhere in the repo, the policies never enter context, and Claude has proposed changes that conflict with them. The team wants these policies present in every session for every teammate. What should they do?

choices.text: Move the refund-policy instructions into the project-root CLAUDE.md that is committed to version control.
Standardize the team on launching Claude Code from src/tools/ so the nested file is on the walk-up path.
Add YAML frontmatter with a paths field of ["**/*"] to src/tools/CLAUDE.md so it activates for every file.
Move the instructions into a CLAUDE.local.md at the project root so they load when each session starts.

explanation: "Claude Code loads CLAUDE.md files by walking up the directory tree from the current working directory, concatenating everything it discovers into context at launch. Files below the working directory behave differently: they are discovered but included only when Claude actually reads files in those subdirectories. This lazy loading is a deliberate context-budget tradeoff; it keeps area-specific conventions from consuming tokens in sessions that never touch that area. The mental model to hold is that placement encodes scope: root-level content is always-on project guidance, while nested content is conditional guidance tied to that part of the tree.

stem: SCENARIO: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow using custom slash commands and CLAUDE.md configuration, and to know when to use plan mode rather than direct execution.Your team created a custom /doc-check slash command that instructs Claude Code to "review all comments and docstrings in the changed files and flag any that are inaccurate." Developers complain that it flags docstrings that merely omit minor implementation details or use informal phrasing, and several have stopped running the command, so genuinely wrong docstrings now slip through unreviewed. Which change to the command's prompt would most effectively reduce these false positives?

choices.text: Add an instruction telling Claude to be conservative and report only inaccuracies it is highly confident are genuine documentation errors.
Enable extended thinking in the command so Claude deliberates more thoroughly about each comment before deciding whether to flag it.
Have the command output a confidence score with each finding and filter out findings below a fixed threshold client-side.
Rewrite the instruction to flag a docstring only when the behavior it describes contradicts what the code actually does.

explanation: "The root cause here is a vague success criterion. An instruction like 'flag any comments that are inaccurate' forces the model to invent its own definition of inaccuracy on every invocation, and that definition naturally drifts to include informal phrasing and omitted details. Anthropic's prompting guidance emphasizes that Claude responds best to clear, explicit instructions with well-defined task boundaries, and that current models follow restrictive criteria literally rather than inferring your intent, so the prompt itself must encode the decision boundary. Rewriting the criterion as 'flag only when the documented behavior contradicts the actual code behavior' converts a subjective judgment into a testable check, which is the highest-leverage fix for false positives.

stem: SCENARIO: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.Your team defines the four specialized subagents programmatically through the agents parameter in the TypeScript SDK's query() options, each with a clear description and system prompt. The coordinator runs unattended with permissionMode set to "dontAsk" and allowedTools set to ["Read", "Grep", "Glob", "WebSearch"]. In every run, the coordinator performs all searching and analysis itself in the main conversation and never spawns any subagent, even when the prompt explicitly says "use the web-searcher agent for this step." What change would most effectively enable delegation to the subagents?

choices.text: Move the subagent definitions out of the agents parameter and into .claude/agents/ Markdown files so they are discoverable.
Set the background field to false on each AgentDefinition so the subagents run synchronously in the main session.
Strengthen each subagent's description field with phrases like "use proactively" to encourage automatic delegation.
Add the Agent tool to the coordinator's allowedTools so subagent spawn requests are pre-approved.

explanation: "In the Claude Agent SDK, a coordinator delegates work by calling the Agent tool (previously named Task), which spawns a subagent instance with its own fresh context. Defining subagents through the agents parameter registers them and lets Claude match tasks to their descriptions, but registration alone does not grant the coordinator permission to spawn them: the Agent tool call itself must pass the permission system like any other tool call. The SDK documentation specifically recommends including Agent in allowedTools so subagent invocations auto-approve without a permission prompt.

stem: SCENARIO: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is a first-contact resolution rate of 80% or higher, with reliable escalation to a human when a case falls outside what the agent should handle.You add a triage subagent to the system that classifies each incoming request (return, billing dispute, or account issue) before the coordinator routes it. Its AgentDefinition specifies a description and a system prompt, but no tools field. During a production audit, you discover the triage subagent directly called process_refund while classifying a billing dispute, issuing a refund before any eligibility checks ran. What change most reliably prevents the triage subagent from executing refunds?

choices.text: Add an explicit instruction to the triage subagent's system prompt stating that it must never call process_refund.
Remove the Agent tool from the coordinator's allowedTools so that every subagent invocation requires approval before it runs.
Specify a tools list in the triage subagent's AgentDefinition limited to get_customer and lookup_order.
Rewrite the triage subagent's description field to state that it is a read-only classifier and should not perform account actions.

explanation: "In the Claude Agent SDK, each subagent's capabilities are defined by its AgentDefinition. The description and prompt fields are required, but tools is optional, and the default is permissive: when tools is omitted, the subagent inherits every tool available to subagents. That is why a classification-only subagent can end up holding process_refund even though nothing in its prompt suggests it should process payments.

stem: SCENARIO: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.Your multi-agent research system's document-analysis subagent depends on a document-processing MCP server that exposes 14 tools for parsing PDFs, spreadsheets, and slide decks. Every engineer who clones the repository must get this server's configuration automatically, and you must guarantee that the other subagents in the system cannot call its tools. How should you configure this?

choices.text: Add the server at project scope so its configuration is written to .mcp.json in the repository, and exclude the document-processing tools from the other subagents' tools allowlists.
Add the server at user scope in ~/.claude.json so it loads across all projects, and exclude the document-processing tools from the other subagents' tools allowlists.
Add the server at project scope so its configuration is written to .mcp.json, and instruct the other subagents in their system prompts to never invoke the document-processing tools.
Add the server at local scope on each engineer's machine, and exclude the document-processing tools from the other subagents' tools allowlists.

explanation: "Claude Code supports three MCP installation scopes, and choosing among them is a distribution decision. Local scope (the default) is private to the current project on one machine; user scope stores personal, cross-project configuration in ~/.claude.json; and project scope writes shared configuration to .mcp.json, which is designed to be checked into version control so the whole team inherits the server the moment they clone or pull. When the requirement is that every engineer gets a server automatically through the repository, project scope is the only mechanism that delivers it; the other two scopes exist precisely so that personal and experimental servers stay off teammates' machines.

stem: SCENARIO: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.During testing, the synthesis subagent's output frequently references vague "industry reports" and invents citations instead of citing the specific sources the other agents actually found. The web search and document analysis subagents both completed successfully and returned detailed, source-attributed findings to the coordinator. The coordinator's logs show it invoked the synthesis subagent with the delegation prompt: "Synthesize the findings from the earlier research on this topic into key themes." What change most reliably fixes this handoff failure?

choices.text: Increase the synthesis subagent's turn limit so it has more iterations to gather the missing findings and sources before producing its final output.
Modify the coordinator to embed the full search and analysis findings, with source URLs and document names, in the synthesis subagent's delegation prompt.
Update the synthesis subagent's system prompt with an instruction to review the coordinator's conversation history and cite only sources found there.
Add the Task tool to the synthesis subagent's allowed tools so it can query the completed search subagent for the source-attributed findings it produced.

explanation: The defining property of subagents in the Claude Agent SDK is context isolation: each subagent runs in its own fresh conversation window with no access to the parent's history, prior tool results, or other subagents' outputs. The only channel from coordinator to subagent is the delegation prompt itself. When a coordinator writes a vague handoff like 'synthesize the findings from the earlier research,' the synthesis agent literally has no findings to work with, so the model does what language models do under missing information: it produces plausible-sounding but ungrounded content, including fabricated citations.

stem: SCENARIO: You are building developer productivity tools using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent helps engineers explore unfamiliar codebases, understand legacy systems, generate boilerplate code, and automate repetitive tasks. It uses the built-in tools (Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob) and integrates with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.The agent is helping engineers migrate a legacy monorepo off a deprecated internal logging package. As its first step, it must produce a list of every TypeScript file that contains an import of that package, without pulling unrelated file contents into its context window. Which built-in tool usage should the agent apply for this discovery step?

choices.text: Call Grep with a pattern for the deprecated import, scoped to TypeScript files via its glob parameter, to return matching file paths.
Call Read on the repository root directory so the agent can scan the tree and identify files that reference the deprecated package.
Call Glob with a pattern for all TypeScript files, then Read each returned file to check whether it contains the deprecated import.
Call Bash to run a recursive shell grep across the repository tree and parse its raw text output for the matching file paths.

explanation: "The core distinction being tested is what each built-in search tool actually looks at. Grep searches the contents of files, while Glob matches files by their names and paths. Finding files that contain a specific import statement is a content search, so Grep is the right tool; a useful mental model is that Glob answers 'which files exist matching this name pattern?' while Grep answers 'which files contain this text?'

stem: SCENARIO: You are building developer productivity tools using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent helps engineers explore unfamiliar codebases, understand legacy systems, generate boilerplate code, and automate repetitive tasks. It uses the built-in tools (Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob) and integrates with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.Your team's nightly boilerplate-generation job submits about 10,000 requests in a single Message Batches API batch at midnight, and a downstream step commits the generated code. Having the code ready before engineers arrive in the morning is a convenience, not a hard deadline: the commit can land later in the day without blocking any engineering work. The pipeline has started intermittently marking the job as failed: its orchestrator polls the batch for 60 minutes and aborts if processing_status is still in_progress, based on the documented note that most batches finish in under 1 hour. When engineers investigate later in the morning, the aborted batches have almost always completed successfully on their own. What is the best way to redesign the pipeline?

choices.text: Split the nightly job into several smaller batches submitted in parallel so that each one is guaranteed to finish within the 60-minute polling window.
Poll processing_status until the batch reaches ended, budgeting for the documented 24-hour processing window, and trigger the commit step on completion.
Resubmit all 10,000 requests in a duplicate batch whenever the 60-minute poll window elapses, and use results from whichever batch reaches ended first.
Cancel the batch at the 60-minute mark and reprocess the outstanding requests through the synchronous Messages API to speed up delivery.

explanation: The core mental model for the Message Batches API is that it trades latency guarantees for cost: usage is charged at 50% of standard API prices precisely because Anthropic schedules the work asynchronously. The documentation notes that most batches finish in under 1 hour, but that is an observation about typical behavior, not an SLA. The only hard boundary is that a batch expires if processing does not complete within 24 hours, and results remain retrievable for 29 days after batch creation. A well-designed consumer therefore polls processing_status until it reaches ended and treats completion as an event, not a scheduled time.

stem: SCENARIO: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.This team's repository already contains an AGENTS.md file at the root holding citation standards and research-quality conventions that a different AI coding tool on the team reads. As the team adopts Claude Code for developing the coordinator and subagents, they want those same conventions loaded into every Claude Code session, plus additional Claude-specific guidance about coordinator delegation patterns that the other tool must not pick up. Claude Code sessions currently do not load AGENTS.md at all. What is the most maintainable configuration?

choices.text: Create a root CLAUDE.md that references the file as @AGENTS.md inside backticks so Claude knows to read it when relevant.
Replace CLAUDE.md with a symlink pointing at AGENTS.md and append the Claude-specific delegation guidance to AGENTS.md.
Create a root CLAUDE.md that imports AGENTS.md using @AGENTS.md syntax and add the delegation guidance in that CLAUDE.md.
Copy the contents of AGENTS.md into a new root CLAUDE.md and keep both files updated in parallel as conventions evolve.

explanation: "Claude Code loads its persistent instructions from CLAUDE.md, not from AGENTS.md, so a repository that standardized on AGENTS.md for another tool gets no automatic pickup. The documented bridge is the @path import syntax: a line like @AGENTS.md in CLAUDE.md is expanded at launch, pulling the referenced file's content into context. Relative import paths resolve relative to the file containing the import, and imports can chain recursively up to a few hops, which is what makes modular, single-source-of-truth configuration practical.

stem: SCENARIO: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow using custom slash commands and CLAUDE.md configuration, and to know when to use plan mode rather than direct execution.Your team's repository includes a custom MCP server in .mcp.json that exposes a search_standards tool for querying the internal engineering wiki during code generation sessions. Developers report that when a query legitimately matches no wiki pages, Claude Code repeatedly retries the search with rephrased queries and eventually concludes the wiki service is down. Inspecting the server code, you find the tool returns a result with isError: true and the message "No matching documents found" whenever the result set is empty. What change to the tool's response handling would best resolve this behavior?

choices.text: Return a normal successful tool result stating that zero documents matched, and reserve isError: true for genuine failures like timeouts.
Add an instruction to the project CLAUDE.md telling Claude that "No matching documents found" errors from search_standards should not be retried.
Convert empty result sets into JSON-RPC protocol error responses so the client-side machinery handles them instead of the model.
Keep isError: true for empty result sets but add structured metadata marking the error as non-retryable so the agent stops rephrasing queries.

explanation: "The core distinction being tested here is between an access failure and a valid empty result. A search that executes correctly and finds nothing is a successful operation; the tool did exactly what was asked. Marking it with isError: true tells the agent that something went wrong, and a well-behaved agent responds to tool errors by attempting recovery: retrying, rephrasing inputs, or eventually concluding the backing service is unavailable. That is precisely the wasted-retry loop the team is observing.

stem: SCENARIO: You are building developer productivity tools using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent helps engineers explore unfamiliar codebases, understand legacy systems, generate boilerplate code, and automate repetitive tasks. It uses the built-in tools (Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob) and integrates with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.Your team's monorepo contains auto-generated API client code under src/generated/ that a codegen pipeline overwrites on every build; hand edits there are always lost and can break builds. To protect it, a teammate created .claude/rules/generated-code.md with YAML frontmatter setting paths to ["src/generated/**"] and content stating that these files must never be modified and that changes belong in the schema source instead. Despite this, session logs show the agent still occasionally edits files in src/generated/ while generating boilerplate. What is the most reliable way to prevent these edits?

choices.text: Add a PreToolUse hook that blocks any write-capable tool call, including Bash commands, targeting paths under src/generated/.
Move the rule's content into the project root CLAUDE.md so the instruction is loaded unconditionally in every session.
Duplicate the instruction into a second rule file with the same glob so the prohibition appears twice when matching files are in play.
Broaden the rule's paths glob to a pattern like **/* so the prohibition is present regardless of which files Claude is working with.

explanation: Files in .claude/rules/ with a paths frontmatter field give Claude Code conditional context loading: the rule content is pulled in when Claude works with files matching the glob, keeping unrelated sessions lean. That mechanism is working correctly here; the misunderstanding is about what rules can guarantee. Rules and CLAUDE.md content are guidance that Claude follows probabilistically, not a control plane that constrains tool execution. When a violation is merely undesirable, guidance is usually sufficient; when a violation is unacceptable (edits that are always destroyed by codegen and can break builds), the architecture needs an enforcement layer.

stem: SCENARIO: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.The final report-generation step is implemented as a direct Messages API call that receives the synthesized findings and is given a single generate_report tool whose input_schema matches the format your downstream publishing pipeline ingests. In roughly 10% of runs, the model returns the report as markdown prose in a text block instead of calling generate_report, and the pipeline fails to parse it. Which configuration change most reliably eliminates these failures?

choices.text: Keep tool_choice as "auto" and add a post-processing service that detects prose responses and re-parses them into the report schema.
Add emphatic system prompt instructions stating that the response must always be a generate_report tool call, never prose.
Mark every field in the generate_report input_schema as required so the model cannot respond without invoking the tool.
Set tool_choice to {"type": "tool", "name": "generate_report"} on the report-generation request.

explanation: The tool_choice parameter is the API-level mechanism for controlling whether Claude may, must, or must not call a tool. Its values are auto (Claude decides, the default when tools are supplied), any (Claude must call some tool), tool (Claude must call one named tool), and none (no tool use). When a request supplies exactly one extraction or output schema and the response must always come through that tool, forcing it with {"type": "tool", "name": …} is the right lever: the API prefills the assistant message to force tool use, so the response reliably contains a tool_use block for the named tool rather than free-form prose.

stem: SCENARIO: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.During a research run, the coordinator decomposes a topic into five independent web search subtopics. Trace logs show the coordinator invokes the web search subagent for the first subtopic, waits for its result, then issues the next invocation in a subsequent turn, repeating until all five complete. End-to-end research time is roughly five times the duration of a single search. What change would most effectively reduce this latency?

choices.text: Raise the CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS environment variable so more search subagents are allowed to run at once.
Migrate the searchers to an agent team so they can message each other directly instead of routing through the coordinator.
Have the coordinator emit all five Agent tool calls in a single response so the independent search subagents execute concurrently.
Combine all five subtopics into a single delegation prompt so one web search subagent handles the entire research pass.

explanation: In a coordinator-subagent architecture, latency for independent subtasks is determined by how the coordinator dispatches work, not by how fast any single subagent runs. The Claude Agent SDK supports parallel subagent execution: when the coordinator emits multiple Agent tool calls in a single assistant response, the runtime executes those subagents concurrently, each in its own isolated context. Independent subtasks then finish in roughly the time of the slowest one instead of the sum of all of them. The sequential pattern in the logs, one spawn per turn with a wait in between, is a dispatch behavior the coordinator can be designed or prompted out of whenever the subtasks have no dependencies on each other's results.

stem: SCENARIO: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.Analysts submit research requests to the system, and a review of unsatisfactory reports shows a consistent pattern: when a request is genuinely ambiguous (for example, "research the merger's impact" when the topic area includes several recent mergers), the coordinator silently picks one interpretation and runs the full subagent pipeline, producing a well-cited report on the wrong question. You want the coordinator to pause and ask the requesting analyst for clarification on genuinely ambiguous requests while still proceeding autonomously on clear ones. Which design most effectively achieves this?

choices.text: Have the coordinator enumerate every plausible interpretation of ambiguous requests, run the full subagent pipeline for each in parallel, and deliver all resulting reports to the analyst.
Require the coordinator to begin every research request with a round of clarifying questions to the analyst before decomposing the topic into subagent tasks.
Have the coordinator output a self-reported confidence score for its chosen interpretation of each request and route the request back to the analyst whenever the score falls below a tuned threshold.

Define explicit criteria in the coordinator's prompt for what makes a request ambiguous, with few-shot examples contrasting requests it should clarify with the analyst versus requests it should decompose and run.

explanation: "The failure here is a classic ambiguity resolution problem: the coordinator commits to one plausible interpretation instead of recognizing that the request itself is underspecified.
