It can make the response conform to the requested structure, while application code still needs to inspect completion state and validate domain facts such as whether cited files and line ranges actually exist.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.A new developer says Claude Code is not applying the repository's TypeScript and testing conventions. The senior engineer can reproduce the conventions on their own machine, but the new developer cannot, and the team is unsure whether the relevant instruction files are actually visible in the new developer's session. What should you do first to diagnose the configuration hierarchy issue?

choices.text: Copy the senior engineer's user-level CLAUDE.md into the new developer's home directory.
Run /status in the new developer's session and inspect the Setting sources line.
Place the team conventions in .claude/settings.local.json on the new developer's machine.
Run /memory in the new developer's session and inspect the loaded instruction files.

explanation: "When Claude Code appears to ignore project guidance, first distinguish memory files from settings files. The /memory command is designed for this diagnostic path because it shows which CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md files are loaded in the current session. If an expected file is absent from that list, Claude cannot see those instructions in that session.

stem: You are building developer productivity tools using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent helps engineers explore unfamiliar codebases, understand legacy systems, generate boilerplate code, and automate repetitive tasks. It uses the built-in tools (Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob) and integrates with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.During a manual orchestration test, Claude returns stop_reason tool_use with two tool requests, one for reading a file and one for searching related symbols. The application executes both operations, but the following Claude response does not incorporate the retrieved file contents or search matches. Which change should this team make to the loop?

choices.text: Append the assistant message with the tool requests, then append one user message containing both matching tool results before the next request.
Append a new assistant message summarizing both tool outputs, then request the next turn without the original tool requests.
Append a user text note describing both outputs, then place the tool result blocks after that note in the same message.
Append two separate user messages, each containing one tool result, then request the next turn after both messages are added.

explanation: "For client tools, Claude does not execute the operation itself. Claude emits structured tool_use blocks, your application runs the requested tools, and the next request must carry the results back as tool_result blocks so Claude can continue reasoning from the new information.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.Your /architectural-scan command asks Claude Code to investigate frontend state management, database access patterns, and test coverage before proposing a refactor. Logs show the main thread waits for the frontend subagent summary before launching the database subagent, then waits again before launching the test subagent, even though the three investigations are independent. What change best reduces this tool-call serialization without changing the analysis scope?

choices.text: Keep one Agent call per assistant turn, wait for each subagent's final result, and mark each subagent as background before launching it.
Return each subagent summary in a separate user message immediately after completion, and let the main thread continue once all summaries have arrived.
Set tool_choice.disable_parallel_tool_use to true, and ask the main thread to prioritize the shortest investigation before launching the others.
Have the main thread issue the independent Agent calls in one assistant turn, then return all matching tool_result blocks together in the next user message.

explanation: "Parallel subagent spawning is an application of parallel tool use: Claude can return several tool_use blocks in a single assistant turn with stop_reason: "tool_use". The API does not require a particular execution order, so the client or orchestrator can run independent calls concurrently and then provide the observations back to Claude.

stem: You are building a structured data extraction system using Claude. The system extracts information from unstructured documents, validates the output using JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) schemas, and maintains high accuracy. It must handle edge cases gracefully and integrate with downstream systems.The research team splits long documents across extraction subagents. In validation, the synthesizer combines several extracted statistics into a single trend, and reviewers later find that two values reflected different collection periods and measurement methods. Logs show each extraction subagent returned a concise prose summary of relevant findings. What change most directly improves synthesis reliability?

choices.text: Send the complete extracted text from every document to the synthesizer for independent provenance reconstruction.
Validate that each extraction subagent returns JSON before the synthesizer processes its summary.
Run each extraction subagent as a fork so it inherits the parent conversation before returning its summary.
Require each subagent to return structured evidence records with the claim, source location, document date, and method context.

explanation: "When extraction work is delegated to subagents, the main workflow should treat each subagent result as a handoff artifact, not as a complete replayable investigation. The Claude Code subagents documentation explains that subagents work in their own context and return a summary to the main conversation, so downstream synthesis can only use the information that summary preserves.https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/sub-agents

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.During a long debugging session, the final report sometimes loses citations that were present in earlier web-search and document-analysis outputs. The team wants Claude Code to investigate specific questions such as where citations are stored, where synthesis rewrites occur, and which tests cover report generation, while keeping the main conversation focused on coordination rather than raw search logs and file contents. What workflow best supports this goal?

choices.text: Run independent Claude Code sessions for each investigation, then paste full transcripts into the main conversation.
Assign a general-purpose subagent to modify the report code while it searches for citation-loss causes.
Delegate focused read-only investigations to subagents, then use their returned summaries in the main conversation.
Ask the main conversation to inspect every relevant file directly, then compact the conversation after each phase.

explanation: "For long codebase investigations, the useful pattern is to keep the main conversation responsible for coordination and delegate narrow discovery tasks to subagents. Claude Code subagents run side work in their own context window and return a result or summary, which helps avoid flooding the main context with file contents, search results, and command output.

stem: You are building a structured data extraction system using Claude. The system extracts information from unstructured documents, validates the output using JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) schemas, and maintains high accuracy. It must handle edge cases gracefully and integrate with downstream systems.The latest evaluation run reports 97.4% overall extraction accuracy across the validation set, and stakeholders want to reduce human review based on that result. What should this team do before changing the review policy?

choices.text: Expand the validation set and keep the same single overall accuracy threshold for release.
Switch every extraction check to exact-match grading and approve the aggregate result.
Rerun the prompt comparison in the Console and deploy the higher average score.
Segment the evaluation by document type and extracted field before changing review thresholds.

explanation: A strong overall accuracy number is useful, but it is not enough for production decisions when failures have uneven impact. Anthropic's evaluation guidance emphasizes specific and measurable success criteria, and notes that many use cases require multidimensional evaluation rather than a single aggregate score, see Define success criteria.https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/test-and-evaluate/define-success

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.This team uses Claude Code while maintaining the repository for the system described above. They want citation and source-handling conventions to be shared by every developer, report-generator guidance to apply only when working in the report agent's directory, and personal editor preferences to remain private. Which configuration approach best matches Claude Code's memory hierarchy?

choices.text: Put all conventions in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, add report-agent notes under .claude/settings.json, and ask each developer to copy the same files locally.
Put shared conventions in CLAUDE.local.md, put report-agent guidance in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, and commit the user-level file for the team.
Put shared conventions in the report agent's CLAUDE.md, put personal preferences in root CLAUDE.md, and rely on subdirectory files to override parent files.
Put shared conventions in root CLAUDE.md or .claude/CLAUDE.md, put report-agent guidance in that directory's CLAUDE.md, and keep personal preferences in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md.

explanation: Claude Code memory is best understood as layered context, not as a permissions system. Team-wide repository guidance belongs in project instructions such as CLAUDE.md at the repository root or .claude/CLAUDE.md, while personal preferences belong in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md.

stem: You are building a structured data extraction system using Claude. The system extracts information from unstructured documents, validates the output using JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) schemas, and maintains high accuracy. It must handle edge cases gracefully and integrate with downstream systems.This team is using Claude Code to update the extraction repository. Which task is the best fit for plan mode before implementation rather than asking Claude to make the change directly in default mode?

choices.text: Have Claude open the known schema file, correct a misspelled field label, and apply the obvious one-line edit.
Have Claude explore the existing invoice extraction flow, then propose a migration plan for changing how ambiguous totals are represented.
Have Claude inspect the already identified validation function, add one logging statement after failures, and save the narrow edit.
Have Claude review the small extractor helper, rename one local variable to the chosen name, and update immediate references.

explanation: "Plan mode is useful when you want Claude Code to explore the repository, reason about alternatives, and produce a proposal before implementation. In this case, changing how ambiguous invoice totals are represented could affect parsing logic, schemas, fixtures, validation behavior, and downstream adapters, so reviewing the plan before edits reduces the chance of an accidental partial migration.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.Your /review command uses detailed review criteria and a fixed output template. It still behaves inconsistently on unfamiliar refactors: sometimes it flags harmless local conventions as defects, and other times it misses real defects that differ from the examples in the checklist. What prompt change is the best next step?

choices.text: Add a larger checklist that enumerates every pattern seen so far, with instructions to report only exact matches.
Add several examples drawn from one recent refactor, with instructions to copy their wording and severity labels.
Add a CLAUDE.md rule that states the reviewer should be conservative, with no examples to avoid bias.
Add diverse few-shot examples that show issue and non-issue reviews, with brief reasoning that marks the decision boundary.

explanation: Few-shot or multishot prompting is useful when instructions alone do not reliably capture judgment. A few carefully selected examples can steer Claude's output format, tone, and structure while improving accuracy and consistency, but the examples should demonstrate the underlying decision rule rather than act as a lookup table.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.During a large refactor, this team wants Claude Code to run a database-migration reviewer, API compatibility reviewer, and test-coverage reviewer in parallel. The team also wants one place to resolve conflicting findings and decide which follow-up work to run. Which orchestration design best matches Claude Code's subagent model?

choices.text: Have the main agent spawn the reviewers with Agent, pass each reviewer its needed context, collect summarized results, and synthesize follow-ups centrally.
Start each reviewer as an isolated subagent, rely on inherited main-thread history, and merge findings without a separate routing step.
Omit Agent from the main agent tools, predefine reviewer prompts in CLAUDE.md, and let Claude choose reviewers implicitly.
Let the reviewer subagents message each other directly, maintain a shared task list, and send the final plan after peer coordination.

explanation: "Claude Code subagents implement a hub and spoke pattern: the main agent manages decomposition, delegates work, receives summarized results, and decides what to do next. A subagent is a specialized assistant inside a Claude Code session with its own context window, system prompt, tool access, and permissions, so the main agent must provide the context needed for that delegated task.

stem: You are building a structured data extraction system using Claude. The system extracts information from unstructured documents, validates the output using JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) schemas, and maintains high accuracy. It must handle edge cases gracefully and integrate with downstream systems.Validation logs show the JSON is syntactically valid, but the review queue is flooded with invoice anomaly flags. Many flags involve harmless formatting differences, while some arithmetic mismatches are missed. The current instruction says, "Find any questionable totals and flag them for review." What prompt change would most directly improve consistency?

choices.text: Require Claude to explain every suspected total anomaly before writing the final JSON output.
Add a stronger instruction to be conservative and flag only high-confidence total anomalies for reviewers.
Replace the vague flagging instruction with measurable rules for when parsed line items conflict with stated totals.
Raise the temperature so Claude considers more possible interpretations of each invoice layout.

explanation: "For extraction systems, a syntactically valid JSON object is not enough. The model also needs explicit decision criteria for fields that involve judgment, such as whether a document should be flagged for review.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.This team wants to run nightly pull request reviews through the Message Batches API. Each review may require an application-hosted client tool, run_repo_checks, that executes local linters and unit tests before Claude writes final feedback. Which design best handles this workflow?

choices.text: Submit the review prompts as batch items, replace run_repo_checks with web_search, and rely on server-tool execution to validate the local repository.
Submit the review prompts as batch items, set tool_choice to run_repo_checks, and rely on the batch worker to run the client tool before returning final feedback.
Submit one batch item containing the prompt, a predicted tool_result block, and the final review instructions so Claude can complete the loop in one request.
Submit the review prompts as batch items, retrieve any tool_use results by custom_id, run the requested client tools, and send follow-up requests with tool_result blocks.

explanation: "The key distinction is between client tools and server tools. A client tool is executed by the developer's application: Claude returns stop_reason: "tool_use" with tool_use blocks, then the application runs the tool and sends a later user message containing matching tool_result blocks. That lifecycle is described in Handle tool calls.https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/handle-tool-calls

stem: You are building a structured data extraction system using Claude. The system extracts information from unstructured documents, validates the output using JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) schemas, and maintains high accuracy. It must handle edge cases gracefully and integrate with downstream systems.The extraction coordinator has specialized agents for table parsing, clause extraction, and schema repair, but its SDK configuration only auto-approves file inspection tools. It keeps performing all extraction work itself instead of delegating focused subtasks. What change should this team make?

choices.text: Force tool_choice to the JSON schema extraction tool for each document.
Add each subagent name directly to the coordinator's allowedTools configuration.
Add Agent to the coordinator's allowedTools or allowed_tools configuration.
Set permissionMode to dontAsk while leaving the coordinator tools unchanged.

explanation: "In current Claude Code and Claude Agent SDK documentation, the tool used to spawn a subagent is Agent. The documentation notes that Task was renamed to Agent, with older references still supported as aliases, but new configurations should use the current tool name.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.A payments platform engineering team is running a multi-hour refactor investigation. Claude Code correctly identifies several legacy payment-flow dependencies early on. After many file reads, searches, and a compaction step, later answers start omitting those dependencies and referring to typical patterns instead of the specific findings. Which change would best preserve the investigation state for subsequent questions?

choices.text: Move the refactor into plan mode and rely on the plan to preserve prior file-analysis details.
Add a longer session-start instruction telling Claude to remember every payment dependency it identifies.
Keep all Grep and Read outputs in the active chat and avoid writing durable investigation notes.
Have the investigation agent maintain a concise investigation-notes.md file of confirmed dependencies and read it before follow-up questions.

explanation: Long Claude Code sessions are vulnerable to context degradation: many turns and verbose tool outputs can make earlier findings less available to the model. A concise investigation notes file works as a practical scratchpad, preserving confirmed architecture facts, dependencies, decisions, and open questions in a form Claude can explicitly reread before continuing.

stem: You are building developer productivity tools using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent helps engineers explore unfamiliar codebases, understand legacy systems, generate boilerplate code, and automate repetitive tasks. It uses the built-in tools (Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob) and integrates with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.Evaluations show two recurring issues: report generation stalls on minor evidence questions, while prior attempts to broaden the synthesis role caused it to duplicate exploration work. What change best improves this design?

choices.text: Give the synthesis subagent a narrow verify_fact tool and route broader investigation requests through the coordinator.
Merge synthesis and exploration into one subagent with a single prompt and shared tool permissions.
Give the synthesis subagent the same Read, Grep, Glob, and Bash access used by the exploration subagent.
Remove all tool access from the synthesis subagent and require coordinator approval for every evidence check.

explanation: "For subagent-based systems, the goal is not to give every role every tool it might conceivably need. A better pattern is scoped cross-role capability: provide a constrained tool for high-frequency, low-risk needs, while preserving the coordinator as the path for complex or open-ended work.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.After adding two MCP servers, Claude Code often calls a documentation search tool when developers ask about symbols in the repository, and calls a repository search tool when developers ask about framework policy pages. The tool names are distinct, and both tools support search-like queries. What should the team change first to improve tool selection reliability?

choices.text: Rename each tool with longer names that encode the target data source, while leaving the existing descriptions unchanged.
Add a project slash command that asks developers to choose the correct search tool before Claude Code begins each task.
Rewrite each tool description to define use cases, non-use cases, input formats, example queries, returned data, and edge cases.
Add a CLAUDE.md instruction that tells Claude Code to avoid documentation tools unless repository search fails first.

explanation: When multiple tools have overlapping names or capabilities, the most reliable first improvement is to make their tool descriptions explicit. Claude uses tool metadata to decide not only what a tool does, but also when it is appropriate, what arguments it expects, and what result it will receive.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports. During evaluation, the final reports are well written but sometimes include unsupported claims and miss contradictions between sections. The current design asks the report generator to review its own draft before publishing. What architecture change would most effectively improve review reliability?

choices.text: Delegate verification to listed subagents without passing source excerpts, relying on shared session context to expose prior findings.
Have the synthesis agent merge all subagent outputs once, then instruct it to mark unsupported claims before publishing.
Ask the report generator to perform an extended self-review immediately after drafting, using its existing conversation history.
Run independent reviewer agents on section-specific claim-source bundles, then run a separate integration pass for conflicts and coverage gaps.

explanation: For high-stakes synthesis, a stronger pattern is to separate generation from review. The report generator's self-review can catch obvious formatting problems, but it is less likely to challenge the assumptions embedded in its own draft. Independent reviewer agents provide a fresh context, and multi-pass review keeps each pass focused: first verify local claim-source alignment, then check cross-section consistency and coverage.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.During an evaluation run, the coordinator's first Messages API response contains a brief text block plus two Task tool_use blocks, and the run history shows no subsequent tool_result messages before report generation. The report is consistently based only on the coordinator's initial text. What change should you make to the coordinator loop?

choices.text: Send each subagent output as a separate tool role message, then continue only if the coordinator asks in prose.
Run each requested Task tool call, send matching tool_result blocks, and keep calling the Messages API until stop_reason is end_turn.
Forward the coordinator's text block to synthesis, skip Task execution, and end the turn when any assistant text is present.
Limit the coordinator to three iterations, summarize partial findings, and stop whenever the iteration cap is reached.

explanation: In a client-executed tool loop, stop_reason is the control signal. A response with stop_reason: "tool_use" means Claude has emitted one or more structured tool_use blocks and expects the application to execute those requested tools, then return matching tool_result blocks. It is not a final-answer state, even if the assistant response also includes a short text block.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.Your team's Claude Code skill/custom command, invoked as /task, is meant to decide whether to investigate, plan, or modify code. In evals, ambiguous requests such as "clean this up," "look into this error," and "can you improve this module?" produce inconsistent behavior. Detailed written criteria have not stabilized the boundary. What should you change next?

choices.text: Add 2-4 tagged examples showing similar ambiguous requests, the selected response path, and concise reasoning against plausible alternatives.
Add a stronger instruction that direct file edits must be avoided whenever the developer's request could imply planning.
Add a large collection of untagged past transcripts so Claude can infer the team's preferred behavior from volume.
Add a longer checklist that enumerates every phrase that should trigger investigation, planning, or code modification.

explanation: When a prompt fails on ambiguous decision boundaries, targeted examples usually outperform more abstract instruction text. The useful pattern is not merely showing the final answer, but showing why one action was chosen over another plausible action, such as planning instead of editing, or investigating instead of proposing a refactor.

stem: You are integrating Claude Code into your Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline. The system runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, and provides feedback on pull requests. You need to design prompts that provide actionable feedback and minimize false positives.After several weeks, developers say the automated reviewer is noisy. Examples show comments about variable names, preferred assertion styles, and missing tests mixed with a few real null dereferences and authorization bypasses. The current prompt says, "Report only issues you are highly confident about." What prompt change would most directly improve review usefulness?

choices.text: Define testable report and skip rules that focus comments on production bugs, security flaws, broken edge cases, and subtle regressions.
Expand the checklist to include naming, formatting, test coverage, and architecture preferences so comments feel more comprehensive.
Move every automated finding into a single nonblocking summary comment so developers can scan the noise separately.
Keep the broad review scope and require each inline comment to include a numerical confidence score and short rationale.

explanation: The failure mode is not that the reviewer lacks confidence metadata, it is that the prompt has not drawn a clear boundary between actionable correctness findings and low-value preference comments. "High confidence" is still subjective: a model can be confident that a variable name differs from a local style, even when that comment is not useful for a pull request review.

stem: You are integrating Claude Code into your Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline. The system runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, and provides feedback on pull requests. You need to design prompts that provide actionable feedback and minimize false positives.Your CI review job needs a project-scoped HTTP MCP server for pull-request metadata. The server requires a bearer token in the Authorization header, and the MCP configuration should be shared with every checkout while avoiding committed credentials. Which implementation best satisfies this requirement?

choices.text: Commit a .mcp.json file that references Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN in headers, and rely on Claude Code to expand it during connection.
Store the MCP server only in ~/.claude.json with the Authorization token, and document the manual setup for every contributor.
Commit a .mcp.json file that references Bearer ${GITHUB_TOKEN} in headers, and set GITHUB_TOKEN in each CI and developer environment.
Commit a .mcp.json file that includes the bearer token directly in headers, and limit repository access to approved maintainers.

explanation: For team-shared MCP servers in Claude Code, .mcp.json at the project root is the project-scope configuration file intended to be checked into version control. The secure pattern is to commit the non-secret server shape, then reference machine-specific or sensitive values through environment variable expansion rather than storing the values themselves.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.While maintaining the system described above, this team keeps citation validation tests beside the agent code they exercise, including files under packages/search/, packages/synthesis/, and apps/reporting/. The team wants Claude Code to apply the same testing conventions whenever editing these test files, without loading those conventions for unrelated production files. What should the team do?

choices.text: Create separate CLAUDE.md files in each package directory that repeat the same testing conventions for local files.
Add the testing conventions to the root CLAUDE.md so Claude Code always loads them for the repository.
Add the testing conventions to each developer's user-level CLAUDE.md so Claude Code loads them during edits.
Create a Markdown rule file under .claude/rules/ with YAML frontmatter using paths glob patterns for the test file names.

explanation: For conventions that should follow a file type rather than a directory, Claude Code path-specific rules are the right fit. A Markdown file in .claude/rules/ can include YAML frontmatter with the exact paths field, for example patterns that match test files wherever they live in the repository.

stem: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.During pilot testing, the refund recommendation step now always produces parseable structured data with required fields present and numeric types correct. The remaining bad cases involve merchandise credits placed in the shipping_refund field or itemized adjustments that do not match the requested refund total. What change should this team make next?

choices.text: Make every refund field required in the schema and reject nullable values during extraction.
Add downstream business-rule validation before refund execution and feed specific failures back for correction.
Rely on strict tool inputs to guarantee the refund recommendation is operationally correct.
Switch to plain JSON instructions and remove tool schemas from the extraction step.

explanation: Schema-based structured output is best understood as controlling shape, not automatically proving meaning. Anthropic documents structured outputs as mechanisms for valid JSON matching a schema, and strict tool use as a way to constrain tool names and tool inputs using JSON Schema and grammar-constrained sampling.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.A custom /parallel-review command starts an SDK run in a repository pinned to a pre-v2.1.63 Claude Code configuration where subagent delegation is performed with Task. It should fan out across specialized review subagents. The current SDK options auto-approve only Read, Grep, and Glob, and each run pauses at the first attempted subagent delegation with an interactive permission prompt. What should the team change?

choices.text: Add Task to the coordinator SDK run's allowedTools or allowed_tools list.
Remove delegation tools from allowedTools and rely on permission prompts.
Add Agent only to worker subagents' tools lists for nested calls.
Add Task delegation guidance to CLAUDE.md for the project repository.

explanation: For the legacy configuration described in the stem, subagent delegation is performed through Task, so the coordinator SDK run needs that delegation tool in allowedTools or allowed_tools. The practical issue is not that the subagents are undefined, it is that the first delegation attempt is not auto-approved and therefore falls into interactive permission handling.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.During evaluation, final reports cite sources but sometimes treat a peer-reviewed study, a vendor benchmark, and an internal survey as equivalent evidence for the same claim. The search and document-analysis subagents currently return concise finding summaries plus a general list of sources consulted. What change best supports accurate downstream synthesis?

choices.text: Add a report-generation pass that expands the final narrative with a separate bibliography and citation appendix.
Require each subagent to return structured claim records with source location, publication date, evidence excerpt, and methodology notes.
Ask the coordinator to retain full subagent transcripts and have the synthesizer infer provenance from prior work.
Give each subagent broader tool access so it can inspect all available sources before summarizing its findings.

explanation: In a multi-agent research system, provenance is an interface contract. A subagent may perform a rich investigation, but downstream agents can only depend on the information that is explicitly returned in its summary or handoff. If the returned output says only that a source supports a finding, the synthesizer may lose the distinction between evidence types, time periods, source locations, and methods.

stem: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.This team wants to move non-urgent post-resolution quality checks to the Message Batches API. Cases arrive continuously, and each check must reach a terminal batch outcome within 30 hours of case arrival for audit triage. Assume a batch may take the full documented 24-hour processing window before results are available or the batch expires. Which submission cadence should the team use?

choices.text: Submit accumulated requests every 4 hours, using custom_id to correlate each case outcome.
Submit accumulated requests every 8 hours, using custom_id to correlate each case outcome.
Submit accumulated requests once daily, using custom_id to correlate each case outcome.
Submit accumulated requests every 12 hours, using custom_id to correlate each case outcome.

explanation: The useful mental model for the Message Batches API is that it is an asynchronous processing mechanism for large volumes of Messages API requests, not a low-latency path for urgent work. For SLA planning, separate the time an item waits before submission from the time Anthropic may spend processing the batch.

stem: You are integrating Claude Code into your Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline. The system runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, and provides feedback on pull requests. You need to design prompts that provide actionable feedback and minimize false positives.The repository's main instruction file has grown to more than 400 lines and mixes review tone, test conventions, API design rules, and deployment checklist guidance. CI runs show that Claude Code is applying deployment guidance to routine unit test reviews and sometimes missing the test-specific criteria developers care about. What change should this team make to reduce irrelevant context while keeping shared review standards available?

choices.text: Split the large instruction file into imported Markdown files and reference each one from the root CLAUDE.md with @path imports.
Move all topic guidance into .claude/rules/ files without paths frontmatter and rely on the directory to lazy-load them.
Move topic-specific guidance into Markdown files under .claude/rules/ and add paths frontmatter for rules that apply only to matching files.
Create separate CLAUDE.md files in every package directory and duplicate the relevant test, API, and deployment guidance there.

explanation: For large Claude Code instruction sets, .claude/rules/ is the right mechanism for modular, topic-specific project guidance. Each rule is a Markdown file, such as testing.md or api-design.md, and rules can include YAML paths frontmatter so they apply only when Claude works with files matching glob patterns.

stem: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.A customer support resolution agent's production logs show that process_refund sometimes returns a successful-looking tool result with content "Refund blocked by policy" when an order is outside the refund window. Claude then retries the same refund call with slightly different wording instead of explaining the policy outcome or escalating when appropriate. What change would best improve the agent's recovery behavior?

choices.text: Return a CallToolResult with isError: true and place custom errorCategory, isRetryable, and policy text in structuredContent.
Update the process_refund description to warn Claude not to request refunds outside the configured refund window.
Raise a JSON-RPC protocol error from tools/call whenever the refund request violates a configured business policy.
Return a normal CallToolResult with a longer refund policy explanation and suggested next steps in the content blocks.

explanation: For customer support tools, the important distinction is between a successful business outcome, a retryable operational failure, and a non-retryable policy denial. If a backend returns a policy denial as ordinary text in a successful-looking result, Claude may interpret the result as ambiguous and try again. Marking the tool result with isError: true gives the agent the documented MCP signal that the tool execution failed, while custom metadata such as errorCategory and isRetryable can provide the recovery policy your application wants.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.The team wants a reusable workflow for adding comprehensive tests to unfamiliar legacy modules. The work usually begins with reading the module, but the next steps vary depending on discovered dependencies, existing test patterns, and whether code seams exist. They care more about producing useful coverage than minimizing latency. What orchestration choice best fits?

choices.text: Use one broad slash command so Claude receives all files and requirements in a single unconstrained request.
Use fixed prompt chaining so Claude always analyzes files, writes tests, runs tests, and fixes failures in that order.
Use dynamic adaptive decomposition so Claude inspects the module, creates subtasks from findings, and synthesizes the test plan.
Use direct execution so Claude immediately writes tests, then handles any missing context after failures appear.

explanation: Anthropic distinguishes workflows, which follow predefined code paths, from more agentic patterns where the model dynamically directs its own process and tool usage. Prompt chaining is a fixed workflow pattern: one step feeds the next, and it is strongest when the task naturally breaks into stable, known subtasks.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.This team wants Claude Code to work with Jira issues for everyday development tasks, and also needs a release-readiness workflow that combines Jira fields with private service ownership rules and internal deployment checks. What integration approach best balances reuse, maintainability, and team-specific behavior?

choices.text: Build one custom MCP server that reimplements Jira operations and also handles the release-readiness workflow.
Create project slash commands for each Jira action and rely on Claude Code prompts to choose API calls.
Store Jira REST procedures in CLAUDE.md and drive ticket updates through slash commands that invoke Bash.
Configure a maintained Jira MCP server for Jira operations, and implement a custom MCP server for the release-readiness workflow.

explanation: MCP helps avoid the N-by-M integration problem: every AI host should not need to hand-build every service integration from scratch. When a standard service integration already exists, such as Jira issue lookup or ticket updates, using a maintained MCP server usually reduces schema design work, implementation effort, and long-term maintenance.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.The team's /release-note workflow rewrites raw commit messages into customer-facing changelog entries. Reviewers notice inconsistent transformations: internal ticket IDs sometimes remain, breaking changes are sometimes softened into vague language, and terse bug-fix commits are sometimes expanded with unsupported details. What change would most directly improve consistency for this workflow?

choices.text: Move the release-note instructions into project settings so the workflow uses shared team configuration.
Add a PreToolUse hook that blocks writes when release notes contain internal ticket IDs.
Run the workflow in plan mode so Claude outlines the changelog strategy before editing text.
Add three representative before-and-after examples, including edge cases, in a clearly tagged examples section.

explanation: When Claude produces inconsistent transformations from the same kind of input, the most effective improvement is usually to show the desired mapping directly. A few well-chosen input/output examples demonstrate judgment that prose often leaves ambiguous: what to remove, what to preserve, how much to rewrite, and how to handle edge cases.

stem: You are integrating Claude Code into your Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline. The system runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, and provides feedback on pull requests. You need to design prompts that provide actionable feedback and minimize false positives.The coordinator delegates pull request review work to separate subagents for security, test coverage, and maintainability. Each subagent returns useful findings to the coordinator, but the final review summary often omits specific file paths, failing test names, and evidence snippets that the coordinator already received. What change best addresses this reliability issue?

choices.text: Tell the review synthesis subagent to infer missing details from the coordinator's earlier conversation history.
Run the synthesis subagent before the specialized review subagents to reduce context size.
Pass each prior subagent's complete structured findings directly into the review synthesis subagent's prompt.
Store the security and test coverage instructions in CLAUDE.md for the next CI pipeline run.

explanation: In a multi-agent review workflow, the coordinator is responsible for moving information between specialized workers. Because subagents are separate agent instances, normal and named subagents run in fresh isolated conversations and do not automatically receive the parent conversation history or prior tool results.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.During evaluation, the synthesis subagent receives a long concatenation of subagent outputs. It repeatedly omits well-supported findings that appear midway through the bundle, while preserving findings near the start and end. What change would best reduce this failure while keeping the synthesis step grounded in the original evidence?

choices.text: Move all source URLs to a final appendix, then keep the narrative evidence together in one continuous section.
Concatenate subagent outputs in completion order, then ask the synthesis agent to infer the main themes from the full bundle.
Replace detailed evidence with progressively shorter summaries, then pass only the newest summary to the synthesis agent.
Prepend a concise findings map before the aggregated outputs, then group detailed evidence under explicit source and topic headers.

explanation: Long-context systems should not treat a large context window as a guarantee that every part of the input will receive equal attention. A practical mitigation is to put a key findings summary or findings map at the beginning of the aggregated input, then organize the supporting material with clear section boundaries so the synthesis agent can locate the relevant evidence.

stem: You are integrating Claude Code into your Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline. The system runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, and provides feedback on pull requests. You need to design prompts that provide actionable feedback and minimize false positives.During a PR review run, Claude calls your submit_review_findings tool with JSON that is syntactically valid and matches the tool schema. Your CI validator rejects the execution because one finding references a file not changed in the PR and another violates an internal review policy. What should the integration do next to give Claude the best chance to correct the review output?

choices.text: Send an immediate tool_result for that tool_use_id with is_error true and the concrete validation failures.
Publish the valid findings and silently discard rejected entries before completing the run.
Retry the request with a higher temperature and ask Claude to produce a cleaner review.
Add a broad CLAUDE.md instruction that review findings must satisfy internal policy.

explanation: When a tool execution fails after Claude has already emitted a tool_use block, the documented feedback path is a tool_result block that references the original tool_use_id. Marking the result with is_error: true and including concrete validation details gives Claude a direct observation it can use in the next turn, which is the practical retry-with-error-feedback pattern for tool workflows.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.This team's custom /upgrade-plan command parses repository upgrade guides into JSON for downstream automation. Evals show valid JSON, but required fields such as rollback_command and compatibility_note are returned as null when the source expresses them in fenced shell blocks, Markdown checklists, or prose paragraphs. The information is present in the source, and the current prompt already lists the schema and says not to omit required fields. What change would most directly address the extraction failures?

choices.text: Add a stronger instruction that required JSON fields must never be null or empty.
Move the schema description into CLAUDE.md so it is always loaded for the command.
Add 3 to 5 structured examples that map varied guide formats to the expected JSON fields.
Raise the temperature to encourage broader interpretation of each upgrade guide format.

explanation: When extraction fails even though the source contains the information, the prompt often needs to teach Claude the mapping behavior, not merely repeat the target schema. Few-shot or multishot prompting is designed for this kind of consistency problem: the examples show that a rollback command in a fenced shell block, a checklist item, or a prose sentence can all populate the same JSON field.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.During a long research run, later synthesis turns sometimes ignore findings that the web search and document analysis subagents returned earlier. Logging shows later Messages API calls contain only the current coordinator instruction and the newest subagent output. What change best addresses the coherence problem?

choices.text: Enable automatic prompt caching so earlier subagent findings are remembered without being included in later requests.
Move prior findings into the system prompt once and omit the historical messages from later requests.
Store a coordinator session identifier and send only the newest subagent result with each follow-up request.
Persist and resend the relevant messages array, including earlier assistant outputs, tool results, and the current user turn.

explanation: The practical mental model for the Messages API is that every call is independent. Claude receives the system content, the current messages array, tools, and other request content for that call, then returns a new assistant message. If a prior subagent result is not present in the current request, Claude cannot rely on it as conversational context.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.This team has a custom /source-check slash command that asks Claude Code to verify report claims against cited sources. One engineer stored source-check.md under ~/.claude/commands/, and the command works for them but not for teammates who clone the repository. What should the team do to make the same command available from the repository?

choices.text: Keep source-check.md in ~/.claude/commands/ and document the command in the project README.
Add the source-check instructions to the root CLAUDE.md and invoke them manually.
Keep source-check.md in .claude/commands/ but exclude the .claude directory from version control.
Move source-check.md into .claude/commands/ in the repository and commit that file.

explanation: Claude Code distinguishes between project-scoped configuration under a repository's .claude/ directory and personal configuration under ~/.claude. For legacy custom slash commands, a Markdown file such as .claude/commands/source-check.md defines the /source-check command for the current project, while ~/.claude/commands/source-check.md defines a personal command available to that user across projects.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.A named dependency-impact subagent is used to inspect changed packages before a refactor plan is finalized. When a local test command intermittently times out after the subagent has already identified several affected files, the parent conversation receives only "impact analysis failed," so the plan omits useful findings. What change best preserves resilience without flooding the parent conversation with raw exploration output?

choices.text: Move the dependency-impact inspection back into the parent conversation, then keep all command logs for planning.
Leave both tools and disallowedTools unset, then rely on inherited access to prevent further Bash retries.
Have the subagent retry transient command failures locally, then return attempts, partial findings, and unresolved errors in its final result.
Have the parent inspect the subagent's intermediate Bash calls, then rerun only the failed command before planning.

explanation: Claude Code subagents are specialized workers inside a single Claude Code session, each with its own context window, system prompt, tool access, and permissions. They are useful for dependency-impact scans because raw grep output, command logs, and file contents can stay out of the main conversation while the parent receives a compact result.

stem: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.A nightly pull request check for this team invokes Claude Code to inspect changes to refund and escalation logic. In CI, the job prints the prompt and then waits until the runner times out because there is no terminal user to answer follow-up prompts. What change best prevents this failure mode?

choices.text: Run Claude Code in plan mode and require the job to approve the generated plan automatically.
Create a shared slash command in .claude/commands/ and invoke that command from the CI job.
Add a CLAUDE.md instruction telling Claude Code not to ask follow-up questions during CI reviews.
Run Claude Code with the -p or --print flag and provide the review prompt non-interactively.

explanation: Claude Code has an interactive terminal mode for developer sessions and a non-interactive mode for automation. In CI, there is no human sitting at the terminal to answer prompts, approve actions, or continue a conversation, so the invocation should use -p or –print to process a prompt and exit.

stem: You are integrating Claude Code into your Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline. The system runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, and provides feedback on pull requests. You need to design prompts that provide actionable feedback and minimize false positives.PR reviews are producing false positives because migration-specific review criteria are being applied to frontend and documentation changes. Migration files can appear under several packages, such as services, apps, and shared libraries. What change should this team make so those conventions are loaded only when Claude reads relevant files?

choices.text: Add .claude/rules/database-migrations.md with YAML frontmatter paths: ["/migrations//*.{sql,ts}"] and place the migration review checklist there.
Create .claude/rules/database-migrations.md without frontmatter and rely on its filename to target migration files.
Move the migration checklist into the root CLAUDE.md and instruct Claude to apply it only to migration-related files.
Add ~/.claude/rules/database-migrations.md with the migration glob and ask each reviewer to install it locally.

explanation: For conventions that should apply only to certain file types or directories, Claude Code supports path-specific rules as Markdown files under .claude/rules/. A rule becomes conditional by adding YAML frontmatter with a paths field, such as paths: ["/migrations//*.{sql,ts}"], and Claude loads it when it reads files matching those glob patterns.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.After one run has completed a broad source review and produced a useful baseline analysis, the team wants to compare two different synthesis strategies from that same starting point. They need each strategy exploration to keep its own conversational history without changing the baseline session history. What should the team do?

choices.text: Resume the baseline session with the SDK fork option enabled for each strategy, then track the new session IDs.
Use continue in each strategy worker, then let the SDK select the latest session in the current directory.
Enable file checkpointing for each strategy, then use checkpoints as the branching mechanism for session history.
Resume the baseline session normally for each strategy, then rely on separate prompts to keep the branches distinct.

explanation: For divergent research approaches, the important distinction is between conversation state and filesystem state. An Agent SDK session is the transcript of prompts, tool calls, tool results, and responses, so returning to a session restores the model's prior conversational context, such as the sources reviewed and analysis already performed.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.This team added a prompt-based quality gate that classifies draft report findings before publication. One category, "unsupported market claim," now produces many false positives on well-cited synthesis paragraphs, while other categories such as missing citation and source conflict are performing well. Engineers have started ignoring the entire quality report. What should the team do next?

choices.text: Temporarily omit the noisy category from the active prompt, keep accurate categories enabled, and rebuild it with examples, definitions, and precision/recall evals.
Force the quality gate to return strict JSON, reject malformed outputs, and use schema compliance as the main trust metric.
Disable every quality category for a release cycle, collect no automated findings, and re-enable all categories after prompt edits.
Keep the noisy category active, add a warning that false positives are expected, and ask engineers to manually disregard those findings.

explanation: When a single high false-positive category undermines confidence in an automated review system, the practical move is to separate the noisy signal from the useful signal. Anthropic's documented moderation pattern uses application-defined category lists in prompts, and those lists are customizable, so temporarily omitting or suppressing one category is an application-level control rather than a special built-in category toggle.

stem: You are integrating Claude Code into your Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline. The system runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, and provides feedback on pull requests. You need to design prompts that provide actionable feedback and minimize false positives.Long pull requests are causing the review step to run near the context limit. The trace shows each file-analysis tool call appends a large tool_result payload with build metadata, ownership data, full lint output, historical CI runs, and dependency details, even though the reviewer uses only a small subset of those fields. What change best addresses the reliability issue?

choices.text: Increase max_tokens for the review response and instruct Claude to ignore irrelevant tool-result fields.
Enable context editing to clear old tool results after the request crosses a configured threshold.
Change the tool wrapper to return compact, review-specific tool_result payloads with only the fields needed.
Apply prompt caching to the tool definitions and repeated review prefix to reduce context-window pressure.

explanation: Tool-heavy review agents often fail because tool results become part of the conversation context. Anthropic documents that tool definitions and accumulated tool_result blocks can exhaust context in long-running agents, and the context window includes messages, tool results, tool definitions, and generated output. See Manage tool context and Context windows.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.The document-analysis subagent uses client-side tools to read licensed reports and extract evidence. When a report is unavailable, the tool returns a tool_result with is_error: true, but the content is always "Operation failed", whether the cause is an expired license, a temporary timeout, an unsupported file format, or a valid search with no matching passages. The coordinator then either retries, drops the source, or escalates unpredictably. What change would best improve recovery behavior?

choices.text: Expand the document tool descriptions so Claude avoids tools that may fail.
Return categorized tool_result errors with retryability, cause, attempted input, and suggested recovery.
Add a coordinator instruction to retry every failed document tool call before escalating.
Convert failed document reads into empty result sets so synthesis can continue.

explanation: For client tools, Claude does not execute the external operation itself. Claude emits a structured tool_use request, the application runs the tool, and the application sends the result back in a tool_result block, as described in Tool use overview and Handle tool calls.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.This team is adding SDK-managed subagents for code review and documentation work. They want Claude to route work to the right subagent based on its purpose, and they want the documentation subagent to read files but not edit or run commands. Which configuration should they use?

choices.text: Create subagent files with prompts only, use filenames as routing descriptions, and rely on parent permissions for tool limits.
Define agents by display name, put the subagent type inside prompt, and block editing tools through top-level disallowedTools.
Define top-level allowedTools for read-only tools, add routing guidance to CLAUDE.md, and omit per-subagent tool settings.
Define a programmatic agents map keyed by subagent type, set each description and prompt, and give the documentation subagent a read-only tools allowlist.

explanation: For SDK-managed subagents, the central configuration object is the AgentDefinition inside the programmatic agents option. Each entry is keyed by the subagent type, and that key is what Claude uses when invoking the Agent tool with subagent_type. The required description is the natural-language routing cue, while the required prompt acts as the subagent's system prompt.

stem:
You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.

The team is refactoring long cases into a coordinator that can delegate billing and returns investigation steps. During testing, a container crash mid-dispute causes the replacement worker to lose the verified customer ID, prior order findings, and a decision that the case must be escalated. The workers do not share a filesystem, and local session JSONL files are not reliably present after restart. What change best supports safe crash recovery?

choices.text: Copy local JSONL transcript files opportunistically, then resume whichever session appears newest on the replacement worker.
Resume the Agent SDK session with continue, then let the coordinator reconstruct state from the latest local transcript.
Add stronger memory instructions to the system prompt, then restart the agent from the last customer message.
Persist an application-defined JSON state manifest, then load it on restart and inject it into coordinator and subagent prompts.

explanation: Local JSONL transcripts are per machine (sessions: where transcripts are stored) and the stem says workers do not share a disk. Persist your own JSON state and inject it on startup. --continue cannot see a file that is gone. A stronger prompt does not restore a crashed process. Copying the newest JSONL is the race the stem rules out. Doc idea: Sessions, transcripts are local; application state is yours.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.Your /review command posts PR feedback in four categories: correctness, security, performance, and style. Evaluation data shows security findings are usually accepted, but style comments are often dismissed as local-preference nitpicks. Developers have begun ignoring the whole review report, including security items. What change should you make first?

choices.text: Move security findings to the top of every report, then label them as mandatory review items for developers.
Track only the overall accepted-finding rate, then revise the prompt when the aggregate metric drops below target.
Raise the severity of all findings, then instruct Claude to be more conservative across every review category.
Track precision and recall by category, then tighten or disable the noisy style criteria using flagged and non-flagged examples.

explanation: For review automation, each finding category behaves like a classification problem: Claude is deciding whether a piece of code should be flagged or not. A high false positive rate in one visible category, such as style, can teach developers that the entire review report is noisy, so they may also ignore accurate security or correctness findings.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.Your team created a Claude Code skill called literature-gap-audit. Its SKILL.md tells Claude to search repository prompts, inspect report templates, and brainstorm missing provenance checks before anyone edits the coordinator. When developers invoke it, pages of file-search notes and rejected alternatives remain in the main session, and later report-generation edits become less focused. What should you change in the skill configuration?

choices.text: Invoke /fork for the audit so it inherits the full current conversation history.
Move the audit instructions into CLAUDE.md and run /compact after the audit finishes.
Set disable-model-invocation: true and leave the audit in the main conversation.
Add context: fork in SKILL.md and keep the audit as explicit task instructions.

explanation: Use context: fork when a Claude Code skill performs a side task that would otherwise flood the main conversation with search results, logs, file contents, or exploratory alternatives. In a forked skill, the rendered SKILL.md content drives work in a separate subagent context, and the main session receives the useful result rather than the full discovery trail.

stem: You are integrating Claude Code into your Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline. The system runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, and provides feedback on pull requests. You need to design prompts that provide actionable feedback and minimize false positives.Recent CI runs show that on pull requests touching 20 to 40 files, the review often reports superficial style issues while missing problems that depend on interactions between files. The team wants a more reliable review design without turning the review into an open-ended investigation. What change should they make?

choices.text: Send the entire diff to one reviewer prompt and raise the severity threshold for comments.
Let Claude dynamically choose its own review path and tools for each pull request.
Run a prompt chain that reviews files in focused passes, then runs a separate integration pass over the collected findings.
Run independent parallel reviewers for file groups and publish their comments without a synthesis step.

explanation: For predictable CI review tasks, a prompt chaining workflow is a strong fit because the desired process is known before the run starts: inspect focused units of work, preserve the findings, then perform a broader consistency check. This is different from asking an agent to dynamically decide the review strategy for every pull request.

stem: You are integrating Claude Code into your Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline. The system runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, and provides feedback on pull requests. You need to design prompts that provide actionable feedback and minimize false positives.This team's CI review prompt flags possible policy violations and requires each finding to include a policy_section and supporting_quote. A pull request adds retention logic for customer support transcripts, but the only policy excerpt provided to Claude covers application logs and analytics events, with no transcript policy. The validator rejects Claude's finding because supporting_quote is empty. What should the pipeline do?

choices.text: Increase max_tokens and continue the response to complete the missing policy evidence.
Return an insufficient information result and require a supporting quote before posting the finding.
Force a strict structured output schema so supporting_quote is always present.
Retry the same review prompt until Claude produces a non-empty supporting_quote field.

explanation: Validation-retry loops are useful when Claude's output is malformed, incomplete, or structurally inconsistent with the expected format. They are not a mechanism for discovering facts that are absent from the source material. When a CI review finding requires evidence, the safer design is to let the system emit insufficient information rather than retry until a claim appears.

stem: You are integrating Claude Code into your Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline. The system runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, and provides feedback on pull requests. You need to design prompts that provide actionable feedback and minimize false positives.A compliance review finds that, in rare pull requests, the system posts an approving review before the required test-result artifact has been attached. The rule is non-negotiable: approval actions must not execute unless the artifact is already present and passing. What change should this team make?

choices.text: Add a stronger system prompt that instructs Claude to verify artifacts before approvals.
Add a PreToolUse command hook that denies approval commands when the passing artifact is absent.
Add a UserPromptSubmit command hook that appends artifact-check instructions to approval requests.
Add a PostToolUse command hook that checks the artifact after approval commands complete.

explanation: When a CI/CD rule is non-negotiable, the enforcement point should be outside the model's voluntary behavior. Claude Code hooks are designed as lifecycle automation points that provide deterministic control, so required actions happen, or forbidden actions are blocked, without relying on the LLM to choose correctly every time.

stem: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.For a nightly backlog triage run, this team plans to submit thousands of unresolved conversations through the Message Batches API. The batch inputs include client tool definitions for MCP-backed customer and order systems that are implemented by the team's service. Which design is most appropriate?

choices.text: Move all customer support tools into batch requests as server tools so refunds can complete without follow-up requests.
Use batch for initial analysis or tool requests, then execute returned client tools and continue each case in later Messages requests.
Include the client tool schemas in each batch item and let the batch worker execute the backend tools before finalizing responses.
Prompt Claude to infer missing customer and order fields whenever a batch item cannot complete the tool loop.

explanation: The important distinction is not that Message Batches cannot use tools at all. Anthropic documents that batches can include many Messages API features, including tool use, and that server tools can run as part of batch processing.

stem: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.During a billing dispute flow, Claude requests get_customer and lookup_order in the same assistant turn. The get_customer call succeeds, but lookup_order intermittently times out. Production logs show two attempted fixes: one wrapper returns an empty order list as a successful lookup, while another aborts the entire conversation whenever lookup_order fails. What change best addresses the reliability issue?

choices.text: Return tool results for completed calls only, omit lookup_order after its timeout, and ask Claude to proceed.
