Return tool results for both calls, flag lookup_order with is_error: true, and continue from partial context.
Return tool results for both calls, replace lookup_order with an empty order list, and continue as a successful lookup.
Return tool results for both calls, discard get_customer after lookup_order fails, and end the support workflow.

explanation: Tool failures should be treated as part of the agent's observed state, not hidden or converted into misleading business facts. When Claude emits tool_use, the application is expected to execute the requested client tools and return matching tool_result blocks, using the same tool_use_id so Claude can connect each result to the right call.

stem: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.An online retailer's support automation team has successful MCP tool calls returning values in inconsistent formats: one response uses Unix timestamps and numeric status codes, while another uses ISO 8601 dates and string status values. Claude sometimes misinterprets these fields when deciding whether an order is eligible for refund. What should this team implement to give the agent a canonical representation before it reasons over successful tool results?

choices.text: Add a PostToolUse hook that returns decision: "block" when a tool response uses noncanonical fields.
Add a PostToolUse hook that returns hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext with mappings for the inconsistent fields.
Add a PreToolUse hook that blocks calls whenever the selected tool may return noncanonical fields.
Add a PostToolUse hook that reads tool_response and returns hookSpecificOutput.updatedToolOutput with normalized fields.

explanation: For successful tool calls, a PostToolUse hook is the right interception point for normalizing returned data before Claude reasons over it. The hook input includes tool-dependent fields such as tool_input and tool_response, so the normalization logic must understand each MCP tool's output shape rather than assuming one fixed schema.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.Benchmark runs on broad topics are slow and produce uneven coverage. Logs show the coordinator asks one specialist to research every dimension, passes a compressed prose summary to the next specialist, and only then asks for the final report. The relevant dimensions are known at the start and do not depend on one another. What design change best improves latency and coverage while preserving a coherent final report?

choices.text: Have the coordinator split the request into dimension-specific subtasks, pass shared constraints to each, invoke independent specialists together, and synthesize their findings.
Have the coordinator disable parallel tool use, process each dimension in separate turns, append every raw result, and synthesize after the last subtask.
Have each specialist hand off unfinished dimensions to another specialist, merge their private context, and return a consolidated answer to the coordinator.
Have the coordinator keep one broad subtask, increase the search specialist's source budget, pass its summary downstream, and request a completeness critique.

explanation: For independent research dimensions, the strongest pattern is to split, run, collect, then synthesize. The coordinator should create distinct subtasks, provide each specialist with the shared scope, constraints, and citation requirements, then combine their structured findings into one coherent report.

stem: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.A customer support engineering team is building a resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK with MCP tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). During testing, the agent trace shows Claude requesting lookup_order through MCP, but no order lookup result is observed and the session ends without a final customer response. What implementation change should this team make?

choices.text: Run all support MCP tools before starting the agent, then provide their outputs for Claude to summarize in one turn.
Parse the assistant's natural-language text for completion phrases, then end the workflow when it says the issue is resolved.
Add a system instruction that tells Claude to execute each MCP backend operation itself before producing any customer-facing response.
Run the SDK-driven agent loop so each MCP tool invocation is dispatched, results are returned, and processing continues until a final response.

explanation: Tool use is a contract between Claude and the surrounding runtime. In an Agent SDK system with MCP tools, Claude can decide that it needs a tool and emit a structured tool invocation, but the model itself does not perform backend operations such as customer or order lookups.

stem: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.A refund operation sometimes fails because the order is outside the return window, but the agent treats the MCP response as a successful refund and tells the customer it was completed. What change should this team make to communicate the tool failure correctly?

choices.text: Return a CallToolResult with isError: true and include structured failure details in the result content.
Return a normal tool result containing an error field and ask the agent to infer failure from the content.
Return a CallToolResult with isError: false and include structured failure details in the result content.
Raise a protocol-level server exception and include structured failure details in the exception message.

explanation: In MCP, a tool can be invoked successfully at the protocol level while still failing at the application or business-logic level. The right pattern is to return a CallToolResult that marks the result with isError: true, then put useful recovery context in the result content.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.For documentation produced during this workflow, the team runs an extraction job that converts design docs and pull request descriptions into JSON work items. Reviewers can inspect only about 20% of items. The current job sends any response with stop_reason: end_turn directly into the tracker, and spot checks find bad work items when two source files disagree or a field is inferred weakly from context. What change best improves the review workflow?

choices.text: Use end_turn as the acceptance signal, retry max_tokens outputs with more tokens, then queue refusals and malformed records for reviewers.
Request logprobs and top_logprobs through the OpenAI SDK layer, then queue low-probability records before well-formed records for reviewers.
Enable citations on the source documents alongside JSON schema output, then queue records missing citation blocks before other records for reviewers.
Add per-field confidence, ambiguity, contradiction, and evidence-excerpt fields to the JSON schema, then queue flagged records before clean records.

explanation: For high-stakes extraction workflows, review routing should be driven by application-defined uncertainty signals, not by API mechanics that were designed for other purposes. stop_reason tells the application whether Claude ended normally, requested a tool, hit a token limit, refused, or encountered another stopping condition; it does not say that an extracted field is trustworthy.

stem: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.The team keeps refund and escalation policy changes in GitHub and requests managed Claude Code Review only during scheduled review batches. A reviewer comments @claude review once, fixes are pushed, and then a second @claude review once repeats several resolved findings as new inline comments. They want the next manual re-review to preserve reviewer trust while still surfacing any unresolved issue from the first review. What should they change?

choices.text: Change the manual command to @claude review so the PR subscribes to push-triggered reviews for the remaining work.
Add REVIEW.md guidance that uses prior findings during re-reviews and reports only new or still-unresolved issues.
Rerun the review from the GitHub Checks tab so Claude Code refreshes comments against the new commit.
Keep review instructions unchanged and have maintainers close any duplicate inline threads after each re-review.

explanation: Repeated review runs need more than access to the current diff. The review should be given a clear comparison task: consider the prior findings, then report only issues that are new or still unaddressed. In managed Claude Code Review, the documented place for review-specific guidance is REVIEW.md, which is injected into the review pipeline as review guidance.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.This team is adding a custom MCP server and client-side integration for engineering reference material. Developers want the host to present a browsable list of design docs, runbooks, database schemas, and architecture notes, then attach selected content to Claude's context only when needed. They do not want Claude to spend turns calling exploratory functions just to discover what exists. What design best matches MCP's control model?

choices.text: Publish each reference item as a prompt, require developers to run a slash command, and inject the document text from that prompt.
Declare the server's resources capability, expose catalog metadata through resources/list, and read selected URI contents with resources/read.
Copy the catalog into CLAUDE.md, refresh it during repository updates, and ask Claude to request document names from developers.
Add a list_reference_material tool, require Claude to call it first, and fetch selected documents through additional tool calls.

explanation: MCP separates server capabilities by control model. Resources are application-controlled contextual data, tools are model-controlled executable functions, and prompts are user-controlled templates. A content catalog belongs in resources because the host or client can decide how to show, filter, search, or attach available context without asking the model to discover the catalog through tool calls.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.A university library's multi-agent research system routes tasks to MCP-backed web search and document analysis subagents. During evaluation, the coordinator often sends literature-review tasks to the web search subagent when the user asked for analysis of uploaded PDFs, and sends web-currentness tasks to the document analysis subagent. The tool implementations work correctly once called. Which tool-definition change should this team make first to improve selection reliability?

choices.text: Rewrite each tool definition with detailed descriptions covering use cases, non-use cases, inputs, returned data, and caveats.
Add request examples inside JSON Schema field descriptions for web queries, PDF analysis, and citation searches.
Force each research turn through the model API to call one available tool before returning results to the coordinator.
Rename each tool with shorter service-prefixed names while leaving the current descriptions and schemas unchanged.

explanation: When several tools have similar capabilities, tool descriptions are the highest-leverage place to improve selection reliability. Claude decides whether and which tool to call from the user request plus the tool definition, and Anthropic identifies detailed descriptions as a major factor in tool performance.

stem: You are integrating Claude Code into your Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline. The system runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, and provides feedback on pull requests. You need to design prompts that provide actionable feedback and minimize false positives.The system described above uses one Claude call for pull request review, test generation, and PR metadata updates. Logs show the review phase sometimes invokes test-writing tools for non-testable style comments, then returns prose instead of the structured finding object your pipeline expects. What change best improves tool selection reliability while preserving automated test generation elsewhere in the pipeline?

choices.text: Keep one shared CI step, expose all tools with sharper descriptions, and set tool_choice to any for review output.
Keep one shared CI step, namespace tool names by category, and leave tool_choice on auto for model flexibility.
Expose all CI tools to both steps, set tool_choice to none during review, and parse JSON from assistant text.
Separate review and test-generation steps, expose only role-specific tools to each step, and force the review step's reporting tool with tool_choice.

explanation: When a workflow has distinct responsibilities, tool access should be scoped to the role performing that step. A review step should not have write-test or PR-label mutation tools if its job is to produce review findings, because every extra tool increases the chance of an irrelevant action being selected.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.After a long plan-mode investigation, a developer saves the session ID before making changes. They want to test a minimal patch and a larger refactor from the same analyzed context, but both attempts will touch overlapping files in the same working directory. Which approach best supports independent exploration without confusing conversation history with file state?

choices.text: Fork the saved session once, and run both attempts in the same working directory as isolated file branches.
Resume the saved session ID with the fork option for each attempt, and checkpoint files before edits.
Use continue twice from the project directory, and rely on Claude Code to select the baseline automatically.
Resume the saved session ID twice without forking, and ask Claude to keep each attempt separate.

explanation: Forking is the right tool when the valuable asset is prior conversational context: prompts, tool calls, tool results, and Claude's previous analysis. A fork starts a new session from a copy of an existing session's history, with its own session ID, while the original session remains unchanged. That is ideal for comparing divergent plans that should share the same investigation baseline.

stem: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.Production traces show that every incoming request is sent through separate identity, order, refund-policy, and escalation-summary subagents. Simple order-status questions now have high latency, and some responses include irrelevant refund-policy caveats. What change best improves the design while preserving specialized workers for cases that need them?

choices.text: Route every case through all subagents, then ask the final responder to remove irrelevant findings before answering.
Give every subagent the same backend tools, then instruct each worker to skip itself when it is not needed.
Replace the subagents with one large system prompt that covers identity, orders, refunds, and escalation.
Add a coordinator step that inspects the case, invokes only needed subagents, and passes each a self-contained task summary.

explanation: A good coordinator does not treat every request as if it needs the maximum workflow. It should analyze the current case, determine which capabilities are actually needed, and delegate only the self-contained pieces of work that benefit from a specialized worker.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.This team uses Claude Code to generate release notes and API documentation from pull requests. Reviewers can check only a small fraction of generated fields before publishing, and pilots show accuracy differs by field, with endpoint names usually correct and breaking-change labels often wrong. What change best routes human review to the items most likely to benefit from it?

choices.text: Emit per-field confidence values in structured output, calibrate thresholds on labeled examples, and route low-confidence fields to reviewers.
Use aggregate accuracy from the pilot, reduce review when it exceeds target, and sample remaining outputs uniformly.
Compute one document-level confidence score, review documents below a threshold, and publish all fields in approved documents.
Treat successful stop reasons as high confidence, skip review for those outputs, and review only truncated responses.

explanation: For production extraction and documentation workflows, the useful unit of review is often the field, not the whole response. A generated release note might have a correct endpoint name, an uncertain migration instruction, and an incorrect breaking-change label. Asking Claude to emit per-field confidence values in a structured format gives downstream systems something to route on, but those values should be treated as model outputs that require calibration, not as native API probabilities.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.Recent evaluations show that the final report sometimes treats the same source as both confirming and contradicting a claim, and reviewers find that unsupported claims in long source bundles are missed. The team also wants review checkpoints it can log and score before the report is generated. What should the team do?

choices.text: Run an explicit prompt chain with source-level review passes, then run a separate integration pass over the reviewed findings.
Launch several identical reviewers on the full source bundle and accept findings that appear most often.
Add confidence scores to every cited claim and route only low-confidence claims to another reviewer.
Send the complete source bundle to one reviewer and require a longer checklist before report generation.

explanation: The stronger design is to treat this as explicit prompt chaining: use separate API calls for focused source-level review, then pass the resulting structured findings into a cross-source integration review. Anthropic documents prompt chaining as a way to break a task into sequential calls when you need visible intermediate outputs, evaluation points, or a fixed pipeline structure.

stem: You are integrating Claude Code into your Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline. The system runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, and provides feedback on pull requests. You need to design prompts that provide actionable feedback and minimize false positives.After three months, the system described above assigns a high confidence score to most structured review findings and generated test recommendations. Manual review capacity is being reduced, but the team still needs to measure production error rates and catch rare failure modes in areas like migrations, security-sensitive changes, and language-specific conventions. What monitoring approach best fits this goal?

choices.text: Sample high-confidence findings uniformly across all repositories, then publish one aggregate error rate for the whole pipeline.
Sample high-confidence findings within strata for change type, component, language, and finding category, then label errors and novel patterns separately.
Sample only low-confidence findings within queues for human review, then treat high-confidence accepted pull requests as error-free cases.
Increase the confidence cutoff for findings before merging, then discontinue review for outputs above the new cutoff.

explanation: For a CI review system, high confidence should not mean no measurement. It should mean the output is eligible for lighter review, while a designed sample of those outputs is still checked so the team can estimate real error rates and detect unexpected failures.

stem: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.A customer support platform uses the Messages API client tool-use loop. During beta testing, policy requires refunds above $500 to be reviewed by a human. In several high-emotion billing disputes, the agent emits a process_refund tool_use request for amounts above that threshold after lookup_order, and the application executes the request. What change would most effectively enforce the workflow requirement?

choices.text: Set tool_choice to none whenever the customer message includes emotionally charged billing language.
Update the system prompt to state that over-threshold refunds must always be sent to escalate_to_human.
Force tool_choice to the escalate_to_human tool for every billing dispute involving a refund request.
Add an application-side guard that blocks over-threshold process_refund calls and routes the case to escalate_to_human.

explanation: For client-executed tools in the Messages API tool-use loop, Claude does not run the backend operation itself. Claude emits a structured tool_use request, then the application decides whether and how to execute the requested operation and sends back a tool_result. That makes the application boundary the right place to enforce business rules that must not be bypassed.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.A payments platform team is about to migrate a shared logging library used across more than 45 files. Two viable integration approaches have different infrastructure requirements, and the maintainers want Claude Code to inspect the codebase and propose an approach before implementation begins. Which initial workflow is most appropriate?

choices.text: Start in acceptEdits, let Claude apply the migration, and review the resulting diff after the changes finish.
Start in bypassPermissions, let Claude run commands freely, and rely on tests to identify any regressions afterward.
Start with a direct implementation prompt, ask Claude to choose an approach, and refine the design during editing.
Enter plan mode, have Claude inspect the affected areas, and review the proposed plan before choosing execution mode.

explanation: Plan mode in Claude Code is a permission mode for analysis before implementation, not a different model or subscription tier. It lets Claude inspect the codebase and develop a plan while avoiding source file edits until the user approves the plan, which is exactly the control point needed for large migrations and architecture-sensitive changes.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.After receiving a broad prompt such as "produce a comprehensive cited report on AI adoption in healthcare," the coordinator must decide how to start before delegating research. Past runs produced well-written reports but had uneven coverage and wasted effort on tangential details. Which coordinator strategy best addresses this class of task?

choices.text: Start with a fixed search-to-report pipeline, then prevent the coordinator from revising scope once the first subagent assignments are sent.
Start with a complete report outline from the report agent, then task other subagents with finding citations for each planned section.
Start with parallel assignments for the most obvious keywords, then ask the synthesis agent to merge completed findings into a unified report.
Start with a discovery pass that maps the topic structure and high-impact areas, then assign prioritized subtasks that can change as findings reveal dependencies.

explanation: Open-ended work benefits from separating exploration, planning, and execution. In a multi-agent research system, exploration means mapping the topic dimensions, likely source types, stakeholder groups, and possible coverage gaps before the coordinator commits subagents to detailed work.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.In this team's monorepo, unit and component tests sit next to the source files they cover under services/, packages/, and apps/. Claude Code applies inconsistent testing guidance because similar instructions were copied into several directory-level memory files, and some directories are missing updates. What should you change to make the testing convention easier to maintain while avoiding unnecessary context for non-test work?

choices.text: Move the testing conventions into the root CLAUDE.md so Claude loads them during all project conversations.
Add a CLAUDE.md file to every directory that contains tests and duplicate the shared testing conventions there.
Create a .claude/rules/testing.md file with paths globs for test files and store the shared testing conventions there.
Put the testing conventions in a project slash command under .claude/commands/ and ask developers to run it before editing tests.

explanation: When a convention applies to files scattered across a repository, use a path-scoped rule rather than many directory-local memory files. Claude Code supports markdown rules under .claude/rules/ with YAML frontmatter such as a paths field, allowing a rule to target glob patterns like test file names across multiple directories.

stem: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.During an incident review, this team needs Claude Code to understand where refund escalation decisions are made in a large repository. Previous investigations loaded entire service directories into context before identifying the relevant flow, which made the session noisy and slow. What approach should the team use first?

choices.text: Use Read across the service directories, then summarize all files before searching for refund and escalation identifiers.
Use Glob for refund and escalation identifiers, then infer the control flow from the returned matching paths.
Use Grep for refund and escalation identifiers, then Read only matching files and follow imports from those entry points.
Use Bash for broad shell searches, then paste full command output before deciding which files to inspect.

explanation: For large codebase exploration, the practical pattern is search first, read second. Claude Code's Grep tool is designed to search for patterns in file contents, while Read loads the contents of specific files. Starting with content search lets the agent find likely entry points such as refund handlers, escalation checks, or MCP tool wrappers before spending context on full file contents.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.During evals, the synthesis phase is given access to two client tools: analyze_content for web search snippets and analyze_content_docs for uploaded PDFs. The model frequently calls the PDF-oriented tool on search results and the web-oriented tool on document excerpts. Both tool descriptions are nearly identical, saying only that the tool analyzes content and returns key findings. The team must keep separate web-snippet and PDF-specific analyzers exposed for separate output contracts and audit logging. What change would most effectively reduce the wrong-tool calls?

choices.text: Force tool_choice to the document analyzer first, then let Claude call the web analyzer if the first result is insufficient.
Keep the tool names unchanged, add more examples to the synthesis prompt, and ask Claude to choose the correct analyzer carefully.
Merge the analyzers into one generic tool, accept either web snippets or PDFs, and decide source handling inside the tool.
Rename the tools with source-specific names, rewrite each description with use and non-use boundaries, and update the dispatcher for the new names.

explanation: When two tools appear to do the same thing, Claude has little basis for choosing reliably. Tool definitions should make the intended use clear in the description, including when to use the tool, when not to use it, what inputs it expects, and what it returns. Anthropic's troubleshooting guidance identifies wrong-tool calls as a likely symptom of description ambiguity, with the recommended fix being to differentiate tools by usage boundaries, not just capabilities.

stem: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.This team wants an on-demand Claude Code workflow named /case-review for support engineers. The workflow produces lengthy exploratory notes, should run outside the main conversation context, should let Claude read and search project files without repeated permission prompts, and should show the expected case ID when developers invoke it. Which setup best fits these requirements?

choices.text: Create .claude/skills/case-review/SKILL.md with context: main, allowed-tools for Read and Grep, and argument-hint: [case-id].
Create .claude/skills/case-review.md with context: fork, allowed-tools for Read and Grep, and argument-hint: [case-id].
Create .claude/skills/case-review/SKILL.md with context: fork, allowed-tools for Read and Grep, and argument-hint: [case-id].
Create .claude/skills/case-review/SKILL.md with context: fork, allowed-tools as an exclusive allowlist, and argument-hint as a validator.

explanation: Claude Code skills package reusable workflows as directories containing a required SKILL.md. The file can include YAML frontmatter between — markers plus Markdown instructions, and a project skill stored under .claude/skills//SKILL.md can be invoked directly as /skill-name or loaded when relevant.

stem: You are integrating Claude Code into your Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline. The system runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, and provides feedback on pull requests. You need to design prompts that provide actionable feedback and minimize false positives.This team is designing a new automated reviewer for flaky-test risk. The requested behavior has unresolved product and workflow questions, including when comments are actionable, when they are noise, and what verification should prove. What should the team do before asking Claude Code to implement it?

choices.text: Run an interactive planning session where Claude uses AskUserQuestion, writes a self-contained SPEC.md, then implement it from a fresh session.
Run a delegated subagent via the Agent tool to ask AskUserQuestion prompts, then pass its transcript to the implementer.
Run direct execution with a detailed review checklist in the prompt, then adjust the workflow after the first CI failures.
Run a scheduled autonomous Claude Code job that infers missing requirements from recent pull request discussions.

explanation: For larger or ambiguous Claude Code work, the recommended pattern is to let Claude interview the developer before implementation. The documented workflow starts from a minimal feature prompt, asks Claude to use AskUserQuestion to explore technical implementation, UI or developer experience, edge cases, concerns, and tradeoffs, then writes the result to a self-contained SPEC.md. See Best practices for Claude Code.

stem: You are integrating Claude Code into your Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline. The system runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, and provides feedback on pull requests. You need to design prompts that provide actionable feedback and minimize false positives.During a PR review run, the main session reads the changed files, notes a failing test, and then delegates to an ordinary named security-review subagent, not a fork. The subagent returns generic findings and misses PR-specific evidence from the diff and test output. What change would most directly improve the review's reliability?

choices.text: Instruct the subagent to read the parent conversation transcript before producing review findings.
Include the changed files, key diff excerpts, failing test output, and review criteria in the subagent prompt.
Start a fresh named subagent invocation and rely on its persisted transcript from earlier CI steps.
Compact the main conversation before delegation so the subagent inherits only the important parent context.

explanation: Ordinary named Claude Code subagents are designed for isolated, task-specific work. That isolation is valuable in CI because a security reviewer can have its own instructions, tool access, and permissions, while the main review conversation avoids being flooded with every intermediate step. The tradeoff is that the subagent does not automatically know what the main session already read or decided.

stem: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate. An online retailer's support engineering team is implementing billing dispute handling as a lower-level Messages API tool loop. After a pilot, the orchestration layer is found to map every billing dispute to the same fixed path, even though some cases need only a policy explanation, some require order lookup, and some should be escalated before any refund action. Which change best aligns the system with Claude's tool-use model?

choices.text: Force the next support tool with tool_choice: {"type":"tool","name":"process_refund"} on each turn according to application-managed workflow state.
Route each request through an intent classifier that selects one predefined chain of support tools for that subtype.
Continue calling Claude until its assistant text says the case is resolved, then stop the tool loop.
Run a stop_reason driven loop with tool_choice: {"type":"auto"} and let Claude choose tool use or a final reply each turn.

explanation: Claude tool use is designed around a model-driven loop, not a preconfigured decision tree. With tool_choice: {"type":"auto"}, which is the default when tools are supplied, Claude decides on each turn whether to call a tool or respond directly based on the user request, tool descriptions, and prior context.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.During a trial of a custom /project-release-notes command, this team gives the diff analysis, issue triage, and final synthesis agents the same full tool list: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, WebSearch, WebFetch, and issue-tracker MCP tools. Even when the coordinator provides complete diff and issue summaries, the final synthesis agent often runs broad WebSearch and issue-tracker queries and adds unrelated items to the notes. What change best addresses the behavior?

choices.text: Add few-shot release note examples that show synthesis using only delegated findings.
Rename broad lookup tools so their names indicate they are for research only.
Restrict each agent to role-specific tools and route extra lookups through the coordinator.
Strengthen the synthesis prompt to forbid exploratory searches after summaries are provided.

explanation: Specialized agents work best when their tool access matches their responsibility. Giving every agent the same broad tool set increases the chance that an agent will solve the wrong problem, such as a synthesis agent trying to gather new evidence instead of combining the evidence it was given.

stem: You are building a structured data extraction system using Claude. The system extracts information from unstructured documents, validates the output using JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) schemas, and maintains high accuracy. It must handle edge cases gracefully and integrate with downstream systems.This team is using the Messages API MCP connector with separate MCP servers for schema selection, entity enrichment, and delivery to a downstream queue. They want one extraction request to choose tools from all three integrations as needed, rather than preselecting a single integration per document. What should they implement?

choices.text: Run three separate requests, each with one mcp_toolset, and pass extracted JSON between requests manually.
Define all three servers in mcp_servers only, omit mcp_toolset entries, and rely on automatic tool discovery across the connections.
Create one generic proxy tool, route every operation through it, and hide server-specific tool metadata from Claude.
Define all three servers in mcp_servers, add one matching mcp_toolset per server in tools, and let Claude choose among the discovered tools.

explanation: MCP is designed around a host, client, server architecture in which an AI application can connect to more than one MCP server. The architecture documentation describes fetching tools from all connected MCP servers and combining them into a unified tool registry available to the language model, while routing each tool call back to the server that owns that tool.

stem: You are building a structured data extraction system using Claude. The system extracts information from unstructured documents, validates the output using JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) schemas, and maintains high accuracy. It must handle edge cases gracefully and integrate with downstream systems.The repository has packages for invoices, contracts, and claims, each with different extraction edge cases and validation conventions. Developers usually start Claude Code from the package they are editing, and maintainers want package-specific standards loaded automatically without making every package inherit every domain's guidance. What configuration best fits this workflow?

choices.text: Store each package's standards in separate Markdown files and link them from package READMEs instead of importing them.
Move all domain standards into the root CLAUDE.md and separate them with headings for invoices, contracts, and claims.
Keep shared conventions in the root CLAUDE.md and let each package owner add @ imports for only that package's relevant standards in its package CLAUDE.md.
Place @ imports for every standards file inside a fenced code block in each package CLAUDE.md.

explanation: For a monorepo, the practical pattern is to keep repository-wide conventions in a root CLAUDE.md and place stack-specific or package-specific guidance in each package's own CLAUDE.md. A package maintainer can use @path/to/import entries to include the standards files that actually apply to that package, for example invoice extraction rules in an invoice package and contract clause conventions in a contracts package.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.This team needs issue tracker context in research reports: searching Jira epics, reading tickets, and linking cited issue IDs. It also needs a proprietary evidence-readiness workflow that maps issue labels to internal review stages and report sections. What should you recommend?

choices.text: Use a maintained Jira MCP server for standard issue operations, and build a focused custom MCP server for the proprietary workflow.
Export Jira issues into static files before each run, and have the document analysis subagent read the exported files.
Add Jira instructions to the coordinator prompt, and have the web search subagent locate issue pages through normal search.
Build one custom MCP server that reimplements Jira issue operations and includes the proprietary workflow in the same interface.

explanation: MCP is designed to reduce the N-by-M integration problem: rather than every application hand-writing tool schemas and execution logic for common services, a server can package those capabilities once and expose them through a standard protocol. For standard systems such as issue trackers, the maintainable default is to use an existing maintained MCP server when it covers the needed read or action operations.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.The document analysis subagent must extract each article's primary funding source and provide a citation for the extracted value. In several articles, the only sponsor-like clue appears in the document title metadata supplied by the application, while the document source text contains no funding statement or other passage naming a funder. The validator rejects those records because no supporting citation is present. What should this team do?

choices.text: Increase max_tokens for the extraction call and rerun the analysis to complete the missing funding citation.
Make the funding source a required schema field and force the extraction tool before the synthesis step.
Retry the document analysis subagent with the same source and require a more exhaustive search for funding text.
Return the funding source as unknown and include an evidence-gap note when no citable source passage supports it.

explanation: Retries are useful when the failure is about completion state or format, such as truncated output or schema violations. They are not a way to create missing evidence. When a research pipeline requires citations, the safer design is to let the extractor say unknown, unclear, or insufficient information when no supporting passage exists.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.In a test run, the coordinator executes the search and document analysis subagents, sends their tool_result blocks, then receives another assistant response with stop_reason: "tool_use" requesting the synthesis subagent. The current loop instead treats that response as the final answer and passes its text to the report generator, producing reports with missing synthesis. What change should you make?

choices.text: Continue the loop whenever stop_reason is "tool_use", return matching tool_result blocks, and use the response only when stop_reason is "end_turn".
Send the synthesis subagent result as a tool_result block with a new tool_use_id, then resume report generation.
Run exactly one additional coordinator turn after every tool_result message, then treat the next response as the final report input.
Inspect the coordinator's assistant text for phrases like "ready to synthesize", then decide whether to run another subagent.

explanation: In a client-executed tool loop, stop_reason is the application's control signal. stop_reason: "tool_use" means Claude has successfully stopped because it wants the application to run one or more tools, not because it has finished the task. The application should execute each requested tool, append the assistant tool-use message and the corresponding user tool_result blocks, then call the Messages API again.

stem: You are building a structured data extraction system using Claude. The system extracts information from unstructured documents, validates the output using JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) schemas, and maintains high accuracy. It must handle edge cases gracefully and integrate with downstream systems.The system described above exposes client-executed tools named extract_fields, validate_record, submit_record, and create_review_ticket. Production logs show that when a required field is ambiguous, Claude sometimes guesses a value and emits submit_record without a successful validate_record result. The application then executes the requested tool call, and downstream systems receive records that should have gone to review. What change would most effectively enforce the required workflow?

choices.text: Stop the agent loop whenever the assistant text includes phrases such as ready to submit.
Add stronger system instructions telling Claude to create review tickets for ambiguous required fields.
Add an application-level gate that blocks submit_record unless validate_record has succeeded for the same record.
Set tool_choice to tool for validate_record whenever the extraction prompt mentions ambiguous fields.

explanation: For client-executed tools, Claude does not perform the external operation itself. Claude emits a structured tool_use request, and the application decides whether and how to execute it, then returns a tool_result. That application boundary is the right place to enforce business-critical workflow ordering, such as requiring schema validation before submission.

stem: You are building a structured data extraction system using Claude. The system extracts information from unstructured documents, validates the output using JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) schemas, and maintains high accuracy. It must handle edge cases gracefully and integrate with downstream systems.The current implementation exposes one client tool named analyze_document with parameters for document text, requested operation, and desired format. In evaluation runs, Claude sometimes uses it to produce summaries when the downstream validator expected extracted fields, and sometimes attempts claim verification without passing the source excerpt needed for validation. What redesign best improves tool selection and downstream reliability without creating unnecessary tool sprawl?

choices.text: Keep analyze_document and add more operation names to its schema enum, while requiring Claude to choose the exact operation before each call.
Replace analyze_document with a few non-overlapping tools for distinct workflows, each with clear descriptions, JSON Schema inputs, and minimal stable result fields.
Create a separate tool for every document field, then merge all field-level tool results into one validated downstream record.
Move the operation instructions into the system prompt and keep the same tool schema to reduce changes to the integration.

explanation: The best redesign is to split an overly generic tool into a small number of purpose-specific tools whose purposes do not overlap, such as extraction, summarization, and source-backed verification. Each tool should have a high-quality description explaining what it does, when to use it, when not to use it, what parameters mean, and important caveats. Anthropic documents that client tools are supplied through the top-level tools parameter with name, description, and input_schema, and that descriptions are a primary driver of tool selection. See Implement tool use.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.This team uses Claude Code to maintain the research system's TypeScript repository. Citation-verification tests, report-rendering tests, and orchestration tests live beside implementation files across multiple top-level folders. The team wants the same testing guidance to apply only when Claude Code is working on test files, without duplicating guidance in every package. What should they do?

choices.text: Create .claude/rules/testing.md without frontmatter, then rely on the filename to limit it to test files.
Place the testing guidance in the root CLAUDE.md file so every Claude Code session receives the same instructions.
Add a CLAUDE.md file in each directory that contains tests, then repeat the same testing guidance in each file.
Create .claude/rules/testing.md with paths frontmatter matching the test file patterns, then place the testing guidance below it.

explanation: Claude Code separates broadly applicable project memory from topic-scoped rules. Project instructions can live in CLAUDE.md or .claude/CLAUDE.md, while reusable rules can live under .claude/rules/.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.A payments platform team is replacing its homegrown authorization layer with a policy engine across API handlers, middleware, and tests. Engineers disagree about where the policy boundary should live, and the developer assigned to it is unfamiliar with several affected packages. Which workflow should they choose before implementation?

choices.text: Run a custom slash command that instructs Claude Code to avoid asking questions during the refactor.
Use direct execution so Claude Code starts editing immediately and discovers the architecture through test failures.
Enter plan mode so Claude Code researches the codebase and proposes changes for approval before editing files.
Select the opus model alias and let Claude Code complete the refactor through direct execution.

explanation: Plan mode is designed for work where it is valuable to separate investigation from implementation. In Claude Code, plan is a documented permission mode where Claude can research the codebase, may run exploratory shell commands subject to normal permission flow, and writes a plan before source edits occur. The key operational boundary is that Claude Code does not edit source files until the plan is approved.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.This team creates a reusable source-audit skill that report-generation subagents invoke before drafting final reports. The skill should inspect local templates and citation examples, but it should not be able to edit files or run shell commands when it executes. What is the best way to configure this constraint?

choices.text: Add allowed-tools: Read Grep Glob to the skill's SKILL.md frontmatter.
Wrap the workflow in a project slash command that requests read-only behavior.
Move the workflow into CLAUDE.md with instructions to avoid edits.
Add an inspection-only warning to the skill's description in SKILL.md.

explanation: Claude Code skills are configured through a SKILL.md file that contains YAML frontmatter followed by Markdown instructions. For skill-scoped tool control, the relevant documented field is allowed-tools, which can be written as a space-separated string, comma-separated string, or YAML list, for example allowed-tools: Read Grep.

stem: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.Your CI job runs a nightly support-triage check and needs Claude Code to process a prompt, write the result to standard output, and exit without waiting for a developer. The current job launches Claude Code and intermittently hangs in the runner. What change best fits this automated workflow?

choices.text: Invoke Claude Code with claude -p "..." or claude --print "..." in the job.
Launch plain claude and add an instruction telling Claude to exit after answering.
Add --output-format json to plain claude and parse the response from stdout.
Wrap the interactive claude command in a timeout and retry the job on failure.

explanation: For automated jobs, the key distinction is between an interactive Claude Code session and print mode. The documented CLI pattern is claude -p "query" or claude –print "query", which runs the request non-interactively and then exits, making it suitable for scripts and CI/CD pipelines.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.This team has a custom documentation skill / slash-invoked command that updates README sections, API references, and migration notes after refactors. The command's overall acceptance rate is high, but review data shows that incorrect outputs are concentrated in a few fields, especially function signatures and migration warnings. What should the team do before reducing human review?

choices.text: Approve documentation changes when the command's file-level confidence exceeds a fixed threshold.
Require field-level confidence outputs and calibrate review thresholds using labeled validation examples.
Switch the command to plan mode for all documentation updates before applying changes.
Use aggregate acceptance rate as the release gate and sample merged outputs weekly.

explanation: For reliability-sensitive generated documentation, the useful unit of review is often the field, not the whole file. A README update may be mostly correct while still containing a wrong function signature or an unsafe migration note, so a single aggregate metric can create a false sense of readiness.

stem: You are building a structured data extraction system using Claude. The system extracts information from unstructured documents, validates the output using JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) schemas, and maintains high accuracy. It must handle edge cases gracefully and integrate with downstream systems.The team is adding a new document type. Claude Code must first inspect dozens of existing extractor modules, schema validators, fixture conventions, and error-handling paths. In trial runs, the main conversation fills with search and file-read output, and by implementation time it loses track of the target schema changes. Which workflow best preserves useful context while still doing discovery?

choices.text: Switch the whole task to Plan mode and let it inspect, edit, and validate files in one continuous context.
Delegate the exploratory search to the built-in Explore subagent with explicit scope and conventions, then implement from its summarized findings.
Create a shared slash command that imports all extractor, fixture, and schema files into the prompt before editing.
Run the searches in the main conversation, then use /compact immediately before implementing the schema and validator changes.

explanation: For a multi-phase Claude Code task, broad codebase discovery and implementation place different demands on the context window. The discovery phase often produces large amounts of low-level evidence, such as file listings, grep results, and repeated source reads. The implementation phase needs the conclusions from that evidence, not every intermediate observation.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.This team is creating a project-scoped /investigate command for unfamiliar codebase questions such as "why are refunds sometimes double-counted?" and "where should we add tests for the importer?" The command will use a coordinator that can delegate independent investigations to subagents before proposing a plan. Which prompt design best preserves adaptability while keeping the output reliable?

choices.text: Define the investigation goal, evidence requirements, output format, tool/source guidance, task boundaries, and effort budget heuristics.
Ask each subagent to research the requested area broadly, avoid constraints, and return any useful observations.
Specify a fixed sequence of repository scans, file reads, grep patterns, test commands, and final report sections.
Assign every request to the same frontend, backend, database, and testing subagents before synthesizing results.

explanation: For an agentic codebase investigation, the coordinator should be guided by goals and quality criteria, not a brittle recipe. Anthropic distinguishes workflows, which follow predefined code paths, from agents, which dynamically direct their own process and tool use. A prompt that fixes every scan, command, and subtask can unintentionally turn an adaptive investigation into a rigid workflow.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.During a long research run, early document analysis identifies a domain-specific taxonomy that should drive the final report. After many searches, tool results, and revisions, later synthesis passes start organizing findings around generic categories and occasionally contradict the earlier taxonomy, even though the application resends the accumulated message history. What change would best improve reliability?

choices.text: Maintain a structured research state file with the discovered taxonomy and source mappings, then load it into later synthesis prompts.
Enable prompt caching for the accumulated prefix so earlier findings can be reused without affecting the context window.
Add a synthesis instruction to avoid generic categories unless the full transcript explicitly supports them.
Increase max_tokens for later synthesis calls and continue sending the complete accumulated transcript unchanged.

explanation: Long-running research systems need to distinguish between having information somewhere in the request and making the information usable at the moment of synthesis. Anthropic describes the context window as the model's working memory and documents context rot: more context is not automatically better, and accuracy and recall can degrade as token count grows. A structured research state file, or scratchpad, keeps the discovered taxonomy, key claims, and source mappings compact and explicit so the coordinator can place them where later subagents will reliably use them.

stem: You are building a structured data extraction system using Claude. The system extracts information from unstructured documents, validates the output using JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) schemas, and maintains high accuracy. It must handle edge cases gracefully and integrate with downstream systems.After Claude generates extraction schemas and validation retry logic, subtle defects still reach downstream tests, especially around ambiguous fields and inconsistent totals. The current review prompt runs in the same long session that designed the implementation and justified its choices. What change would most effectively improve the review architecture?

choices.text: Run a separate Claude session with fresh context and provide the requirements, diff, and review checklist.
Add more few-shot extraction examples to the generator prompt and skip the separate review step.
Ask the generating Claude session to review its own code after rereading its implementation rationale.
Use /compact in the generating session, then ask it to audit the schema and retry logic.

explanation: For review quality, the key design choice is independence of context. Anthropic's documented Claude Code pattern recommends using one Claude session as the writer and a separate fresh session as the reviewer because the reviewer is not biased toward code it just wrote.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.During evals, the document-analysis subagent is invoked through the Claude Messages API using the Anthropic client SDK tool-use API, and it must return a tool call for one of three extraction schemas: extract_academic_paper, extract_news_article, or extract_market_report. The document type is not known in advance. In 6% of runs, the subagent returns a conversational summary instead of invoking a schema tool, causing the coordinator to miss citation metadata. What change best enforces structured extraction without hardcoding a specific schema?

choices.text: Set tool_choice to {"type": "any"} while providing all extraction tools.
Set tool_choice to {"type": "tool", "name": "extract_academic_paper"} for every document.
Omit tools and prefill the assistant response with the desired JSON opener.
Set tool_choice to {"type": "auto"} while providing all extraction tools.

explanation: When a workflow using the Messages API tool-use interface needs Claude to produce a tool call rather than conversational text, configure tool_choice as an object in the request. The appropriate setting here is {"type": "any"}, which tells Claude it must use one of the available tools while preserving model choice among the provided schemas.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.The document-analysis subagent has three extraction tools available: extract_metadata, extract_claims, and enrich_sources. For the first request in each document workflow, the coordinator must make the subagent call extract_metadata before any other extraction or enrichment can occur. Which configuration best fits this requirement?

choices.text: Set tool_choice to {"type": "any"} for the first document-analysis request.
Set tool_choice to {"type": "tool", "name": "extract_metadata"} for the first document-analysis request.
Omit tool_choice and rely on the default behavior when extraction tools are supplied.
Set tool_choice to {"type": "none"} until the coordinator has selected the schema.

explanation: tool_choice controls whether Claude may use tools, must use a tool, or must use a specific named tool in a Messages API request that includes tools. For a workflow step that must begin with a particular extraction tool, {"type": "tool", "name": "extract_metadata"} is the precise configuration because it selects the named tool rather than leaving the choice to the model.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.The document-analysis subagent extracts an evidence_type field using a JSON Schema enum of experiment, survey, expert_interview, and market_report. In testing, vague passages are often forced into a specific category, while new source types sometimes produce values outside the schema and fail downstream validation. What change best improves the schema design while preserving reliable categorization?

choices.text: Add unclear and other enum values, plus an other_detail field, and instruct when to use each.
Remove the enum constraint from evidence_type, and ask each subagent to write the best category label.
Keep the current enum list, and instruct the model to select the closest category for every passage.
Make evidence_type required and retry whenever validation fails until a listed category is returned.

explanation: A robust structured extraction schema should constrain predictable values while still representing edge cases honestly. JSON Schema enum is useful for categorical fields because it limits outputs to known values, but a taxonomy that lacks valid categories for ambiguous or novel inputs can push the model toward false precision.

stem: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.During a pilot using the Claude Agent SDK, a policy-research subagent sometimes reports only "search unavailable" to the coordinator. The coordinator cannot tell whether the subagent should retry, reformulate the request, narrow the scope, or treat the result as a true absence of policy, and reviewers cannot verify the evidence behind completed research. What subagent contract change would best improve reliability?

choices.text: Retry failed searches inside the subagent and return "no matching policy" after the final attempt.
Increase the search limit and ask the subagent to summarize only the final search status.
Escalate every search failure directly to a human before the coordinator synthesizes the case.
Return structured subagent results with error codes, attempted queries, and any available source metadata.

explanation: In a multi-agent support workflow, a coordinator can only recover from a subagent failure if the subagent reports actionable error context. For Anthropic's web_search server tool, a tool error can appear inside an HTTP 200 API response as a web_search_tool_result_error, and the meaningful detail is the structured error_code, not a generic phrase such as "search unavailable". The documented error codes include cases like query_too_long, max_uses_exceeded, and too_many_requests, each of which suggests a different recovery path.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.During a pilot, one engineer proposes letting subagents send intermediate findings directly to other subagents so they can coordinate faster without waiting for the coordinator to issue another delegation. Which design should this team choose?

choices.text: Add a peer-messaging tool so subagents can exchange intermediate findings and request work from each other directly.
Route follow-up work through the coordinator and require subagents to return structured final results for any additional delegation.
Create a shared scratchpad that subagents update freely and let the report generator resolve conflicts at the end.
Give every subagent the same full conversation history and let each one decide which other subagent should act next.

explanation: In a hub-and-spoke multi-agent design, the coordinator should remain the point where assignments, results, errors, and provenance are visible. Subagents can be specialized, but their outputs should flow back to the coordinator so it can decide whether to retry, launch another subagent, narrow the scope, or annotate a coverage gap.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.The report-generation subagent follows the required section headings, but its judgment varies across runs when deciding whether a research claim should be stated confidently, qualified as limited evidence, or omitted. The handoff data already includes source URLs, publication dates, and evidence excerpts, and the output format itself is not failing validation. What change would most effectively improve consistency in this judgment?

choices.text: Add 3-5 XML-wrapped examples that show relevant claim-evidence cases, edge cases, and ideal report phrasing.
Add a stronger instruction that the subagent should be conservative and only include high-confidence findings.
Enforce a JSON schema for the final report-generation step.
Add many unrelated report examples so the subagent sees a wider range of writing styles.

explanation: When a model follows the required format but varies in judgment, few-shot or multishot prompting is often the right lever. Anthropic's prompt-engineering guidance describes examples as a reliable way to steer output format, tone, and structure, and recommends making them relevant, diverse, and structured. In this case, examples should show the exact research-report boundary the team wants: a claim supported by multiple credible sources, a claim supported by only one source that needs qualification, and a claim whose evidence is too weak or conflicting to include.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.Evaluation runs show that reports on unfamiliar research topics have uneven coverage: common subdomains are detailed, while less obvious but important angles are missing. Subagents usually complete their assigned work, and the team wants to improve completeness without simply increasing the number of assignments for every topic. What orchestration change would best improve research completeness?

choices.text: Have the coordinator prewrite a larger fixed list of subtasks before any subagent begins research.
Have the synthesis agent fill coverage gaps from the available summaries without launching follow-up research.
Have the coordinator split every retrieved source into separate subagent tasks for maximum parallelism.
Have the coordinator scout initial findings first, then create focused subagent assignments from the discovered work list.

explanation: For open-ended research, an effective coordinator should treat decomposition as an adaptive investigation, not just a one-time planning step. A useful pattern is to scout inline first, discover the actual work list, then fan out focused subtasks to specialized agents once the topic boundaries are clearer.

stem: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.Production transcripts from a support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK show that after long conversations involving multiple orders, the agent sometimes applies a refund amount from one issue to a different order after older turns have been summarized. What change would most effectively preserve the critical issue details across the session?

choices.text: Summarize the complete conversation more frequently and replace prior summaries whenever the context grows large.
Maintain a structured case facts block that is updated after each relevant turn and made available on every relevant turn.
Add a system instruction telling the agent to remember all order IDs and refund amounts throughout the case.
Place the most recent order lookup result at the end of the prompt before the agent responds.

explanation: For long, multi-issue support sessions, the safest pattern is to separate critical case state from the conversational transcript. A structured facts block can track fields such as customer_id, order_id, disputed amount, refund status, customer statements, policy decisions, and unresolved issues. The orchestration layer updates this block as new evidence arrives and makes it available to the agent whenever decisions depend on those exact facts, rather than relying on older dialogue turns to remain salient.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.This team delegates documentation research to separate Claude Code subagents. In a recent upgrade guide, the final write-up treated a 2022 compatibility note and a 2025 release announcement as equally current because the parent conversation only received short summaries from each subagent. What change would most directly improve temporal reliability in future generated documentation?

choices.text: Add a CLAUDE.md instruction telling the parent agent to prefer the most recent findings when combining subagent summaries.
Require each research subagent to return schema-conformant JSON that includes source dates and a date basis for every substantive finding.
Have the parent agent ask each subagent for a prose recap whenever two summarized findings appear to conflict.
Enable citations for all research sources and rely on cited source locations to provide the needed temporal context.

explanation: Claude Code subagents are useful for keeping verbose research, logs, and file exploration out of the main context, but that isolation creates a tradeoff: the parent only sees the result the subagent returns. The Claude Code subagents documentation describes subagents as operating in their own context windows, so source metadata that matters for synthesis must be explicitly returned rather than assumed to remain available.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports.
