The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.After several runs, the final reports contain polished summaries but weak citation coverage. The web and document subagents return useful source details to the coordinator, but the synthesis subagent is invoked later with only a brief instruction to produce themes and recommendations. What change would best improve the orchestration design?

choices.text: Include the relevant findings and source metadata directly in the synthesis subagent's Agent prompt.
Allow research subagents to communicate directly so they can share source details before synthesis.
Broaden the synthesis subagent's description so automatic routing selects it after research completes.
Convert the workflow to independent agent-team sessions with a shared task list for every report.

explanation: In a coordinator to worker design, the coordinator is responsible for routing information, not just routing tasks. Subagents are useful because they have their own context windows and can keep intermediate search, log, or file output from flooding the parent conversation, but that isolation also means the coordinator must explicitly provide the context needed for downstream work.

stem: You are building a structured data extraction system using Claude. The system extracts information from unstructured documents, validates the output using JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) schemas, and maintains high accuracy. It must handle edge cases gracefully and integrate with downstream systems.Production evaluation shows accuracy drops on 60-page packets with predictable sections such as intake forms, narrative notes, invoices, and attachments. The current single-pass extraction often captures fields within individual sections but produces duplicate entities, inconsistent totals, and occasional schema-valid JSON with incorrect relationships. Which task decomposition strategy should this team use first?

choices.text: Run section-level extraction passes, then run a reconciliation pass that validates schema, deduplicates entities, and checks cross-section consistency.
Generate adaptive subtasks after each page, then stop when the agent determines that all required fields have been found.
Summarize each packet into a narrative first, then extract the required schema fields from that summary in a final pass.
Send the full packet through one expanded extraction prompt, then ask Claude to self-check the JSON before returning it.

explanation: For predictable complex workflows, a fixed sequential decomposition is usually more reliable than asking one prompt to do everything. In this case, extracting locally from each known section lets Claude focus on a smaller set of evidence, then a global reconciliation pass can compare entities, totals, dates, and relationships across sections.

stem: You are building a structured data extraction system using Claude. The system extracts information from unstructured documents, validates the output using JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) schemas, and maintains high accuracy. It must handle edge cases gracefully and integrate with downstream systems.This team has two extraction workloads: an interactive upload flow where users wait for validation before submitting documents, and a nightly archive reprocessing job whose results are reviewed the next business day. Leadership wants to reduce token costs without degrading the user-facing flow. What should the architect recommend?

choices.text: Route the nightly archive reprocessing through the Message Batches API, and keep interactive validation on synchronous Messages API calls.
Route interactive validation through the Message Batches API, and reserve synchronous calls for nightly archive reprocessing.
Keep both workloads on synchronous Messages API calls, and avoid Batch because results may take the full processing window.
Route both workloads through the Message Batches API, and rely on typical one-hour completion for interactive validation.

explanation: The Message Batches API is designed for asynchronously processing large volumes of Messages API requests, not for immediate interactive responses. Its main tradeoff is cost versus latency: Anthropic documents that batch usage is charged at 50% of standard API prices, but a batch can take up to 24 hours to complete.

stem: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.Pilot analysis shows the coordinator now sends refund eligibility, account access, and escalation-readiness questions to every specialist before answering. The results are accurate, but ambiguous billing cases often include unnecessary account-recovery details, and low-complexity requests consume too much context. What change best addresses the orchestration problem?

choices.text: Force the coordinator to invoke all specialists in parallel so no request waits on sequential handoffs.
Merge all specialist prompts into the coordinator so every issue is handled in one shared context window.
Route each request through a coordinator step that selects only the specialists whose descriptions match the current issue.
Require every specialist to return shorter summaries before the coordinator writes the final customer response.

explanation: The core design issue is not that specialists exist, it is that the coordinator is treating the specialist set as a fixed pipeline. A better pattern is dynamic delegation: the coordinator inspects the request, identifies which work is actually needed, then invokes only the relevant subagents. This keeps specialized reasoning available for difficult returns, billing disputes, and account issues without making every customer contact pay the cost of every specialist.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.A workflow script receives a response with stop_reason: "tool_use" for a client-executed run_tests tool. The script runs the tests successfully, but Claude keeps asking to run the same tool again instead of interpreting the results. What should the script change in its next request?

choices.text: Append a user text summary first, then include the matching tool result block later in that same turn.
Append a user text turn with the test output, then resume the conversation with a normal user instruction.
Append the assistant tool use turn, then add an immediate user turn with the matching tool result block.
Append an assistant text turn with the test output, then add a user turn asking Claude to continue.

explanation: In Claude's client-tool loop, Claude does not execute your local tool directly. It returns a structured tool_use request, your application runs the operation, and the next API request includes the original conversation, the assistant message containing tool_use, and an immediate user message containing the corresponding tool_result.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.During a long refactoring session, this team notices that Claude Code starts contradicting earlier architectural decisions after many file reads, test outputs, and debugging turns. The team wants the next workflow change to preserve non-negotiable decisions without relying on the full transcript staying salient. What should they do?

choices.text: Maintain a structured project facts file with key decisions, constraints, and open questions, and have Claude Code update and reference it during the session.
Keep the complete transcript in every continuation and rely on the large context window to retain decisions from earlier in the session.
Increase use of prompt caching for repeated project instructions so earlier debugging turns no longer consume the active context window.
Ask Claude Code to summarize the conversation every few turns and replace all earlier decisions with the latest prose summary.

explanation: Long development sessions are vulnerable to context degradation: file contents, test logs, tool results, and back-and-forth discussion all accumulate in the model's working memory. Anthropic documents the context window as the model's working memory for a request, not durable memory, and notes that everything included in the request counts, including system content, messages, tool results, and output budget. See Context windows.

stem: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.While updating a repository file that defines refund triage wording, Claude Code has already read the file and an Edit call fails because the supplied old_string appears in two policy examples. The requested change applies to only one occurrence, but repeated boilerplate makes a unique exact replacement impractical. What should the team instruct Claude Code to do to make the change reliably?

choices.text: Read the current file contents, assemble the full intended file, and use Write to overwrite that file.
Change old_string to a regex pattern that matches the target paragraph with optional whitespace.
Retry Edit with a shorter old_string so Claude Code can select the closest matching occurrence.
Set replace_all: true on the same Edit call so every matching policy phrase is changed consistently.

explanation: Claude Code's Edit tool is designed for targeted exact replacement. Before an edit applies, the file must have been read in the current conversation, the old_string must match exactly, and that string must appear exactly once unless replace_all: true is intentionally used.

stem: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.A customer support engineering team has an agent that collected the relevant case facts for a difficult billing dispute. The team wants to explore two different resolution strategies from that same point in the conversation. Each strategy should have its own conversation history that can be resumed later, and the original analysis thread should remain unchanged. Which approach should the team use?

choices.text: Run query() with resume=baseline_session_id and fork_session=True for each strategy, then store each new session_id.
Run query() twice with continue_conversation=True in the same directory, then store the latest session output.
Enable file checkpointing before each strategy, then rely on checkpoints to create separate conversation histories.
Run query() with resume=baseline_session_id for each strategy, then separate the outcomes using application metadata.

explanation: In the Claude Agent SDK, a session is the accumulated agent conversation history, including the prompt, tool calls, tool results, and model responses. When a team has a valuable shared baseline, such as verified customer facts and order details, resume targets that known session ID, while fork_session=True tells the Python SDK to create a new session from a copy of that history instead of continuing the original.

stem: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.A customer support engineering team is implementing a manual Messages API client-tool loop for get_customer. An integration test shows this sequence: Claude requests get_customer, the application calls the MCP server successfully, and the next Claude turn proceeds as if no customer record was available. The request trace shows the lookup output was stored in an application log, while the next Messages API request included only the original user message and a fresh assistant prefill summarizing the lookup. What change should the team make to the manual orchestration loop?

choices.text: Insert a user clarification message before returning the lookup output, then include the result afterward.
Append the assistant tool_use response, then send a user message containing the matching tool_result block.
Send the lookup output as plain text in a user message, then resume the original conversation history.
Append the lookup output as an assistant message, then ask Claude to continue from that prefilled summary.

explanation: For client tools, Claude does not execute the backend operation itself. Claude emits a structured tool_use request, your application performs the operation, and the next request must include the result as a tool_result so Claude can reason over the new information. The result belongs in a user message, not in an assistant prefill, not in an application log, and not in a separate tool role.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.The /release-note command sends a pull request diff to Claude and needs a typed object containing fields such as title, risk_level, testing_summary, and breaking_change. The prototype asks Claude to return JSON and then parses the assistant text, but failures occur when Claude includes commentary before the JSON. Which implementation change best improves reliability while preserving a schema-based extraction contract?

choices.text: Execute a local extraction function after Claude requests the tool, send a tool_result, and parse the follow-up assistant text.
Declare a client extraction tool with an input_schema for the release note fields, require that tool call, and read the tool_use input object.
Store the release note schema in CLAUDE.md, ask the slash command to follow it, and parse the final assistant text.
Keep the text JSON prompt, prefill the assistant with an opening brace, and parse the first balanced object from the assistant text.

explanation: For schema-based extraction, the stronger pattern is to model the desired output as a client tool: define a tool in the top-level tools request parameter with a clear name, description, and input_schema. When Claude calls that tool, the response has stop_reason: "tool_use" and includes one or more tool_use content blocks containing id, name, and input. The extraction payload lives in input, not in the surrounding prose.

stem: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.Before enabling overnight processing of 35,000 archived support transcripts through the Message Batches API, a pilot of 30 transcripts shows inconsistent disposition decisions and missing rationale fields in some outputs. A product manager proposes running the full archive now and resubmitting bad rows the next day. What should this team do next?

choices.text: Submit the full archive as one batch, review ended results, and resubmit rows whose disposition or fields are wrong.
Run the Prompt improver once on the current template, accept the revised prompt, and start the full overnight batch.
Create a representative evaluation set, refine the templated prompt against clear criteria, and rerun it before submitting the full batch.
Add stricter JSON output constraints, keep the current instructions, and use the batch results to discover decision errors.

explanation: For a large asynchronous workload, the practical goal is to maximize first-pass success before scale. Anthropic frames prompt engineering as an evaluation loop: define success criteria, build tests that mirror real inputs, iterate on the prompt, validate the new version, then ship. In this case, a representative set should include routine returns, billing disputes, explicit human requests, policy edge cases, and transcripts with messy customer language.

stem: You are building a structured data extraction system using Claude. The system extracts information from unstructured documents, validates the output using JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) schemas, and maintains high accuracy. It must handle edge cases gracefully and integrate with downstream systems.During validation, the system described above calls a client-side lookup tool to find matching document IDs in an internal archive. Production traces show that tool timeouts and successful searches with no matches are both returned to Claude as tool_result blocks containing an empty array, causing the agent to treat access failures as confirmed absence. What change would most reliably preserve the distinction for downstream handling?

choices.text: Return both no-match lookups and timeout failures as successful empty results to keep the extraction schema simple.
Return both no-match lookups and timeout failures as error tool results to force conservative human review.
Use the successful Messages response stop_reason to infer whether the archive lookup should be retried.
Return no-match lookups as successful empty results, and return timeout failures as error tool results with retry context.

explanation: The important reliability boundary is between valid negative evidence and missing evidence due to failure. A lookup that successfully returns no matches tells the extractor something meaningful: the queried archive did not contain a match under that query. A timeout tells the extractor something different: the system does not know whether a match exists, because access failed before the query could complete.

stem: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.Production traces show that when customers describe an order indirectly, the agent sends lookup_order vague phrases like "the jacket from last winter" or "the charge on my card," even though the backend works best with exact order IDs, verified customer IDs plus date ranges, or email receipt references. Ambiguous matches are supposed to trigger clarification or escalation, not best-guess refunds, and the backend contract cannot change this sprint. What tool-design change should this team make first?

choices.text: Force lookup_order with tool_choice for order-related turns and ask the agent to inspect matches carefully.
Route all return and billing requests to lookup_order first so backend result ranking can narrow matches.
Add more successful order lookup examples to the system prompt while keeping tool metadata minimal.
Update the tool and field descriptions with accepted input formats, example queries, edge cases, and usage boundaries.

explanation: For tool use, Claude relies heavily on the tool description and the descriptions inside input_schema to decide both when to use a tool and how to populate its arguments. A strong description should explain what the tool does, when to use it, when not to use it, accepted input formats, example values, expected outputs, and boundary cases such as ambiguous or missing identifiers.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.A documentation platform team has a custom MCP tool invoked by a shared /docs command to update architecture documentation after refactors. When the target documentation branch is protected, the tool currently returns the plain text string "operation failed," and Claude Code repeatedly retries the same update before asking the developer what happened. Which change best prevents wasted retry attempts while preserving recovery from temporary failures?

choices.text: Return MCP error results with isError set and structured content that distinguishes protected-branch failures from temporary service failures.
Add a CLAUDE.md instruction telling Claude Code to stop retrying when documentation updates fail.
Return a successful empty result when the branch is protected so Claude Code can continue the workflow.
Configure the command to retry every documentation update with exponential backoff before reporting failure.

explanation: Tool failures should carry enough structured information for the agent to decide whether to retry, change inputs, escalate, or explain the limitation. A protected documentation branch is a non-retryable condition in practice because the same tool call with the same arguments will not succeed until permissions or workflow state changes. A timeout or temporary service outage is different, since retrying later or with backoff can be productive.

stem: You are building a structured data extraction system using Claude. The system extracts information from unstructured documents, validates the output using JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) schemas, and maintains high accuracy. It must handle edge cases gracefully and integrate with downstream systems.Benchmarking shows that long packets with several independent extraction concerns are slow, and the final JSON often omits one concern when another section is unusually long. Each concern uses the same packet metadata and source text, but the extraction tasks do not depend on one another until the final schema validation step. What design change best addresses the latency and coverage issue?

choices.text: Send the full packet to one extractor, increase its output budget, then retry whenever a required field is missing.
Disable parallel tool use, process each concern in a fixed order, then append validation notes to the final JSON.
Split the concerns into parallel extraction tasks, pass shared packet context to each task, then merge and validate the unified JSON.
Let each extraction task call the next task directly, share intermediate state, then return partial JSON fragments as they finish.

explanation: When several extraction concerns are independent, the best orchestration pattern is to split, run, collect, then verify. Each worker should receive the shared packet context it needs, such as document metadata, relevant source text, and the target fields for its concern, rather than relying on hidden shared state. The coordinator then collects the results, resolves conflicts or gaps, and validates a single unified JSON object against the downstream schema.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.A payments platform's developer productivity team is adding a /find-callers command that should locate every reference to a renamed helper function, limit the search to TypeScript source files, and return enough context for a developer to jump directly to each match. Which Claude Code built-in tool configuration should the command use?

choices.text: Use Glob with pattern: "**/*helperName*.ts", sort the returned paths, and treat matching filenames as caller locations.
Use Glob with pattern: "**/*.ts", then Read each file and load all contents into the conversation for scanning.
Use Bash to run grep -R "helperName" --include="*.ts" ., then parse stdout as caller locations.
Use Grep with the helper name as pattern, scope with glob: "**/*.ts", and set output_mode: "content" for matched lines.

explanation: Grep is the Claude Code built-in tool intended for searching file contents, such as function names, error messages, and import statements. In this case, references to a renamed helper function are content inside source files, so the search should be expressed as a Grep pattern rather than a filename lookup.

stem: You are building a structured data extraction system using Claude. The system extracts information from unstructured documents, validates the output using JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) schemas, and maintains high accuracy. It must handle edge cases gracefully and integrate with downstream systems.A compliance automation team's structured extraction system includes a specialized audit_evidence_extractor tool for extracting audit findings from formal audit reports. Production logs show the tool being called for ordinary invoices and contracts whenever the documents contain phrases such as "validation required" or "compliance check," even when no audit evidence is present. The tool description says it is for formal audit reports, while one system instruction says: "CRITICAL: You MUST use audit_evidence_extractor whenever compliance, validation, control, or audit language appears." What change would most directly reduce this unintended tool association while preserving legitimate audit extraction?

choices.text: Rename audit_evidence_extractor to report_parser without changing descriptions or prompt wording.
Set tool_choice to any so Claude must call one extraction tool for every document.
Rewrite the system prompt and tool description with narrower use boundaries and ordinary wording for audit reports.
Set tool_choice to the audit_evidence_extractor tool whenever compliance language appears.

explanation: When tools are available, Claude normally uses tool_choice: {"type": "auto"}, so it decides whether to call a tool based on how the user request maps to the tool's described capability and the surrounding prompt context. Anthropic documents that system prompts can steer tool use, but they are not a hard guarantee, and forceful wording can lead to overtriggering.

stem: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.The team needs to add a larger feature that caches refund eligibility decisions before invoking backend tools. The engineers are unfamiliar with the policy edge cases, cache invalidation risks, and failure modes around stale eligibility data. What should they do before asking Claude Code to implement the change?

choices.text: Ask Claude Code to implement a conservative cache with short expiration, then inspect the diff for any missing policy or escalation behavior.
Ask Claude Code to draft a detailed implementation plan from the current codebase and proceed once the plan appears technically consistent.
Ask Claude Code to use AskUserQuestion to gather requirements about implementation constraints, edge cases, and failure modes before planning code changes.
Ask Claude Code to create tests for common refund cache scenarios, then use failing tests to drive the implementation iteratively.

explanation: For larger features in unfamiliar domains, the useful first move is often to have Claude ask questions before designing. The documented pattern is to let Claude interview you, using AskUserQuestion, so it can surface requirements around technical implementation, edge cases, constraints, and failure modes before it commits to a plan.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.This team's /review command classifies pull request comments into defects, missing tests, dependency risks, and dead-code findings. In the last month, defect and missing-test comments are usually accepted, but dead-code findings are frequently dismissed because Claude flags framework entry points and reflection-based handlers that are intentionally unused by direct imports. Several developers now skim or mute the entire review output. What change should you make first?

choices.text: Increase the severity of defect and missing-test comments so developers notice the useful findings.
Measure precision and recall by finding category, then narrow or pause the noisy dead-code checks.
Add a CLAUDE.md note asking Claude to be more conservative when reporting dead code.
Combine all review categories into one quality score and tune the prompt only if that score drops.

explanation: The issue is not that Claude Code can never identify dead code, it is that one false-positive-heavy category can undermine confidence in the entire review surface. For developer-facing automation, trust is often categorical: if engineers repeatedly see bogus dead-code comments, they may stop reading useful defect and missing-test findings too.

stem: You are building a structured data extraction system using Claude. The system extracts information from unstructured documents, validates the output using JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) schemas, and maintains high accuracy. It must handle edge cases gracefully and integrate with downstream systems.This team asks Claude to review a 42-file extraction pipeline in a single pass, including parsers, normalization rules, JSON schemas, validators, and downstream mapping code. Recent reviews are inconsistent: some obvious defects are found, while other issues are missed depending on which part of the pipeline dominates the review. What review design should the team adopt?

choices.text: Run one larger review prompt that includes every file, all requirements, and a stricter instruction to identify every possible defect.
Run focused per-file review passes first, then run a separate integration pass over the summarized local findings and cross-file data flow.
Run only a cross-file integration review that traces extracted fields from parsing through validation and downstream export.
Run several independent full-pipeline reviews in parallel, then merge all findings that appear in at least two review outputs.

explanation: For large multi-file reviews, a reliable pattern is to split the task into focused local passes and a separate integration pass. Local passes ask Claude to inspect one file or a small group of related files for issues that can be judged in that scope, such as schema constraints, nullable fields, validation behavior, and normalization rules.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.After a web exploration phase in a Claude Code research workflow, later subagents repeatedly rerun searches that earlier subagents already completed and fail to preserve why certain sources were rejected. The coordinator receives brief outputs from the earlier subagents, but next-phase work still starts as if no exploration happened. What should the coordinator change before spawning each next-phase subagent?

choices.text: Spawn the next subagents normally and rely on their isolated context windows to access the parent history.
Save the prior findings for the final synthesis prompt and keep next subagent delegations independent.
Condense prior exploration into a source-linked summary and include it in each next subagent's delegation prompt.
Attach complete prior subagent transcripts to every next delegation so no detail is omitted.

explanation: Subagents are useful for multi-agent research because they can keep verbose search logs, file contents, and exploratory work out of the main conversation, then return a compact summary. The tradeoff is that a normal subagent starts with a fresh, isolated context window, so it will not automatically know what earlier subagents found, rejected, or left unresolved.

stem: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.An online retailer's support engineering team wants to add a reusable /refund-audit workflow in Claude Code for reviewing changes to refund logic. It must be version-controlled with the repository, include a checklist plus example transcripts as supporting files, and prevent file modification tools or shell commands while the workflow is active. Which implementation best fits these requirements?

choices.text: Create .claude/skills/refund-audit/SKILL.md with supporting files referenced from it, and set disallowed-tools for Write, Edit, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit, and Bash.
Create .claude/skills/refund-audit/SKILL.md with supporting files referenced from it, and set allowed-tools to Read and Grep.
Create .claude/commands/refund-audit.md with links to supporting files, and set allowed-tools to Read and Grep.
Create ~/.claude/skills/refund-audit/SKILL.md with supporting files referenced from it, and set disable-model-invocation: true.

explanation: For a team-shared Claude Code workflow, use a project skill under .claude/skills//SKILL.md. The directory name normally determines the slash command, so .claude/skills/refund-audit/SKILL.md creates /refund-audit, and the skill directory can hold related checklists, examples, templates, or scripts that are referenced from SKILL.md.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.A senior engineer is about to migrate a shared authorization layer used by several packages. The dependency graph is unclear, there are multiple viable designs, and prior immediate-edit attempts caused broad rewrites that were later reverted. What should the engineer do first?

choices.text: Switch to bypassPermissions mode, let Claude inspect and edit freely, then rely on tests to catch bad changes.
Use direct execution, ask Claude to update one package at a time, then revert commits if the design shifts.
Start Claude Code in plan mode, have it inspect the affected areas, review the proposed plan, then approve an editing mode.
Start Claude Code in acceptEdits mode, have it inspect the affected areas, then review the resulting source changes.

explanation: Plan mode is designed for situations where changing code immediately would be risky because the design, dependencies, or scope are not yet clear. In this mode, Claude Code can analyze the codebase and write a proposed plan, but it does not edit source files until the plan is approved.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.After a long codebase analysis, this team wants to compare two alternative test-generation strategies from the same discovered baseline. Each investigation should preserve the baseline context, avoid contaminating the other strategy's reasoning history, and leave the original analysis session available for later use. What should the team do?

choices.text: Continue the most recent session in the directory twice and assign each strategy a different prompt label.
Duplicate the project folder twice and rely on each copied folder to contain an independent session history.
Resume the baseline session ID with fork_session enabled for each strategy and run each investigation in a new session.
Resume the baseline session normally and ask Claude to keep each strategy in a separate section of its answer.

explanation: Use session forking when you want multiple investigations to start from the same accumulated context and then diverge. In the Claude Agent SDK, a session contains the conversation history, including prompts, tool calls, tool results, and responses. The documentation distinguishes continue, resume, and fork: continue finds the most recent session in the current directory, resume targets a specific session ID, and fork creates a new session that begins with a copy of the original session history while leaving the original unchanged.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.When Claude Code runs npm test through Bash, the raw stdout often includes long dependency warnings and absolute local paths. The team wants Claude to reason from a shorter, normalized version of successful Bash results while leaving the command execution itself unchanged. What implementation should they choose?

choices.text: Configure a PostToolUse hook matching Bash that exits with code 2 and writes normalized stdout to stderr.
Configure a PostToolUse hook matching Bash that returns updatedToolOutput with the Bash result shape.
Configure a PostToolUse hook matching Bash that returns decision: "block" with a normalization reason.
Configure a PreToolUse hook matching Bash that rewrites stdout inside the incoming tool input.

explanation: PostToolUse is the appropriate hook event when Claude Code should transform a successful tool result after execution but before Claude reasons over that result. The hook receives the original tool arguments and the tool response, then can return updatedToolOutput to replace what Claude sees on the next model request.

stem: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.During an audit rollout, this team adds a required resolution record containing customer_id, order_id, action_taken, escalation_reason, and policy_basis. The current implementation asks Claude to respond with only valid JSON, but production logs still show occasional trailing prose and missing required keys, which break parsing before the case can be stored. What change would most reliably produce a schema-compliant record that application code can consume?

choices.text: Add stronger JSON-only instructions, wrap the schema in XML tags, and reject any response with prose.
Register a resolution-record tool but leave tool_choice on auto for normal flexibility.
Define a strict client tool for the resolution record with an input_schema and force that tool with tool_choice.
Prefill the assistant response with an opening brace and use a delimiter stop sequence.

explanation: For production structured data that must be parsed reliably, prompt-only JSON is the wrong reliability layer. Anthropic documents that without structured outputs, Claude can produce malformed JSON, missing fields, inconsistent types, or schema violations, which is exactly the failure mode shown here in JSON.parse() failures.

stem: You are building a structured data extraction system using Claude. The system extracts information from unstructured documents, validates the output using JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) schemas, and maintains high accuracy. It must handle edge cases gracefully and integrate with downstream systems.During evaluation, this team asks Claude Code to use subagents to investigate extraction errors across 600 vendor invoices, intake forms, and contracts. The current approach gives each subagent the same instruction, "find causes of schema validation failures across all documents," producing repeated observations and a large synthesis context. What change best partitions the investigation while preserving synthesis quality?

choices.text: Assign each subagent a distinct document group or extraction concern, provide needed context, and require concise findings for synthesis.
Create one nested subagent chain per document type, require verbose summaries at each level, and synthesize the final outputs.
Assign overlapping document subsets to multiple subagents, ask each to find any schema issue, and reconcile duplicates afterward.
Ask every subagent to review the full corpus independently, compare their repeated findings, and merge common schema issues.

explanation: Claude Code subagents are useful when the main agent needs focused side investigations without filling the main conversation with raw search, log, or file output. The documented parallel research pattern is to spawn multiple subagents for independent investigations, then have the main conversation synthesize their results. In a structured extraction system, that usually means dividing work by document family, source type, schema section, failure mode, or another boundary that makes each research path non-overlapping.

stem: You are building a structured data extraction system using Claude. The system extracts information from unstructured documents, validates the output using JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) schemas, and maintains high accuracy. It must handle edge cases gracefully and integrate with downstream systems.The system described above now reports 99% schema-valid outputs, and most invoices, intake forms, and contracts receive high field-level confidence scores. Reviewers can inspect only a small portion of high-confidence records each week, but the team still needs to estimate production error rates and detect rare new failure patterns before further reducing review. What should the team do?

choices.text: Use the Claude Console Evaluation Tool as the sole monitor, then stop manual spot checks for high-confidence records.
Draw one random sample across all high-confidence records, then report only the aggregate weekly accuracy rate.
Sample high-confidence records within each document type and critical field, then track reviewed error patterns by segment.
Review only low-confidence records and ambiguous documents, then assume high-confidence records remain accurate after validation.

explanation: For structured extraction systems, high aggregate accuracy can be misleading because errors often concentrate in particular document types, fields, source formats, or edge cases. A strong monitoring design samples high-confidence outputs across meaningful strata, such as document category and critical field, so the team can estimate error rates where they matter rather than relying on one blended number.

stem: You are building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. It has access to your backend systems through custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human). Your target is 80%+ first-contact resolution while knowing when to escalate.In production tests, the agent's first-pass case analysis lists every plausible billing or return issue, including marginal ones. Reviewers complain that all findings arrive with the same priority, so they cannot decide which should be auto-resolved, queued for human review, or used only for trend analysis. What change best supports calibrated review routing while preserving broad coverage?

choices.text: Ask the agent to describe uncertainty in prose so reviewers can triage each case.
Run a separate verification pass that returns schema-constrained findings with confidence, severity, evidence, and routing fields.
Route cases by reading a confidence value from each Messages API response object.
Instruct the initial finding pass to return only high-confidence issues with customer-impact severity labels.

explanation: For review routing, the useful pattern is a two-stage finding and verification flow. The first stage should maximize coverage by reporting plausible issues, while the later verification or ranking stage assigns fields such as confidence and severity so the system can prioritize human attention without losing low-confidence signals.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.A healthcare analytics team's extraction job uses Claude with a strict extraction tool to convert discharge summaries into medication reconciliation records. The tool input schema is valid, but an application validator rejects some records because medication entries cite the wrong note section or omit the required source quote. The current retry prompt says only "fix the invalid JSON," and the same citation defects often reappear. What should the extraction loop do before accepting the records?

choices.text: Retry the same request with a higher temperature, then accept the first response that differs from the rejected output.
Return the validator's field paths and citation failures with the original note, then retry and route unresolved cases to review.
Replace the validator with broader prompt instructions, then ask Claude to be more careful with citations on every run.
Accept records once the strict tool input matches the schema, then rely on reviewers to find citation mistakes later.

explanation: Validation-retry loops are most useful when they turn a vague failure into precise correction context. Instead of saying only that the output is invalid, the application should send Claude the original source plus specific validator failures, such as the field path, the missing source quote, or the cited section that does not support the extracted medication.

stem: You are building a multi-agent research system using the Claude Agent SDK. A coordinator agent delegates to specialized subagents: one searches the web, one analyzes documents, one synthesizes findings, and one generates reports. The system researches topics and produces comprehensive, cited reports.After a refactor, generated reports now show two linked defects: citations render twice in the final report, and some evidence excerpts disappear when the synthesis subagent output is passed to the report generator. The likely cause spans the claim-source schema, the synthesis prompt, and the report template, and the acceptance test should confirm that each claim appears once with its evidence excerpt and source URL. How should this team use Claude Code to address the defects most effectively?

choices.text: Enter plan mode, give one detailed request covering both defects, affected areas, constraints, and verification checks before approving edits.
Add a Stop hook that runs the acceptance test and rely on repeated blocks as the main debugging strategy.
Skip planning and ask Claude to fix the report bugs broadly, then inspect the diff after it finishes.
Open separate cleared sessions for each defect, ask each session to edit only its assigned file, then merge results.

explanation: Claude Code is most effective when the workflow matches the dependency structure of the work. For interacting fixes, splitting the defects too early can create inconsistent edits because each session may make different assumptions about the shared interface between synthesis and report generation.

stem: You are using Claude Code to accelerate software development. Your team uses it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and documentation. You need to integrate it into your development workflow with custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, and understand when to use plan mode vs direct execution.A teammate wants Claude Code to add one guard clause to a single known function so it rejects negative quantities, then run the existing unit test for that file. The relevant file path and expected behavior are already known, and no API, schema, or architectural changes are involved. What should the developer do?

choices.text: Start with bypassPermissions so Claude can edit and test without permission prompts.
Enter plan mode first, review a plan, then approve implementation after exploration.
Ask Claude Code to make the small change directly and run the specified test.
Switch to acceptEdits mode first, let Claude edit, then inspect the diff afterward.

explanation: For a small, well-scoped change, Claude Code is most effective when you ask for the outcome directly and include a verification step. Anthropic's best-practices guidance says plan mode adds overhead, and that if the diff can be described in one sentence, you should skip the plan and ask Claude to do it directly.

stem: You are building a structured data extraction system using Claude. The system extracts information from unstructured documents, validates the output using JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) schemas, and maintains high accuracy. It must handle edge cases gracefully and integrate with downstream systems.During extraction prompt development, identical Claude Code requests behave differently depending on where developers start the session. The invoice package has a package-specific CLAUDE.md that says missing invoice identifiers must be represented as null, but some sessions do not follow it. What should the team do first to diagnose whether Claude Code is receiving the intended instructions in the current session?

choices.text: Disable auto memory and rerun the same prompt to confirm that repository instructions are the only influence.
Rerun /init from the repository root and regenerate the project CLAUDE.md before comparing any session behavior.
Move the invoice extraction rule into ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md so every developer inherits the same instruction globally.
Run /memory in each affected session and compare the listed CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, user-level, and managed policy memory files.

explanation: /memory is the right first diagnostic tool when Claude Code behaves differently across sessions. It shows the memory files loaded into the current session, such as relevant CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, user-level, and managed policy memory, so the team can compare a working session with a failing one.
